items.q: The fire bombing of Black homes in a neighborhood in this state led it to be nicknamed "Dynamite Hill." Robin D.G. Kelley profiled Angela Davis's parents in his history of this State's Communist Party, Hammer and Hoe. A letter written in this state laments the hesitancy of white (*) moderates who are "the great... stumbling block in the stride toward freedom." John Coltrane's song titled for this state was inspired by the death of four Black girls killed in a bombing of a Baptist Church in this state. A bus boycott started in this state when Rosa Parks refused to give up her seat. For 10 points, name this state where Martin Luther King Jr. wrote his "Letter from a Birmingham Jail."
items.a: Alabama

items.q: This U.S. state, the first to recognize Christmas as a legal holiday, is home to a city named after the inventor of a steel-making process, Henry Bessemer. Famous musical acts such as The Rolling Stones have recorded in this state's Muscle Shoals Sound Studio. The Saturn V (*) rocket that sent astronauts to the moon was developed at the Marshall Space Flight Center in this state. For ten points, name this state whose capital is Montgomery.
items.a: Alabama

items.q: This state's original capital of Cahaba became a ghost town by 1900, and the last remaining year-round water delivery route by the US Postal Service serves residents of this state's Magnolia and Fish rivers. The eastern half of the Black Belt Prairie lies in this state, whose official state bird is the Yellowhammer. This state's Jefferson County is home to the "Pittsburgh of the South", while (*) Muscle Shoals lies on the south bank of the Tennessee River in this state. The first capital of the Confederate States of America was in this state's capital of Montgomery. For 10 points, name this US state which is home to Birmingham.
items.a: Alabama

items.q: This state is home to the first officially recorded cave in the United States, DeSoto Caverns, which was originally a burial ground for the Copena civilization. This state's town of Enterprise has a monument to the Boll Weevil which ironically saved the economy of this state. While not Louisiana, the oldest (*) Mardi Gras celebration in the US happens in one of this state's port cities. Bob Dylan wrote of events in this state, instructing one governor to "Not Stand in the Doorway." A racist governor of this state was elected twice as a staunch segregationist, but he became a born-again Christian and renounced segregationist views before his fourth and final term. That man was George Wallace. For 10 points, name this southern state with capital at Montgomery and most populous city at Huntsville.
items.a: Alabama

items.q: Peoples in what is now this US state added Christian practices to the concept of himdag, which supposedly emerged when the Wooshkam tore down Siwani's cities. The mistranslation "all used up" has been applied to a culture in this state that built a ruin indigenously called Siwan Wa'a Ki, which sits under a shelter designed by Frederick Law Olmsted and was first described by Eusebio Kino. The settlement of Snaketown and vast networks of canals were built in this state by an urban culture named after "those who came before," the Hohokam. Lifestyles centered on what are called Hia-C'ed ("HEE-ah ched"), Tohono, or Akimel name the O'odham ("OH-od-um") peoples of this US state, who revolted against Spanish incursion when it made up the north of the Pimeria Alta or "Land of the Upper Pima." For 10 points, what state's settlers built Fort Defiance and Fort Yuma?
items.a: Arizona [or AZ] (The name Hohokam derives from the O'odham concept of huhugam, which refers to ancestors rather than vanished cultures. The Hia-C'ed, Tohono, and Akimel O'odham are respectively named for dunes, desert, and the river. Eusebio Kino described the Casa Grande.)

items.q: In this state, the series "Fridays with Frank" follows a deputy in Pinal County. Paul Penzone defeated "America's Toughest Sheriff," Joe Arpaio, in this state's most populous county. This state's city of Window Rock is the capital of a reservation that completely surrounds the (*) Hopi Reservation. Robert McCulloch funded the reconstruction of London Bridge in this state's Lake Havasu City. Maricopa County is home to this state's capital, whose metro area is called the "Valley of the Sun." A horseshoe-shaped "Skywalk" allows people to look through a glass floor into a natural feature in this state created by the Colorado River. For 10 points, name this state home to the Grand Canyon.
items.a: Arizona [or AZ]

items.q: In 1946, a magazine titled for this state became the first consumer publication to issue an all-color special issue under legendary editor Raymond Carlson. This state's Daily Citizen newspaper featured photographer Esther Henderson, whose photo of its Mather Point appeared in the Saturday Evening Post. A magazine titled for this state's highways was the first to print a photo taken from its (*) Havasu Canyon by Ansel Adams, and the Ansel Adams Center for Creative Photography is located near Speedway Boulevard at one of its state universities. Adams took photographs such as White House Ruin in Canyon de Chelly National Monument in this state. For 10 points, name this state whose namesake Highways magazine published photos of Native Americans by a not-yet-famous local politician named Barry Goldwater.
items.a: Arizona [accept Arizona Highways] ~30920~

items.q: Richard Hofsteder was inspired by a politician from this state to write "The Paranoid Style in American Politics." L. Brent Bozell ghostwrote The Conscience of a Conservative for a politician from this state. That politician from this state was endorsed in the speech "A Time For Choosing" and was targeted by the (*) "Daisy" ad. A senator from this state was shot down and tortured in Vietnam before becoming the 2008 Republican nominee for President. For 10 points, name this state whose senators included Barry Goldwater and John McCain.
items.a: Arizona

items.q: A future governor of this state was asked to leave the Red Hen restaurant in Lexington, Virginia in 2018. This state's governor was criticized for buying a lectern that cost over $19,000. A former governor from this state finished last in the Republican Iowa caucuses in 2024. This state is the home of Donald Trump skeptic (*) Asa Hutchinson. For 10 points, name this state, currently governed by Sarah Huckabee Sanders, which is the home of Bill Clinton and the headquarters of Wal-Mart.
items.a: Arkansas

items.q: After one crisis, this state was ruled against in Cooper v. Aaron, leading to the "Lost Year." The first Republican governor of this state in 100 years was Winthrop Rockefeller. NAACP ["N double-A C P"] field Secretary Walter White investigated the Elaine Race Riot in this state. During a crisis in this state, mayor Woodrow Wilson Mann asked for federal assistance, leading to the deployment of the (*) 101st Airborne. During that crisis in this state's capital, Governor Orval Faubus sent in the national guard to prevent the desegregation of Central High School. For 10 points, name this state whose public schools were integrated by the Little Rock Nine.
items.a: Arkansas

items.q: Women from this state's capital gave an engraved sword to James Totten for peacefully evacuating an arsenal during a crisis that nearly began the Civil War. A disagreement over railroad bonds issued by this state culminated in a "war" between two Republican faction leaders that engulfed Senators Stephen W. Dorsey and Powell Clayton. Frederick Steele recaptured much of this state, from which he launched the 1864 Camden Expedition. Politics in this state were dominated by "the Family" before the Civil War and by factions called "Brindletails" and "Minstrels" afterwards. The resolution of the Brooks-Baxter War in this state coincided with the end of Reconstruction. Confederate forces abandoned this state following Earl Van Dorn's retreat after the Battle of Pea Ridge. For 10 points, name this state that formed the fourth military district during Reconstruction with its southeastern neighbor, Mississippi.
items.a: Arkansas [or AR]

items.q: This state is home to the eastern end of the Ouachita Mountains and the southern end of the Ozark Mountains. Tourists in this state can dig up gemstones at Crater of (*) Diamonds State Park and visit the oldest National Park in Hot Springs. This state's town of Bentonville boomed with the founding and growth of Wal-Mart. For 10 points, name this southern state that is sandwiched between Missouri and Louisiana, and whose capital is Little Rock.
items.a: Arkansas

items.q: During a strike in this state, its national guard built the temporary Camp McIntire from parts of the Ice Palace, created for the "Crystal Carnival." This state was the site of the "Mount Pisgah" gold hoax, near where "Crazy Bob" Womack actually found gold in 1890. William Greeneberry Russell began a gold rush in this state that was commented on by Horace Greeley, who attempted to found this state's "Union Colony." Louis Tikas was killed in this state, where John Calderwood led a miners' strike in Cripple Creek. During a conflict in this state, the "Death Special," an armored car with a mounted machine gun, was used by the Baldwin-Felts Detective Agency. A "Coalfield War" in this state saw John D. Rockefeller Jr.'s implication in the Ludlow Massacre. For 10 points, what state was the site of the Pike's Peak gold rush?
items.a: Colorado [or CO; accept the Colorado Coalfield War; accept the Union Colony of Colorado] (The first line refers to the Leadville miners' strike.)

items.q: In September 2022, this state became the first to allow residents to pay state taxes in Bitcoin. This state's The Edge at Lowry was the subject of disputed claims of either absentee landlord or Tren de Aragua takeover after video emerged of armed men entering an apartment. Kevin Grantham placed a portrait of Vladimir Putin in this state's Capitol to raise money to commission an allegedly unflattering (*) portrait of Donald Trump. In 2025, this state's Run for their Lives protest to support hostages in Gaza was attacked with a Molotov cocktail by an Egyptian immigrant. Jared Polis is the governor of, for 10 points, what state governed from Denver?
items.a: Colorado

items.q: This state's town of Dinosaur is located near its Yampa River State Park in Moffat County. The vast majority of the Front Range urban corridor is located in this state and connected by the "Valley Highway" section of Interstate 25. Parts of this state's "Black Canyon" only receive 33 minutes of sunlight a day. The Gunnison River merges with a river named for this state near the city of (*) Grand Junction. This state's "Grand Mesa" should not be confused with dwellings found in its site of Mesa Verde. This state's ski industry is driven by the cities of Aspen and Vail. Pike's Peak is located in, for 10 points, what state with capital at Denver?
items.a: Colorado [accept CO]

items.q: Ken Buck, a Republican congressperson from this state, announced his early resignation from Congress in March. In 2023, a congressperson from this state was removed from a performance of Beetlejuice for allegedly vaping, singing, and groping their partner. This state's current governor, (*) Jared Polis, was the first openly gay man to be elected governor. Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper are this state's senators, while Lauren Boebert represents this state in the House. For 10 points, name this state governed from Denver.
items.a: Colorado

items.q: An Indian fort in this present-day state was attacked by John Mason's forces. The colony that later became this state was founded by Thomas Hooker, who authored its "Fundamental Orders." This future state's royal charter was hidden from Edmund Andros in an oak tree. A delegate from this state, Roger Sherman, solved the debate between the (*) Virginia and New Jersey Plans by introducing this state's namesake compromise. The Saybrook and New Haven colonies merged to form the colony that became this state. For 10 points, name this "Nutmeg State" home to Yale University and governed from Hartford.
items.a: Connecticut [or CT]

items.q: A lawyer from this state, named Amasa Learned, replaced the author of A Caveat Against Injustice as a U.S. Representative. Settlers of a colony in this present-day state saw a vision of a ghost ship, which some believed was the missing trade ship built by its first governor, Theophilus Eaton. John Haynes helped draft a document in a colony in this state mostly written by Roger Ludlow, which was supplanted by a 1662 royal charter. (*) Windsor and Wethersfield were named in an early constitution from a colony in this state, a set of "Fundamental Orders" drafted by Thomas Hooker. States were given equal power in the Senate by a Great Compromise named for this state. Roger Sherman represented, for 10 points, what state, the home of the New Haven Colony?
items.a: Connecticut [or CT; accept Connecticut Compromise or Fundamental Orders of Connecticut; prompt on New Haven Colony until read]

items.q: Robert Dale Segee confessed to starting a fire in this state that spread quickly due to paraffin wax used to waterproof a temporary structure. Famous photos from that disaster in this state include that of a girl known only as "Little Miss 1565" and a frowning Emmett Kelly carrying a bucket on "The Day the Clowns Cried." A museum in this state, closed since a December 2024 boiler explosion, has a replica of its namesake's Iranistan Estate and a slice of fruit cake from the wedding of (*) Lavinia Warren. That museum in this state also contains a mummy that was verified to be 2,500 years old by researchers at a university in this state, Quinnipiac. A city in this state installed gas lighting in the 1870s under mayor P. T. Barnum. For 10 points, name this state home to Bridgeport where a deadly circus fire took place in Hartford.
items.a: Connecticut [or CT]

items.q: A poem imagines seeing a city in this U.S. state through "The eye made clear of uncertainty, with the sight / Of simple seeing, without reflection." The image of the ocean "shaking the water off / like a poodle" appears in a poem titled for this state's capital "in a purple light." A poem set in this state begins with the lines, "The eye's plain version is a thing apart, / The vulgate of experience." In another poem, a man traveling in this state is pierced by fear when mistaking "the shadow of his equipage" while riding in a glass coach. Wallace Stevens wrote a poem titled for "An Ordinary Evening in" a city in this state. An academic who taught at a university in this state for 64 years included four collections by Stevens in The Western Canon. For 10 points, name this state where Stevens was championed for decades by Harold Bloom.
items.a: Connecticut

items.q: Dick Cavett told a governor of this state, "If I called any of your admirers bigots, who are not bigots, I apologize." Before being elected governor, the owner of Pickrick Cafeteria in this state held pickaxes to prevent entry for Black patrons. After running a conservative campaign, a politician from this state shocked segregationists by declaring, "The time for racial discrimination is over." That politician defeated the incumbent (*) Lester Maddox to become governor of this state. The Supreme Court ruled that the Commerce Clause prohibited racial discrimination in a motel in this state under the Civil Rights Act. After refusing to join a local White Citizens' council, a future president from this state faced boycotts against his family's peanut business. For 10 points, name this state home to Jimmy Carter.
items.a: Georgia [or GA]

items.q: The Adelphean Society was established at this state's Wesleyan Female College as the nation's first sorority. Though serving for just one day, a politician from this state was the first woman, and the last slave owner, to serve in the Senate. At age 87, this state's Senator Rebecca Latimer Felton took office, replacing the Populist Thomas Watson. In this state, Harriet Powers's quilts were displayed at an event in which a speaker stated, "we can be as separate as the fingers, yet one as the hand." Elise Mercur designed a Women's Building for this state's 1895 Cotton States and International Exposition, where Booker T. Washington gave a "Compromise" speech. For 10 points, name this state where Spelman College was established as a women's college in Atlanta.
items.a: Georgia

items.q: A senior pastor in this state named Jamal Bryant has advocated adding worshippers by growing marijuana inside its New Birth Missionary Church. A theologian active in this state founded the Women in Ministry Conference in 2005 and is the head of the Ray of Hope Ministry, Cynthia Hale. In February 2023, a pastor from this state argued Joshua was not to "fill Moses' Shoes" in the "Courage to Be" sermon; that pastor wrote the 2022 memoir A Way Out of No Way. Otis Moss was co-pastor at a church in this state whose senior pastor broadcast sermons on its (*) WERD radio station alongside his two sons, one of whom was Alfred Daniel. That church's most notable pastor organized a sit-in at Rich's department store and garnered support from students at Morehouse College. For 10 points, name this state where Raphael Warnock and Martin Luther King were pastors at Ebenezer Baptist Church.
items.a: Georgia

items.q: This colony's oldest city was designed upon Enlightenment ideals in a "plan" named for its first governor. After landing in this colony, Mary Musgrove translated the welcoming words of Chief Tomochichi. During the War of Jenkins' Ear, Manuel de Montiano was defeated by the Yamacraw at this state's Battle of Bloody (*) Marsh. After this state became a Royal Colony in 1752, South Carolina planters began producing Indigo on its Cumberland Island. The British parliament prevented the founder of this state from turning it into a debtors colony. For 10 points, name this state where James Oglethorpe founded the city of Savannah.
items.a: Georgia

items.q: In a short story set in this state, the elderly Mr. Baptiste is killed by a thrown brick after cheering Black workers on strike. The author of the WWI protest poem "I Sit and Sew," Alice Dunbar-Nelson, was born in this state. This state is the setting of a novel in which Lana Lee runs the sleazy Night of Joy bar, in which a brawl breaks out when a (*) parrot bites a man's pirate earring. Armand is revealed to be part-Black in a short story set in this state, "Desiree's Baby," written by an author who created the pianist Mademoiselle Reisz. Edna Pontellier drowns herself in a novel set in this state, the home of Ignatius Reilly. For 10 points, what US state is the setting of A Confederacy of Dunces and The Awakening, written by Creole author Kate Chopin?
items.a: Louisiana [or LA] (The story in the first line is Alice Dunbar-Nelson's "Mr. Baptiste.")

items.q: A governor of this state took an eight-day trip to Europe, spawning the bumper sticker "I did Paris with the gov." Former 49ers owner Edward DeBartolo Jr. confessed to bribing a politician from this state, who was indicted in 1998 for fraud. John Maginnis's book The Last Hayride details an election in this state lost by David Treen. A governor of this state joked that he would only lose an election if he was caught in bed with a "dead girl or a live boy." Bumper stickers in this state quoted "Vote for the Lizard" after George H.W. Bush withdrew support for a Republican. A Democrat governor of this state claimed the only thing he had in common with his opponent was being a "wizard in the sheets." For 10 points, a 1991 gubernatorial election in what state resulted in Edwin Edwards's defeat of KKK leader David Duke?
items.a: Louisiana [or LA]

items.q: A governor of this state funded a capitol building featuring a 450-foot tall art deco tower. A governor of this state who had an affair with stripper Blaze Starr was known as Uncle Earl. A plan to eliminate dust storms was detailed by a book written in this state that proposed appointing Franklin Roosevelt as Secretary of the Navy. That book written in this state advocated for a wealth cap and is titled (*) My First Days in the White House. This state's Depression-era governor used the slogan "Every Man a King" to promote his "Share Our Wealth" program before his 1935 assassination. For 10 points, Huey Long governed what state from Baton Rouge?
items.a: Louisiana [or LA]

items.q: In this state, supporters of Governor William Pitt Kellogg were killed by men later prosecuted under theEnforcement Act. The Supreme Court ruled that the Fourteenth Amendment did not limit private actorsafter this state's Colfax massacre led to the caseUnited States v. Cruikshank. The Court limited theFourteenth Amendment in a case concerning butchers in this state, the (*) Slaughter-House Cases. A Citizens'Committee recruited a creole man from this state to board a whites-only train car, leading to a "separate but equal"ruling from the Supreme Court. For 10 points, name this state where Homer Plessy was arrested in New Orleans.
items.a: Louisiana

items.q: This state's namesake "Won't Wait" plan targets carbon neutrality by 2045. The governor of this state replied "see you in court" to Donald Trump in defiance of the federal ban on trans athletes. Brewer Dan Kleban and oyster farmer Graham Plattner are running in the 2026 Senate election in this state. Janet (*) Mills governs this state, which like Alaska uses ranked-choice voting for presidential elections. For 10 points, name this US state represented by Susan Collins, with capital at Augusta.
items.a: Maine [or ME]

items.q: In 2024, this state's WLBZ radio station closed after an author stopped bankrolling it. This state's superlatives include having the highest rate of heat pump adoption in the country and the oldest population. A chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee from this state was one of only three Republicans to vote to confirm Ketanji Brown Jackson. Donald Trump has clashed with this state's "radical-left governor," (*) Janet Mills, a supporter of trans athletes. Vermont and this state are the only ones represented in the Senate by an Independent. In 2023, a mass shooter terrorized a bowling alley in this state's city of Lewiston. For 10 points, swing voter Susan Collins represents what New England state?
items.a: Maine [or ME] (The author is Stephen King, and the independent senator is Angus King.)

items.q: A company in this state challenged having to pay truck drivers overtime pay based on the lack of an Oxford comma in one piece of legislation. In 2021, voters in this state approved a ballot measure that guaranteed a constitutional right to food. Three years earlier, this state introduced (*) ranked-choice voting. For 10 points, name this state once governed by Paul LePage.
items.a: Maine

items.q: Popham Colony, which was in this modern-day state, was a direct rival of Jamestown. This state's Penobscot County is home to its city of Bangor. Cadillac Mountain, which is located on Mount Desert Island, is in this state's (*) Acadia National Park. This state's coast is a major site for lobster fishing. A city in Oregon was named after this state's largest city, Portland. For ten points, name this northernmost New England state that has its capital at Augusta.
items.a: Maine

items.q: In December 2025, a wine magnate and former congressman from this state announced he would primary his own successor, April McClain-Delaney. Hakeem Jeffries mocked a senator from this state as "Chris Van Who?" for attacking his refusal to endorse Zohran Mamdani. In 2024, this state's governor accepted a Bronze Star medal twenty years late. Before being elected as a Senator, (*) Angela Alsobrooks responded to the 2024 ramming of this state's Key Bridge. ICE took Kilmar Abrego Garcia from this state to El Salvador's CECOT prison before later returning him. For 10 points, Wes Moore leads what state from Annapolis?
items.a: Maryland [or MD] (The leadin refers to David Trone)

items.q: Akhil Reed Amar called Martin v. Hunter's Lessee the "landmark precursor" of a case involving this state. A precedent established in a case originating from this state was circumvented by selective incorporation. The Supreme Court ruled that the Bill of Rights did not apply to the states when a city in this state was sued by the wharf owner James Barron. Ex parte Merryman challenged (*) Lincoln's suspension of habeas corpus in this state. The Supreme Court ruled that the "necessary and proper" clause gave the federal government implied powers, and that federal law supersedes state law, in a case started by this state's attempt to tax the Second National Bank. For 10 points, name this state sued by James McCulloh.
items.a: Maryland [accept McCulloch v. Maryland] (The case is called McCulloch v. Maryland because the court clerk misspelled his name.)

items.q: This state pioneered "Global Budgets" to prevent rural hospital closures after having the highest rate of readmissions for Medicare beneficiaries. R. Adams Cowley pioneered the nation's first shock trauma center in this state and promoted the "golden hour." The first public US medical school was chartered in this state. The US site of Qiagen ("KY-uh-jen"), the Human Genome Project, and the eastern HQ of the Venter Institute are in this state. The long-tenured director of (*) NIAID ("NY-ad"), an institute in this state, was criticized for its slow HIV/AIDS epidemic response. An ex-Stanford researcher who co-signed the Great Barrington Declaration currently leads a federal agency located in this state. For 10 points, name this state home to the National Institutes of Health.
items.a: Maryland [accept MD]

items.q: This US state is home to a form of fried chicken with cream gravy often garnished with bananas. Tiger sauce and a Kaiser roll are used to serve pit beef, a specialty from this state. A seasoning originally created in this state contains pepper, dry mustard, paprika, and celery salt. One city in this state contains the headquarters of the National Institutes of Health. In this state's largest city, the (*) National Aquarium is located in the Inner Harbor. The Coalition Against Policing is suing to block Johns Hopkins University from establishing a private police force in this state. For 10 points, name this state, where one often adds Old Bay seasoning from blue crabs fished from Chesapeake Bay.
items.a: Maryland

items.q: In this state's town of Whitman, the chocolate chip cookie was supposedly invented at the Toll House Inn. A Nabisco product consisting of fig paste in cookie dough is named for this state's town of Newton. Peanut butter and marshmallow fluff between slices of white bread make up this state's official sandwich, the fluffernutter. A city in this state is nicknamed for a dish of navy (*) beans flavored with molasses and bacon. Dunkin' Donuts was founded in this state, where "Fenway Franks" can be purchased at baseball games. For 10 points, "Beantown" is a nickname for the capital of what state, whose official dessert is Boston cream pie?
items.a: Massachusetts [or MA or Commonwealth of Massachusetts]

items.q: The protagonist of a novel set in this state is reimagined to have five illegitimate children in Suzan-Lori Parks's play In the Blood. George Cram Cook and Susan Glaspell founded an acting troupe in this state that launched the career of Eugene O'Neill. A character from a play set in this state, whose wife is earlier given a 'poppet' doll by Mary, fails to recite the Ten Commandments while being (*) questioned by Reverend Hale. The slave Tituba dances with Betty and Abigail in a play set in this state that ends with John Proctor being hanged. For 10 points, Arthur Miller's The Crucible depicts a witch trial in what state's city of Salem?
items.a: Massachusetts [or MA]

items.q: The 1847 arrival to this state of Peter Randolph and other members of the "Edloe Sixty-Six" was chronicled in Jacqueline Jones' 2023 book No Right to an Honest Living. William Cooper Nell, who established a holiday named for a former slave from this state, worked for a businessman who partnered with Isaac Knapp. After he labeled it a "covenant with Death," an abolitionist in this state burned a copy of the (*) Constitution. The Liberator was published in this home state of William Lloyd Garrison. In this state, troops under Thomas Preston murdered the former slave Crispus Attucks. For 10 points, John Adams hailed from what state that was the site of the Boston Massacre?
items.a: Massachusetts [or MA; accept Commonwealth of Massachusetts]

items.q: The speaker of a poem set in this state accompanies her Aunt Consuelo to a dentist appointment and reads National Geographic in the waiting room. An aquarium in this state "stands in a Sahara of snow now" according to the poem "For the Union Dead." After seeing a "gleam of light" in a (*) "belfry-tower," a character in a poem set in this state "springs to the saddle." That character instructs a friend to hang "one [lantern] if by land, and two if by sea" in a church in this state to alert him to the approach of the British. For 10 points, what U.S. state is the setting of Henry Wadsworth Longfellow's "Paul Revere's Ride"?
items.a: Massachusetts [or MA] (The first poem is Elizabeth Bishop's "In the Waiting Room.")

items.q: A politician from this state taught a lesson on the Holocaust that was later used by a high school class to predict the Rwandan genocide. Don Samuels lost a 2024 primary to a representative from this state who used the phrase "some people did something" in relation to 9/11. This state's new flag features an eight-pointed white star on a dark blue field. This state is home to the largest (*) Somali-American population in the U.S., which includes a member of "The Squad," Ilhan Omar. A governor of this state who described J.D. Vance as "weird" is Kamala Harris' running mate. For 10 points, in what state did Governor Tim Walz respond to the death of George Floyd?
items.a: Minnesota [or MN]

items.q: This state's Fort Saint Charles is in the Northwest Angle, which sits on the Lake of the Woods and crosses north of the forty-ninth parallel. This state is home to Lake Itasca, the source of the (*) MississippiRiver, and its city of Duluth is on the western tip of Lake Superior, just near its border with Wisconsin to the east. The "Land of Ten Thousand Lakes" is, for ten points, what U.S. state whose capital is Saint Paul, a "twin city" with Minneapolis?
items.a: Minnesota

items.q: After a representative from this state was found to not live in his district, Lisa Demuth was elected as its State House Speaker. A politician from this state was removed from the House Foreign Affairs Committee for a 2019 statement declaring "It's All About the Benjamins. " This state's large population of Somali immigrants is represented in Congress by (*) Ilhan Omar. During a 2024 debate, a politician from this state was accused of lying about being in China during the Tiananmen Square massacre. Amy Klobuchar is a senator from, for 10 points, what state where Tim Walz serves as governor from St.Paul, near Minneapolis?
items.a: Minnesota

items.q: Antofagasta and a mining company in this state merged to form Twin Metals, whose copper-and-nickel mine in this state have stalled over a 20-year moratorium imposed around the Boundary Waters. In this state, Toua Xiong ("twah s'yong") and Nou Vang ("noo vahng") plan to open a second location of an ethnic market in early 2025 at Maplewood Mall; vendors in that market's original location serve dishes such as kooj tis qaib ("kone tee KYE") and papaya salad. In the 1970s, this state's two largest cities were home to the largest (*) Swedish American neighborhoods in the United States. Little Mogadishu is located where I-94 and I-35 intersect in this state and where I-94 crosses the Mississippi River. It's not California, but this state houses the second-largest statewide population of Hmong Americans. For 10 points, name this state home to Representative Ilhan Omar.
items.a: Minnesota [or MN]

items.q: Tim Ryan lost this state's 2022 election to succeed Rob Portman and join Sherrod Brown in the Senate; the election was won by the author ofHillbilly Elegy.False, racist allegations against this state's (*) Haitian population in Springfield were made by the Republican Vice Presidential candidate, this state's JD Vance. For ten points, name this former presidential swing state whose Rust Belt cities include Cincinnati and Cleveland.
items.a: Ohio

items.q: The narrator describes a river that has "two shores: / the one in hell, the other / in [this US state]" in a poem titled for a [emphasize] neighboring state's "Oldest Whorehouse." Sons who "grow suicidally beautiful" appear in a poem titled "Autumn Begins in" a town in this state. This was the home state of the poet of The Branch Will Not Break, James Wright, who contributed to a literary magazine founded at a college in this state by John Crowe Ransom. In a story, a teacher's tendency to caress his students forces him to flee [emphasize] to this state and change his name from Adolph Myers. Wing Biddlebaum appears in a collection set in this state introduced as a "Book of the Grotesque." For 10 points, the story "Hands" appears in a Sherwood Anderson collection set in what state's fictional town of Winesburg?
items.a: Ohio [or OH; accept Winesburg, Ohio] (The magazine is The Kenyon Review.)

items.q: In this state, Charles Grandison Finney led the first university to graduate Black women. The Kirtland Temple is in this state, where in 1830, Lyman Beecher became president of its Lane Seminary and oversaw 1834 abolitionist debates. A former Shaker settlement in this state names its suburb of Shaker Heights. A young John Brown moved to the Connecticut Western Reserve in this state, the easternmost in which public schools were created under the Northwest Ordinance. After Virginia, this state has produced the most U.S. Presidents. For 10 points, the Toledo War was fought between Michigan and what state, where a Roman hero is the namesake of Cincinnati?
items.a: Ohio [or OH] (Charles Grandison Finney led Oberlin College.)

items.q: In a film, a theater in this state is shown in cutscenes with a marquee advertising "Fiddler on the Roof" and "Porgy and Bess" for its 2013 season. In an updated version of a song, one character sings "Is it just that you're disappointed / to be going again" to this state before asking, "did you think this would all be much easier / than it turned out to be?" A character says "I mean you made it to" this state before asking "who knows where else we can go?" in a song where a character says, "I think we're gonna be okay" because of her smile. In a song describing this state, a character sings "I could have a satchel full of dollar bills / (*) cures for all the nation's ills / pills to make a lion purr," but is instead in this state. An actress in this state shares her dressing room with "a former stripper and her snake, Wayne" while performing as Evita in matinee shows. In The Last Five Years, Kathy describes her summers working at a theater in, for 10 points, what state where she is "certain [she'd] prefer to be going slowly batty / forty miles east of Cincinnati"?
items.a: Ohio

items.q: For playing a character in this musical, Ali Stroker became the first actor in a wheelchair to win a TonyAward. In this musical, a character sings that "folks are feeling sad / 'Cause they used to treat him bad"while acting out his own funeral. In one song from this musical, two characters advise each other on how tonot (*) appear in love. Agnes de Mille choreographedthis musical's dream ballet. In this musical, Curly sings, "Thecorn is as high as a elephant's eye" when he enters on a "beautiful mornin'." For 10 points, name this Rodgers andHammerstein musical with cowmen and farmers, which takes place in its namesake U.S. territory.
items.a: Oklahoma!

items.q: In this state, Laura and L. D. Nelson were lynched by Woody Guthrie's father and 40 other men who seized them from a jail in Okemah County. A sit-in movement in this state's capital, led by Clara Luper, partly slowed Stanley Draper's plans to make this one of the largest by area. This state's Drexel Building was where Sarah Page was assaulted leading up to the lynching Dick Rowland. A city in this state is home to the Greenwood district, where three dozen people died during riots on "Black Wall Street." The first freed Black residents to settle in this state came during the Trail of Tears. For 10 points, name this state where a race massacre took place in Tulsa.
items.a: Oklahoma [or OK]

items.q: John Wilson's 2023 recording of this musical was the first complete recording of the original orchestration by Robert Russell Bennett. Miles Davis's album Steamin' opens with a cover of a song from this musical in which a character describes "the slickest gig you'll ever see." A character in this musical imagines "long tangled hair" which "falls across my face" in a song in which he vows to win a bride, "Lonely Room." One of the female lead's love interests sings "chicks and ducks and geese better scurry" before the imagined "surrey with the fringe on top." Agnes de Mille choreographed this musical's "dream ballet" in which Laurey "makes up her mind" about Jud and Curly. For 10 points, name this Rodgers and Hammerstein musical titled after a US state.
items.a: Oklahoma!

items.q: This state's waterfall-rich Arbuckle Mountains are home to the largest Christian youth camp in the US. It's not Kansas, but in 1907 the American Bison Society shipped 15 bison to a refuge in this state's Wichita Mountains. A college town in this state is home to the NWS's Storm Prediction Center. In 2014, this state had twice as many earthquakes as California due to "wastewater disposal" from the (*) fracking industry. This state's northeastern Green Country contains part of the Will Rogers Turnpike as well as the city of Tahlequah, where road signs use a syllabary invented by Sequoyah. This state houses the headquarters of the Cherokee Nation. For 10 points, name this state home to the oil boom town of Tulsa.
items.a: Oklahoma [or OK]

items.q: The bilingual radio station KILI operates out of this state's town of Porcupine, which was proposed as the capital of a breakaway nation-state in 2007. The local grocery store chain Buche ("BOO-ee") Foods, spelled B-U-C-H-E, and its convenience store affiliate Gus Stop operate entirely in this state. During World War II, the US evicted Indigenous residents for practice bombing runs in this state's Stronghold District, which took off from Ellsworth Air Force Base. Each April, this state's flagship university in Vermilion hosts a Wacipi ("wah-CHEE-pee") powwow. The Rosebud Indian Reservation is in this state, where a rideable jackalope statue sits outside the road stop Wall Drug. A region with eroded buttes ("byootz") sacred to local Indigenous people names Badlands National Park in, for 10 points, what state, where some Native residents object to Mount Rushmore?
items.a: South Dakota [accept SD] (Activist Russell Means proposed Porcupine as the capital for the "Republic of Lakotah.")

items.q: In this state, the Minuteman Missile National Historic Site is located east of Ellsworth Air Force Base. Attractions in this state include the Wall Drug Store and the world's largest reptile zoo. This state boasts the world's last remaining corn palace in its city of Mitchell. This state's town of (*) Sturgis annually hosts the largest motorcycle rally in the world. The Pine Ridge Reservation is in this state, which contains the southern portion of Standing Rock. This state's largest cities are Rapid City and Sioux Falls. Kristi Noem governs, for 10 points, what Plains state whose Black Hills contain Mount Rushmore?
items.a: South Dakota [or SD]

items.q: 81 of the 206 US-based trusts revealed in the Pandora Papers are based in this state, making it likely the US's biggest tax haven. In 1979, governor "Wild Bill" Janklow forced through deregulation of credit rates to allow Citibank's credit card division to move to this state's largest city. Indigenous groups have protested the use of alcohol near this state's sacred Bear Butte by participants in an annual event whose 2020 iteration may have been the US's largest (*) Covid superspreader. This state is home to the world's largest motorcycle rally in its town of Sturgis. To keep a claim on the land home to this state's most famous tourist site, a $1 billion settlement has long been rejected by the Sioux. For 10 points, name this state home to Black Hills State University and Mount Rushmore.
items.a: South Dakota

items.q: A jurisdiction located almost entirely within this state was where chairman Dick Wilson formed a paramilitary police force called the GOONs. In 1973, two years after a similar action in California at Alcatraz, a historically significant site in this state was occupied by Russell Means and other members of AIM. A location in this state titles a Dee Brown work of popular history named Bury My Heart at [that location in this state]. In this state, the 7th Cavalry killed Spotted Elk and over 200 civilians at a Lakota camp in 1890. For 10 points, what state was the site of the Wounded Knee massacre and hosts a Crazy Horse memorial near Mount Rushmore?
items.a: South Dakota [accept SD]

items.q: The seat of this state's Millard County is Fillmore and contains Sawtooth Mountain. This state's Dixie region is home to the Hurricane Cliffs. The Weber River empties into a body of water in this state whose arms include Willard Bay. The annual (*) Sundance Film Festival takes place in this state's ski resort of Park City, which is overlooked by the Wasatch Mountains. Antelope Island can be found in this state's largest lake, and the Bonneville Salt Flats can be found here. For 10 points, name this state home to a Great Salt Lake.
items.a: Utah

items.q: The only non-California node on the original ARPANET was a university in this state, where Turing winner Alan Kay wrote a dissertation on FLEX. A young Nolan Bushnell ran the Lagoon Amusement Park in the largest city in this state before going on to found Atari. Bui Tuong Phong came up with Phong shading in this state. A common "Hello World" for 3D modeling is a (*) teapot named for this state. Newspapers.com and Ancestry.com were founded in this state, building on records collected to assist in proxy baptism. A university in this state has a library named for the Marriott family and is in this same city as the largest Missionary Training Center in the world. A university in this state was once called the University of Deseret. For 10 points, name this state whose city of Provo is home to Brigham Young University.
items.a: Utah

items.q: A widespread but likely false rumor claims that this state's largest city bans publicly carrying a violin in a paper bag. Belle London capitalized on the policies of this state's short-lived American Party by founding a red-light district known as the Stockade. A chain based in this state that divides its menu into "refresher" and "reviver" categories sells pink-frosted sugar cookies in addition to its main product. In a controversial book published in this state, Bruce McConkie popularized local resistance to the use of face cards. Before becoming a poet, Dana Gioia was partially responsible for marketing that led to families in this state eating an unusual amount of (*) lime Jell-O. The "dirty soda" concept was pioneered by Swig, a drive-through soda chain based in this state. To shield impressionable children from viewing the preparation of cocktails, this state required bars to erect frosted glass "Zion Curtains" until 2017. For 10 points, what state's restrictive vice laws are inspired by Mormonism?
items.a: Utah [or UT] (Bruce McConkie is the author of the book Mormon Doctrine.)

items.q: This state's capital is laid out in a compass street grid pattern whose namesake meridian is at the southeast corner of its central square. This state is home to the northernmost extent of the Navajo Nation. A 2024 redesign of this state's flag features a beehive against five white peaks. Tall, thin spires of rock called hoodoos can be found in this state's Goblin Valley State Park and (*) Bryce Canyon National Park.A national park in this state contains the Fiery Furnace and "Landscape" and "Delicate" examples of its titular rock formations near the town of Moab. For 10 points, name this state home to Arches National Park and the Great Salt Lake.
items.a: Utah

items.q: A politician with this surname was depicted wearing female undergarments in the painting Mirth & Girth, which led to the court case Nelson v. Streeter. That politician with this last name was the first black mayor of Chicago. A man with this surname recounted attending Hampton University in his autobiography Up from Slavery. The Niagara Movement opposed a man with this surname who argued in favor of (*) vocational training for African-Americans in the Atlanta Compromise, where he repeatedly called for the audience to "cast down your bucket where you are." For 10 points, give this last name of the founder of the Tuskegee Institute, Booker T.
items.a: Washington [accept Harold Washington or Booker T. Washington]

items.q: Indigenous people believed that a foaming meromictic lake in this state had healing properties, leading settlers to found the town of Soap Lake. A polysynthetic language spoken in this state, Halkomelem, is endangered and exhibits a large consonant inventory of 36, both traits typical of its family. In a legend of indigenous people native to this state, a trickster deity becomes bored of his wives and turns them into stone pillars, creating the Twin Sisters formation near Wallula Gap. The contravention of treaties signed at Point No Point and Medicine Creek led tribes in this state to pressure the government in the (*) "Fish Wars". This state's Quileute ("quill-EE-oot") tribe gave the city of Forks, a primary setting of the Twilight novels, its original name. Many tribes native to this state, such as the Cowlitz and Skokomish, once spoke Salishan languages. For 10 points, a chief of the Duwamish people names the largest city in what northwestern state home to Seattle?
items.a: Washington [or WA] (Forks was previously known as Quillayute.)

items.q: A mountain overlooking this river, Mount Muleros, was renamed following the construction of a statue of Jesus on the Cross in the suburb of Sunland Park. A giant red "X" designed by Sebastian overlooks this river and stands on land that was ceded following the resolution of the Chamizal dispute. A pass that this river passes through south of the (*) Franklin Mountains provides the name of a city home to Fort Bliss. A curve of this river is home to Big Bend National Park. Goods crossing the Santa Teresa bridge over this river are frequently produced in maquiladoras ("mah-KEE-lah-DOR-ahz"). The Pecos is a tributary of this river, which flows through the cities of Laredo, Brownsville, and Albuquerque. For 10 points, what river separates the Mexican city of Ciudad Juarez from the Texan city of El Paso?
items.a: Rio Grande

items.q: This body of water was central to a dispute resolved in 1927 that resulted in the unusual geographic position of the so-called "Country Club Area." C. R. Moore foiled a double assassination attempt in 1909 during a conference that involved land adjacent to this body of water called Cordova Island. A 1967 discovery by James Hill Jr. has allowed over 250 people to successfully claim citizenship due to being born near this body of water on the Horcon ("ohr-KOHN") Tract. Outside of Bluetown near the mouth of this river sits a historical marker for the (*) Thornton Affair. Its course was partly placed into a concrete channel in the 1960s to resolve the long-running Chamizal dispute. An incident at a city near this river's mouth resulted in Theodore Roosevelt dishonorably discharging buffalo soldiers who allegedly killed a white bartender. For 10 points, Brownsville lies at the mouth of what river which sets the US-Mexico border in Texas?
items.a: Rio Grande [or Rio Bravo del Norte]

items.q: This river's valley is home to the World Birding Center, a series of nine parks including ones in Roma and Harlingen. It's not in Iraq, but Bagdad Beach lies just to the south of the mouth of this river. The Charro Days festival is held along both sides of this river. Shantytowns called colonias along this river pose public health problems due to lack of clean drinking water. In 2020, there was a large (*) GOP swing in Cameron and Starr counties in this river's valley. This river is just south of SpaceX's Starbase and the vacation spot South Padre Island. Big Bend National Park is named for a section of this river, which divides the cities of Brownsville and Matamoros, and Laredo and Nuevo Laredo. For 10 points, name this river that establishes the eastern part of the US-Mexico border.
items.a: Rio Grande [or Rio Bravo del Norte]

items.q: A city along this river hosts the world's largest yearly celebration of George Washington's birthday; that city also has seven flags on its coat of arms. Many Virgin Galactic launches take place near this river at Spaceport America. This river's floodplain includes the world's largest bosque ("BOSS-kay") ecosystem. This river irrigates the chile fields of the town of Hatch. This river forms the western boundary of the Tularosa Basin, which contains large gypsum dunes in White Sands National Park. This river, whose lower valley names a region that contains cities such as McAllen and Reynosa, forms the eponymous bend of Big Bend National Park. Laredo, Brownsville, and Juarez lie along, for 10 points, what river that forms much of the US-Mexico border?
items.a: Rio Grande [or Rio Bravo del Norte; or Rio del Norte; or Po'soge; or Paslapaane; or Hanapakwa; or Mets'ichi chena; or To Ba'aadi; accept Lower Rio Grande Valley or alle del Rio Grande]

items.q: It's not in Germany, but the folk song "The Wanderer" tells the story of a convict returning from an area named for this body of water. The area around this body of water was once home to the Mal'ta-Buret culture and later the Kurykans, before being taken over by a nomadic confederation. The 1956 damming of the Angara River has caused this body of water to rise by 1.4m. This body of water is sometimes nicknamed (*) "the older sister" in reference to its larger size compared to a nearby lake. The region known as trans-this body of water contains the city of Chita and was part of the short lived Far Eastern Republic from 1920-22. For 10 points, name this largest freshwater lake in the world by volume, containing more fresh water than the North American Great Lakes combined.
items.a: Lake Baikal (prompt on Baikalia, Transbaikal and Transbaikalia with "which is named after what body of water)

items.q: This body of water is home to an endemic species of whitefish called Omul which is recovering from overfishing. The swoop of a dragon's tail created this body of water according to shamans who worship at poles near Cape Burkhan. An area called "Trans-[this body of water]" is also named for the Daur people and is home to the city of Ulan-Ude. This body of water separates agrarians named for its island of Olkhon from the more nomadic eastern (*) Buryats. This body of water is home to the only freshwater seal, the Nerpa. The city of Irkutsk on the Angara River is just north of this body of water in the Yenisey River system. This lake contains over a fifth of all the freshwater on Earth. For 10 points, name this oldest and deepest lake in the world, located in Siberia.
items.a: Lake Baikal [accept Transbaikalia]

items.q: An island in this body of water contains the Khuzhir Museum, which hosts an annual international convention of shamanism, while other cultural events on its shores include an oriental marketplace occupying the Kyngyra Valley to its southwest. A regional wind called the Sarma influences ice road access to its largest island, Orkhon, and its promontories include the Holy Nose Peninsula. Part of a rift zone also cleaving the northeasterly Stanovoy Mountains, it receives the Selenga River which flows north through the Autonomous Republic of Buryatia. The Angara River drains this lake, and provides highly pure water to nearby Irkutsk. For 10 points, name this central Siberian lake, the deepest on Earth.
items.a: Lake Baikal

items.q: In the early 2000s, environmentalists successfully diverted a Transneft oil pipeline from passing within 3,000 feet of this body of water. A polluting pulp and paper mill on its banks was closed in 2013. A first millennium BC stele near this lake shows a giant lizard-like monster similar to the cryptid Lusud-Khan said to live here. The Buryat people who live around this lake refer to it as the "blue eye." This lake is threatened by a plan to open a uranium plant in (*) Angarsk. The Selenga river flows into this lake, which is home to nerpa seals. The 45-mile-long island of Olkhon is located in this lake. It is both the oldest freshwater lake on Earth and, at 1,620 meters, the deepest. For 10 points, name this Siberian lake.
items.a: Lake Baikal [or Ozero Baykal; or Ozero Bajkal]

items.q: Many haplochromine species in this lake are called mbuna in Chitonga. One country claims that a disputed border through this lake hugs its eastern shore; another unusual border makes this lake's Chizumulu and Likoma islands exclaves. This lake has the most unique fish species of any lake and is the southernmost lake where adaptive radiation is exemplified by diverse (*) cichlids. This lake is drained by the Shire River into the Zambezi River. For 10 points, name this African Rift Valley lake whose namesake country has its capital at Lilongwe.
items.a: Lake Malawi [or Lake Nyasa; prompt on Lake Lake]

items.q: People living around this lake catch millions of midges by waving around nets or an oiled frying pan and compress them to make a savory cake called kunga. Surfing on this lake is enabled by strong mwera winds. The exclave islands of Chizumulu and Likoma lie in this lake. Two countries that border this lake refer to it by a name that translates from Yao as "Lake Lake." This is the largest lake situated between the Rovuma plate and the Nubian plate. A UNESCO World Heritage Site celebrates the explosive speciation of mbuna, haplochromine (*) cichlids ("SICK-lids") endemic to this lake. This is the largest lake drained by the Shire ("SHE-ray") River and is also called Lake Nyasa. For 10 points, name this southernmost of the African Great Lakes, bordered by Tanzania, Mozambique, and its namesake country.
items.a: Lake Malawi [accept Lake Nyasa before read] (Lake Nyasa translates to "Lake Lake.")

items.q: This body of water includes Monkey Bay, which is located in the Mangochi district. This lake was the site of the first naval engagement of the Great War. This lake is home to the ports of Likoma Island and Chipoka. This body of water is known by a name that translates to "Lake Lake." This lake is bounded by the Krik Range and the Viphya Mountains. It was discovered by a Portuguese trader in 1846, and David (*) Livingstone referred to it as the Lake of Stars and the Lake of Storms. This lake is drained by the Shire River, a tributary of the Zambezi. It is the 2nd deepest lake in Africa, and is also famous for the variety of cichlids endemic to it. For 10 points, name this lake, also known as Lake Nyasa, whose namesake country has its capital at Lilongwe.
items.a: Lake Malawi [accept Lake Nyasa before mention]

items.q: Portuguese Caspar Bacarro was the first European to report this body of water's existence, which was the site of the first naval action of the First World War, when a single gunboat was disabled by the SS Gwendolen in a port then called Spinxhaven. A territorial dispute in this body of water resulted from the 1890 Heligoland Agreement that gave the polity controlling its northeastern shore no jurisdiction over it. Other ports on this body of water include Likoma Island, Nkhata Bay, and Chipoka. This lake has a southeasterly wind called the mwera. Two countries that border this lake is prefer to call this lake by a generic term from languages spoken around it that literally means "Lake Lake." This lake lies south of the David Livingstone Mountain Range and is drained a tributary of the Zambezi River; that tributary is the Shire River. This southernmost lake of the Eastern African Rift Valley system separates Mozambique and Tanzania from its namesake country. For 10 points, name this lake named for a nearby nation with capital at Lilongwe.
items.a: Lake Malawi [or Lake Nyasa; or Lake lake before mention; prompt on "lake"]

items.q: A family of giant beavers that terrorized this body of water was slain by the hero Atachuukai (a-ta-CHOO-kai) according to the Gwi'chin people and by Yamozha according to the Tli'cho. Its nation's largest national historic site, which centers on the Scented Grass Hills on its southwest edge, protects the heroic legends of its Ehdacho (e-DA-cho) and Sahoue (sa-WAY) Peninsulas. A prophet who predicted the discovery of diamonds to its east, Ayah, lived to see the development at Gras Lake of the Diavik Mine. That eastern shore, at which the Camsell River enters Conjuror Bay at its McTavish Arm, also includes the former pitchblende mines of Port Radium. The Johnny Hoe River empties into its McVicar Arm, while the Keith Arm hosts its main settlement of Deline, also known as Fort Franklin, at which an outlet of this lake passes on to the McKenzie. For 10 points, name this largest lake completely within Canada, located in the Northwest Territories.
items.a: Great Bear Lake

items.q: This feature is known as Sahtu in the predominant native language of its region, and is home to the Saoyu-Ɂehdacho National Historic Site, which is the largest of its kind by area. Jules Verne's The Fur Country features the settlement of Fort Confidence at the mouth of the Dease River, which flows into this body, of which currently only 4 chimneys remain. Located between its country's Interior Plains and Kazan Uplands, this lake's McTavish Arm is bounded by Precambrian rock exposed by glacial erosion from former Glacial Lake McConnell. The largest lake trout ever caught by angling was caught in this body of water, and in 2016 a fuel tanker truck fell through the ice road crossing this lake to Deline. The mining area of Port Radium on this lake was home to the Eldorado and Echo Bay Mines where Gilbert LaBine discovered high-grade pitchblende and silver deposits, though this site was abandoned in 1982. For 10 points, what is this 8th-largest lake in the world and largest lake entirely within Canada, located in the Northwest Territories?
items.a: Great Bear Lake

items.q: The documentary Village of Widows noted the high death rate surrounding this body of water, which was historically used to transport pitchblende to Port Radium. Permanent protection has been granted to sacred land on the peninsulas of Sahoyue-Edacho on this body of water. The five "arms" of this body of water are named Dease, McTavish, McVicar, Keith, and Smith. Fort Confidence, established by the (*) Hudson's Bay Company on this body of water, now lies in ruins. The community of Deline [day-li-nay] lies on this body of water, where Sir John Franklin may have documented the birth of ► ice hockey. For 10 points, name this largest lake entirely within Canada, located in the Northwest Territories.
items.a: Great Bear Lake [or Grand lac de l'Ours; or Sahtu]

items.q: The main settelements on this body of water are located near Echo and Sawmill bays on the east, where one can find the Port Radium mining area, and Fort Franklin on the west coast. The Acasta people were the first to live on its shores, and upon its first discovery by European traders, Athabascan tribes such as the Dogrib and the Hare lived in its vicinity. Noted for its speckled trout, this lake is in the Fort Smith southern Inuvik regions of the Northwest Territories, where it straddles the Arctic circle. Drained to the west by the namesake river into the Mackenzie River, for 10 points, identify this fourth-largest lake in North America and the largest lake entirely in Canada.
items.a: Great Bear Lake

items.q: Around this lake, fishermen use lamp light attraction to catch the endemic sleek late perch in the practice of lusenga. Water temperature in this meromictic lake unusually differs by only three degrees Celsius between its surface and lower regions. This "practically endorheic" lake has an outflow to the sea only when overflowing water levels spill into the Lukuga River at colonial Albertville. At the town of Ujiji on this lake, Henry Morton Stanley uttered the famous words "Dr. Livingston, I presume?" Bujumbura, the former capital of Burundi, is situated at the northern terminus of this lake, which is both the world's longest and second deepest freshwater lake. For 10 points, name this African Great Lake that shares its name with a British colony that united with Zanzibar to form Tanzania.
items.a: Lake Tanganyika [accept Ikiyaga ca Tanganyika]

items.q: The roadless Mahale Mountains National Park is east of this lake, and it is the largest lake directly east of the Mitumba Mountains. The Malagarasi River forms a national border before ending in this lake. The Ruzizi River drains Lake Kivu into this lake. This lake was the largest reached by Burton and Speke; Burton then falsely claimed it as the source of the Nile. This lake is the largest in the Albertine Rift, and it drains via the Lukuga into the (*) Lualaba River. Among freshwater lakes, this lake is the second oldest, second deepest, and longest. For 10 points, name this African Great Lake that used to name non-Zanzibar Tanzania and drains into the Congo River system.
items.a: Lake Tanganyika

items.q: Great Britain and Belgium gained control of this body of water following a bizarre World War 1 naval battle. The Malagarasi and Ruzizi rivers flow into this body of water whose main outlet is the Lukuga River, and the first Western explorers to discover this non-Victoria lake were (*) Richard Burton and John Speke. This lake partially names a modern-day African country, along with an island group to the east. For 10 points name this 2nd deepest lake in the world that is found between the DRC and Tanzania.
items.a: Lake Tanganyika

items.q: The Ubwari Peninsula indents the west shore of this lake, which is only periodically drained by its major outflow, the Lukuga River. Che Guevara used the western shores of this lake as a training camp and water from Lake Kivu flows into this lake via the Ruzizi River. The port of Kigoma is situated on the shore of this lake, as is the capital of (*) Burundi, Bujumbura. Henry Stanley found Dr. Livingstone in the town of Ujiji on the shore of this lake, which is only surpassed in volume and depth by Lake Baikal. Larger than Lake Malawi, for 10 points, name this long African lake that shares its name with a state now joined with Zanzibar.
items.a: Lake Tanganyika

items.q: Nitraria and Tamarix have been planted as a windbreak on this body of water's village of Jabal Kandi. Inhabitants of the Geoy Hill complex depended on a spring flowing into this body of water, and were likely related to the Yanik culture to its east. Several Girdan kurgans overlook this body of water from the south. To the inhabitants of one island within this body of water, it is known as Darya, while an ethnic group dwelling on the shores of this body of water refers to it as the Blue Sea of Kaputan. In ancient times its inhabitants knew it as Chichast, meaning "glittering," though Ptolemy mapped it as Lake (*) Martian. Hulagu Khan and his son Abaka are supposedly entombed in a buried castle on Shahi Island in this body of water along with a massive treasure hoard. This body of water receives snowmelt from the twin massifs of Sabalan and Sahand from the north via the Talkheh River, and is the endpoint for the north-flowing Jagatu and Tatavi. Several islands in this body of water have merged into a large peninsula, as this southernmost of the historical Seas of Armenia rapidly loses volume due in part to a mixing-restricting bridge that causes its north and south waters to often take on blue and red hues. Attempts to revive this lake have brought overflows to its basin from the Zab. FTP, name this salt lake between the provinces of East and West Azerbaijan in Iran.
items.a: Lake Urmia or Daryacheh-ye Orumiyeh (accept Urmu or Darya or Kaputan Tsov also)

items.q: One of the waterways feeding into this body of water is a source of placer gold and emeralds from deposits like Shoshoba and Hariri, and is famous for an ancient stele describing how to find and harvest water for gold miners. That waterway's mineral wealth was protected by fortresses at Ikkur and Quban. The trade terminal of Korosko on this body of water replaced by the railroad to (*) Wadi Halfa which enters it from the south; both of those routes begin at Abu Hamad. The Oasis of Kharga is dominated by the Qamhat, a people originally from the basin of this body of water. The Kiosk of Qertassi as well as the serpent idols of Dedwen and a series of inscriptions which portrays the king Silko as a Roman horseman are found to the north of this body of water. The Gate of Kalabsha was gifted to Germany in gratitude for efforts surrounding this body of water. The Hall of Nectanebo is found on the island of Agilkia as a result of those efforts, though the great fortress of Buhen could not be saved from the creation of this body of water. FTP, name this large lake formed by the Aswan High Dam overlooked by the Temple of Abu Simbel, named for a president of Egypt.
items.a: Lake Nasser (accept Lake Nubia) or Boheirat Naser

items.q: The border between two cities on this lake is marked by 22 oversized sculptures depicting the Major Arcana, the trump cards of a tarot deck. In 2019, Rolls Royce is scheduled to test a liquefied natural gas engine on a car ferry that operates on this lake. Swedish countess Bettina Bernadotte [BEAR-nah-DOT] owns a baroque palace on this lake's island of (*) Mainau [MY-now]. The mountainous Bodan ridge juts into this lake, giving it the appearance of a tuning fork. Bregenz, Kreuzlingen [CROYTS-ling-inn], and Lindau are among the major cities on this lake. A Carolingian polity centered on the northwestern arm of this lake is the likely origin of its German name, Bodensee. For 10 points, name this lake at the junction of Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.
items.a: Lake Constance (or Lake Konstanz; accept Bodensee until mention)

items.q: Sir John Moore led a disastrous expeditionary force to this body of water that never landed as he quarreled with the local king over command. A division of Spanish troops on this body of water under the Marquis de la Romana arranged to be spirited away by the Royal Navy when they learned of the accession of Joseph Bonaparte. During the winter of 1809, an army had to burn frozen ships to keep warm as they took heavy losses marching across this body of water. After fighting two simultaneous wars around this body of water, a country deposed an erratic British (*) ally for a 41-year-old crown prince who quickly dropped dead from a stroke. The Royal Navy responded to the launch of the Continental System by bombarding a neutral capital on this body of water. For 10 points, a country on what body of water elected Marshal Bernadotte king during the Napoleonic Wars after losing the Grand Duchy of Finland?
items.a: Baltic Sea [accept the Øresund, Sound, Danish straits, Gulf of Bothnia, Kvarken, or Gulf of Riga; accept Gulf of Finland before "Finland"]
items.s: 2024 History of the World Part II

items.q: The northern terminus of the Old Salt Road was a city on this body of water that was referred to as the "Queen of" one confederation. Amber from along this body of water was transported south as part of the Amber Route. One confederation built trading posts called kontors along this body of water. Albert of Mecklenburg hired a band of pirates to oppose a monopoly held by that confederation in this body of water. The yearly (*) Skane Market was a major trading event for herring in this body of water. The Victual Brothers were headquartered in this body of water's port of Visby. Other major trading centers along this body of water included Lubeck and Danzig. The Hanseatic League operated in, for 10 points, what sea in Northern Europe?
items.a: Baltic Sea

items.q: Ancylus Lake is a predecessor of this body of water, and the Sambia Peninsula is located in this body of water. Oulu and Vaasa are located on this body of water. The Great and Little Belts drain this body of water into the Kattegat, and Lake Peipus flows into it. Islands in this sea include (*) Aland ("OH-land") and Gotland, and Kaliningrad Oblast borders this sea. The Gulfs of Bothnia, Finland, and Riga are parts of this sea, and cities on its shore include St. Petersburg and Stockholm. For 10 points, name this sea whose namesake states include Latvia, Estonia, and Lithuania.
items.a: Baltic Sea

items.q: A storm surge on this body of water in 1304 killed nearly 300 people in the All Saints' Day Flood. The MV Wilhelm Gustoff was sunk in this body of water, resulting in the largest maritime disaster in history. An order of pirates known as the Victual Brothers constantly opposed a military alliance of cities on this body of water. The (*) Livonian Brothers of the sword established a crusader state at the eastern end of this sea. In 1920, Poland gained access to this sea via a corridor that separated East Prussia from the rest of Germany. For 10 points, name this Northern European body of water, whose trade was dominated by the Hanseatic League.
items.a: Baltic Sea

items.q: Two boys named Jaqmaq are among the enslaved people around this body of water whose lives are chronicled in That Most Precious Merchandise by Hannah Barker. On this body of water, Geoffrey de Thoisy captured hundreds of people near Copa and sold five into slavery. The Office of Saint Anthony levied a head tax on the slave trade on this body of water, which mainly trafficked women to serve as ancillae domestic servants and was similar in scale to the Atlantic slave trade until the 18th century. The Alexandria Ban failed to stop the (*) Mamluks' import of slave soldiers from this body of water like the future Sultan Barquq, founder of the Burji line. Venice competed with the Genoese slave trade on this body of water, which was supplied by Nogai raids on the Wild Fields that brought enslaved Christians and Muslims alike to the port of Kaffa. For 10 points, what body of water was the southern shore of the Golden Horde and its successor, the Tatar Khanate?
items.a: Black Sea [accept the Sea of Azov until Kaffa is read; prompt on the Mediterranean and ask "what body of water were these people first sold and transported from?"]
items.s: 2024 History of the World Part II

items.q: The Empire of Trebizond was centered around this body of water that is north of the Pontic Alps. The Golden Horn is located where this sea connects to the Sea of Marmara via the Bosphorus Strait. The city of Sevastopol is located in (*) Crimea, which is a Russian-controlled peninsula that juts into this sea. The countries of Georgia and Ukraine are situated on this body of water, and Turkey has a northern coastline on it. For ten points, name this colorfully-named body of water in Eastern Europe.
items.a: Black Sea

items.q: Walter Pitman argued that the Biblical flood myth could have originated from a rapid rise in sea level of this body of water. This body of water connects to the Sea of Marmara through the Bosphorus, right next to the city of Istanbul. The city of Sevastopol lies on the shores of this body of water on the (*) Crimean Peninsula. For 10 points, what sea lies south of Ukraine and north of Turkey, possibly named for the dark shadows its storms cast over the water?
items.a: Black Sea

items.q: This body of water is home to St. Anastasia Island and the disputed Zmiinyi Island, known in English as Snake Island. A disputed region along this body of water has a green and white striped flag with a hand and seven stars in the upper left corner. One city on this body of water is Sukhumi, the capital of the separatist region (*) Abkhazia. This body of water lies south of the disputed Tuzla Island, which lies in the Kerch Strait. The cities of Stary Krym and Sevastopol are found in a disputed territory along the northern coast of this body of water. Crimea lies along the shore of, for 10 points, what sea south of Ukraine, which is separated from the Mediteranian by the Bosporus?
items.a: Black Sea [accept Euxine Sea]

items.q: The Tantramar Marshes, which lie northeast of this body of water, are attributed to a giant mythological beaver slapping his tail in it. That beaver, which was really the deity Glooscap in disguise, dwelled on its Cape Blomedon (BLOW-me-don). The fossiliferous Wasson's Bluff and the Five Islands Fault lies along a section of its coast known as the Parrsboro Shore which extends from the Apple River to the Portaupique (por-taw-PEEK) River, and which are known as the "cliffs of" this place. The Cobequid Mountains line that section of coast on Minas Basin. An international park which was a popular retreat for the Roosevelts lies on Campobello Island at the entrance to this body of water whose northwesternmost extension is Passamaquoddy (pa-sa-ma-KWO-dee) Bay. A phenomenon associated with the mushroom-shaped Hopewell Rocks and the Old Sow whirlpool in this body of water is also responsible for a bore on the St. John River which causes its reversing falls. Truro and Annapolis Royal lie on, For 10 points, what Canadian bay noted for its extreme tidal fluctuations?
items.a: Bay of Fundy

items.q: Its northern shore includes Cape d'Or, which is confusingly named after copper deposits. The first European to discover it was probably Joao Alvares Fagundes, who may have made it all the way to Advocate Harbor. Its easternmost point is in Coquid Bay and its northern point is in Chignecto Bay, but the most famous area, just east of Cape Split, is Minas Basin. Its most distinguishing characteristic is the reversing falls where the St. John River enters it. Located between Maine, Nova Scotia, and New Brunswick, FTP, identify this body of water in competition with Ungava Bay for the world's highest tides.
items.a: Bay of Fundy

items.q: Benedict Anderson adopted a title originally used by leaders on this body of water to refer to Filipino semi-feudalistic society. Theodore de Bry made many engravings for an author who advocated for people on this body of water and was welcomed by the queen Anacaona. After failing to convince others to perform a dance called an areito, a revolt on this body of water was led by Hatuey. A branch of people indigenous to this body of water, the (*) Lucayan, were nearly extinct prior to a visit to this body of water by Bartolome de las Casas. The Taino were the indigenous people of, for 10 points, what body of water where Christopher Columbus arrived at the Bahamas?
items.a: Caribbean Sea [prompt on Atlantic Ocean]

items.q: This body of water's Ostinoid culture practiced a form of gardening using raised mounds called canucos. Irving Rouse used pottery styles to delineate the Meillacoid culture in this body of water. This body's Pomier Caves include depictions of people sniffing hallucinogenic powder in a ritual called cohoba, which used stands shaped like zemi spirits. This body of water contains the last remaining Kalinago speakers. In a document addressed to Cardinal Cisneros, this body of water's Lucayan and Ciboney peoples were identified by Bartolome de las Casas. A matrilineal society in this body of water was led by cacique Enriquillo. For 10 points, name this body of water where Taino people settled Hispaniola.
items.a: Caribbean Sea

items.q: This body of water's Ostinoid culture practiced a form of gardening using raised mounds called canucos. Irving Rouse used pottery styles to delineate material cultures in this body of water including the Meillacoid. This body of water's Pomier Caves includes depictions of people sniffing hallucinogenic powder in a ritual called cohoba, which made use of stands shaped like zemi spirits. This body of water contains the last remaining (*) Kalinago speakers. In a document addressed to Cardinal Cisneros, this body of water's Guanahatabey, Lucayan, and Ciboney peoples were identified by Bartolome de las Casas. A matrilineal society in this body of water was led by cacique Enriquillo. For 10 points, name this body of water where Taino people settled Hispaniola.
items.a: Caribbean Sea

items.q: This sea's oldest-known archaeological site, which consists of a shell midden made by the Ortoiroid people, is Banwari Trace. A matrilineal culture from around this sea made three-point stone sculptures of spirits called zemis. Agueybana ("ah-hway-BAN-ah") and Enriquillo ("ehn-ree-KEY-yoh") were leaders of an indigenous group that live in this sea who took the title cacique ("ka-SEE-kay"). The (*) Garifuna descended from inhabitants of an island in this sea. Ciboney ("see-bo-NAY") is a dialect of a language from this sea which is the source of the English words hurricane, barbecue, and cassava. Indigenous peoples often joined the crews of buccaneers active in this sea such as Henry Morgan. For 10 points, name this sea where Taino ("tah-EE-no") people live on Hispaniola.
items.a: Caribbean Sea

items.q: An organization named for this body of water was nicknamed "The Machine" during a period in which its members included Jose Moreno and Adolfo Pedernera. Carlo Zucchi designed much of the dockside of a city on this body of water, including the Solis Theatre. A city on this body of water contains an unusual D-shaped stadium whose architect nicknamed it the "chocolate box". A 22-kilometer coastal avenue along this non-Mediterranean body of water is called the Rambla. An airport named for (*) Jorge Newbery, which lies on this body of water, serves the same city as the larger Ezeiza airport. The "Superclasico" rivalry involves Boca Juniors and a club named for this body of water, which is supposedly the widest river in the world. For 10 points, name this estuary formed by the confluence of the Parana and Uruguay rivers, on which Buenos Aires and Montevideo lie.
items.a: Rio de la Plata [or River Plate]

items.q: To commemorate the 2010 bicentennial of its salt mines, a polluted tributary of this river was dyed Uriburu Green. It's not Tampa, but a city along this river created the longest continuous sidewalk in the world inspired by Barcelona's Rambla. A dialect named for this river is used by the poet Oscar Conde and includes terms named after "Lombard villainy." This river's estuary is bounded by a line that runs from Cabo San Antonio to Punta del Este. The Admiral Graf Spee was scuttled in this river after the first naval battle of World War II. The most spoken dialect to use "vos" in place of "tu" originated along this river in neighborhoods like Palermo. The Superclasico is played between a team named for this body of water and Boca Juniors. For 10 points, the tango developed in dance halls along what river whose estuary borders Montevideo and Buenos Aires?
items.a: Rio de la Plata [or Plate River; accept Rioplatense Spanish]

items.q: After running out of cannonballs, a ship on this river began firing wheels of stale cheese until it dismasted its pursuer and escaped.
