The east coast of (*) Streymoy ("STRAY-moy") in this archipelago includes the Tinganes ("TEEN-gah-ness") peninsula, and is the home of the Logting ("LOOK-ting") parliament. A whale hunt on this archipelago called the grindadrap ("GRIN-dah-drop") is often led by inhabitants of its capital of Torshavn ("TOH-shauwn"). The United Kingdom is south of, for 10 points, what archipelago that serves as an autonomous territory of Denmark?
items.a: Faroe Islands [or Faroes; or Foroyar; or Færoerne]

items.q: Calendar reform in this modern-day country occurred following a man dreaming that everyone else was asleep while he was awake. A struck-through letter "g" was proposed by this modern-day country's First Grammarian in his spelling reforms, which are found in the Codex Wormianus ("vor-mee-AH-nus"). The early history of this modern-day country is dated based on its proximity to the death of St Edmund in a "little book" written by (*) Ari the Wise. According to its Book of Settlements, this modern-day country was first inhabited by monks called Papar. A site in this modern-day country which was taken from the land of a convicted murderer housed its central court at Þingvellir ("THINK-vet-leer"). For 10 points, name this island whose Lawspeaker, Snorri Sturluson, wrote the Prose Edda.
items.a: Iceland [or Island]

items.q: An author from this country described his support for the outcome of the "Trial of the Twenty-One" in his travelogue The Russian Adventure. The time that an author from this country spent at Clervaux Abbey in Luxembourg inspired a novel about a "Great Weaver" from Kashmir. In a novel, "Years of Prosperity" ensue when wool and mutton farmers from this country profit from price increases during World War I. An author who wrote a historical novel about this country's Bell wrote about the sheep farmer Bjartur's attempt to establish the estate Summerhouses. An epic from this country describes how the supernaturally strong Gunnar ends up in multiple feuds, including with his friend Njall. For 10 points, name this country home to Independent People novelist Halldor Laxness and Snorri Sturluson.
items.a: Iceland [or Island; accept Iceland's Bell]

items.q: After being elected in 1980, a president of this country planted sets of three birch trees dedicated to boys, girls, and the unborn while touring it. This country's Redstockings group led the Women's Day Off, in which ninety-percent of its women went on strike. The world's first-ever elected female president led this country and hosted a 1986 (*) disarmament summit in its capital between Ronald Reagan and Mikhail Gorbachev. This country's navy shelled the C. S. Forester, a boat belonging to the United Kingdom, in a series of fishing rights disputes called the Cod Wars. This country's legislature, the oldest in the world, is known as the Althing. For 10 points, name this Nordic country with a capital at Reykjavik.
items.a: Iceland [or Island]

items.q: Water from 24 different sources in this country is displayed in transparent columns in The Library of Water. An artist from this country plays guitar while reclining in a full bathtub in a video installation by him in which nine film projections show musicians in different rooms of a farmhouse, titled The Visitors. In a 2015 retrospective, the MoMA displayed a gravity harp, Tesla coil, and other instruments that an artist from this country used on her "app-album" Biophilia. An artist with heritage from Denmark and this country created four cascades of water emptying into a harbor in New York City Waterfalls and filled the Tate's Turbine Hall with mist and an artificial sun in The Weather Project. A performer from this country wore a dress designed by Marjan Pejoski ("MAR-yahn PAY-oh-skee") that resembles a swan. For 10 points, name this birth country of Bjork.
items.a: Iceland [or Republic of Iceland or Lydveldid Island] (The Library of Water is by Roni Horn. The Visitors is by Ragnar Kjartansson. Icelandic-Danish artist Olafur Eliasson made New York City Waterfalls and The Weather Project.)

items.q: A thinker from this country drew on Jean-Luc Nancy's "The Abandoned Being" to codify a state of exposure to death he called bare life. That thinker from this country synthesized Foucault's biopower with Carl Schmitt's "state of exception" in Homo Sacer. Another thinker from this country questioned whether a new historical epoch was created by Taylor's scientific management in "Americanism and Fordism." That thinker coined the term (*) subaltern to refer to subjects of cultural hegemony in a set of Marxist texts written while incarcerated in this country. Another treatise from this modern-day country advises that it is better to be feared than loved. For 10 points, name this country where the Prison Notebooks were written by Antonio Gramsci, drawing on a treatise from this country titled The Prince.
items.a: Italy [or Italia] (The first two sentences refer to Giorgio Agamben.)

items.q: One film by a director from this country features a dream sequence in which the protagonist's father steps into a grave before his mother transforms into his wife. In another movie from this country, Wanda deduces that her friend's boyfriend robbed her and pushed her into a river. In one movie set in this country, workmen expanding a subway open an ancient crypt, but the murals on the walls (*) dissolve when exposed to air. The opening of one film from this country features a statue of Jesus being carried by a helicopter, which is juxtaposed with a concluding scene of a sea monster caught in a net. That film set in this country sees Marcello chase an actress into a famous fountain. For 10 points, name this country home to the director of 8 1/2 ("eight and one-half") and La Dolce Vita, Federico Fellini, whose film Roma is named for this country's capital.
items.a: Italy [or Italian Republic or Repubblica Italiana]

items.q: A soapmaking poet from this modern country included "Against the Unlearned Poet" in a collection titled for her being a "posthumous muse." The speaker of a poem from this country says "neither tears, nor sighs, nor zest / Wakes pity in [a] cruel lover's breast" after asking "ladies" to "picture a gentle knight." An ornate 17th-century style from this modern country is named for the poet who wrote the epic poem Adonis. Poems of Widowhood collects "spiritual rhymes" by a poet from this modern country who corresponded with a famous painter. A 16th-century woman from this country, who dedicated "Deeply repentant of my sinful ways" and 310 other poems to her aristocratic lover, is mentioned in the first Duino Elegy, which was itself written in this country. For 10 points, what modern-day country was home to Vittoria Colonna and Gaspara Stampa?
items.a: Italy [or Italia; or Italian Republic or Repubblica Italiana] (The first line refers to The Posthumous Muse of Martha Marchina, the Virgin of Naples. The style is Marinism, named for Giambattista Marino.)

items.q: In 1974, an actress-turned-photojournalist from this country interviewed Fidel Castro. Howard Hughes had divorce lawyers waiting at LAX for that actress from this country, who spurned him and made her English debut opposite Humphrey Bogart in Beat the Devil. Two actresses from this country, who may have both had affairs with heart transplant pioneer Christiaan Barnard, posed for a photo together with Michael Jackson as a "truce" during their career-long feud, which was partly over their bust sizes. While eating at (*) Romanoff's restaurant in 1957, the younger of those actresses from this country was photographed side-eyeing at the breasts of Jayne Mansfield. That actress from this country played three roles in the triptych Yesterday, Today, and Tomorrow, starred in A Special Day, and won an Oscar for playing a wartime mother in Two Women. For 10 points, name this home country of rival actresses Gina Lollobrigida ("loh-loh-BREE-jee-dah") and Sophia Loren.
items.a: Italy [or Italia; or Italian Republic; or Repubblica Italiana]

items.q: The Samina River originates in this country and flows into this country's only eastern neighbor. This country is split into two electoral districts called Oberland and Unterland, the latter containing the largest city of Schaan. Outside of Asia, this is the only doubly (*) landlocked country. The Rhine River forms its entire western border and Grauspitz, its tallest mountain, sits on its border with Switzerland. For 10 points, name this tiny municipality located in the Alps, with capital Vaduz.
items.a: Liechtenstein

items.q: In the 1810s, this country's last plague outbreak spurred British official Hildebrand Oakes to execute anyone concealing their infectiousness. As part of a religious revival after a 17th-century epidemic in this country, Nicolas Cotoner ordered the construction of the Sarria Church in Floriana. A lazaretto quarantine station in this country was located at Marsamxett ("mar-sum-SHET") Harbour. Slavery was abolished in this country during a brief French occupation while Napoleon was en route to Egypt. Tripoli and this country were granted in exchange for a yearly tribute of a falcon. The corsair Dragut died attacking Fort St. Elmo during the "great siege" of this country ordered by Suleiman the Magnificent. For 10 points, name this Mediterranean country ruled by the Knights of St. John after their expulsion from Rhodes.
items.a: Malta [or Republic of Malta or Repubblika ta' Malta; accept Great Siege of Malta; prompt on Gozo]

items.q: Sound in a temple in this country was passed by an "oracle hole" through walls made of Globigerina limestone. The last period of temple construction in this country, the site of Ħagar Qim, is named for the site of Tarxien. After Gobekli Tepe in Turkey, the next oldest extant religious structure built by humans is in this country, a temple complex with a name meaning Giantess. The temple of Proserpina on the hill of Mtarfa and the Domus Romana were built in a Roman-era town with a name similar to that of this country. The (*) Holy Infirmary was built in this country after its center of power moved from the non-Arab walled city of Mdina in 1530. The corsair Dragut was killed in this country after directing cannons to attack Fort Saint Elmo protecting its capital's Grand Harbour. That fort and Fort Saint Angelo helped defend this country during a 1565 siege. For 10 points, name this country where the Ottomans were defeated by the heavy fortifications built by the Knights Hospitaller.
items.a: Malta

items.q: A monument in this country's town of Floriana honors its postwar child emigrants, whom the Christian Brothers abused in Australia. The 1980 movie set of "Sweethaven" became this country's Popeye Village. It's not Saudi Arabia or Morocco, but the author of the 15th-century poem Il-Kantilena lived in this country's "silent city" of Mdina near Rabat. Since 2020 due diligence measures, this country only offers "exceptional investors" who obtain residency its "golden passports." This country's Xagħra ("SHAH-ra") Stone Circle and two "megalithic temples" stand northwest of Comino on the island of Gozo. This country's national language, whose Latin script includes the letter "H with stroke," is a Semitic tongue derived from Siculo-Arabic. For 10 points, the father of Pete Buttigieg emigrated from what Mediterranean island country south of Sicily?
items.a: Malta [or Republic of Malta or Repubblika ta' Malta; accept Maltese language or L-Ilsien Malti or Il-Lingwa Maltija] (Pietru Caxaro wrote Il-Kantilena.)

items.q: This country's biggest TV event is a Good Friday telethon to fight children's cancer. A 2019 Guardian piece credits a police dog named Peter with upending this country's politics by catching taxi driver Melvin Theuma, who testified to being involved in an assassination. Hong Kong's Binance Holdings moved its operations to this country, as it was the first to allow regular cryptocurrency exchanges. Michelle, the wife of this country's former Prime Minister, was acquitted of charges that her Panamanian shell company was involved in money laundering. It's not Cyprus, but this country's Individual (*) Investor Program offers passports for about 1 million dollars. A car bomb killed journalist Daphne Caruana Galizia in a scandal that brought down this country's Prime Minister, Joseph Muscat. For 10 points, name this island country, the smallest in the EU.
items.a: Malta [or Republic of Malta; or Repubblika ta' Malta]

items.q: A princess of this country converted her estate into a rehabilitation center for ex-convicts after entering a relationship with a robber known as Rene the Cane. In 1953, a ruler of this country sold control of its "Society of Sea Baths" company to Greece's Aristotle Onassis to revitalize this country's economy. The children's charity AMADE was founded by a princess of this country who had (*) starred in Alfred Hitchcock's Rear Window and To Catch a Thief. In the 1970s, this country's Hercules Port was overhauled to accommodate large cruise ships and yachts. Grace Kelly left acting to marry this country's Prince Rainier III. For 10 points, name this country on the French Riviera that is home to the Monte Carlo Casino.
items.a: Monaco [or Principality of Monaco]

items.q: During a 1955 event in this city, Alberto Ascari accidentally plunged into its Port Hercules. The architect of the Parisian opera house Palais Garnier also designed an opera house in this city called Salle Garnier. Land southwest of this city's Le Rocher district reclaimed from the sea became its Fontvieille ward, which contains this city's Louis II Stadium. After being challenged by its chief official, Alain Ducasse opened the restaurant Le Louis XV in this city. This city is divided into four historical (*) quartiers. The Fairmont Hotel names a notorious "Hairpin" turn of this city's Formula One Grand Prix. In 1956, actress Grace Kelly married into the royal family of this city, becoming involved in its Monte Carlo Ballet. For 10 points, name this small principality in the French Riviera, a resort town for millionaires.
items.a: Monaco

items.q: Around 20 percent of this nation's landmass was recovered from the sea. The highest point in this nation is 535 feet above sea level and located on the slope of Mont Agel, whose peak is in the territory of another country surrounding this one on three sides. This nation plays host to the only marathon whose course passes through three different sovereign nations, and one of the hardest Formula One Grands Prix. This nation ranges from 382 yards to two thirds of a mile wide. Its estimated thirty five thousand citizens cannot enter an edifice in its east hosting a casino. For 10 points, name this second smallest sovereign nation located on the French Riviera which contains Monte Carlo.
items.a: Monaco

items.q: The area around its harbor is known as the Condamine, while Fontvieille is a manmade platform of twenty-two hectares reclaimed from the sea. Despite having only three miles of coastline and thirty thousand people, it joined the United Nations in 1993 with the blessing of the Grimaldi line. For 10 points, name this principality, nine miles east of Nice [NEECE], where Monte Carlo can be found.
items.a: Monaco

items.q: The Ostrog Monastery in this country is an Orthodox Christian pilgrimage site. This country contains one of the oldest virgin forests in its continent, found in a national park that contains Lake Biograd. This country's Durmitor National Park is the predominant location of the Tara River Gorge, the deepest canyon in this country's continent. This country's Boka Navy is a former independent group of sailors that has evolved into a group promoting local folklore, headquartered in Kotor. A major source of tourism in this country is Velika Plaza, a beach found near the city of Ulcinj. The Old Bridge over the Ribnica is found in this country's Stara Varos neighborhood. For 10 points, name this Southeastern European country with capital at Podgorica.
items.a: Montenegro [or Crna Gora]

items.q: It contains the cities of Bar and Cetinje and the western part of Lake Scutari. Its largest city and capital, located at the confluence of the Ribnica and Moraca rivers, is Podgorica. Independent as a kingdom under Nicholas I from 1910 to 1918, its residents voted against resuming independence in a 1992 plebiscite. For 10 points-name this only member, besides Serbia, of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.
items.a: Montenegro [prompt on Federal Republic of Yugoslavia before "Ribnica"]

items.q: In 1861, this country's government sent Abraham Lincoln a letter in 'imperfect but clear' English proposing an alliance and extending honorary citizenship. Napoleon once gifted this country four cannons, although for mysterious reasons, these cannons never reached this country. This country was elected a Communist-Socialist coalition from 1945, the only country in Western Europe to democratically elect a Communist government. A 1957 constitutional crisis in this country was triggered when the majority parliamentary coalition submitted resignation letters before electing an executive body, leading the opposition to declare a provisional government in (*) Rovereta. For 10 points, name this European microstate that remained independent upon the unification of Italy.
items.a: San Marino

items.q: A gang based out of this country, which has stolen over $500 million worth of jewels from London, Tokyo, and Dubai, was dubbed "the Pink Panthers" by the Daily Mail. In this country, the grassroots "OTPOR" movement distributed campaign stickers with the slogan "He's finished!" The 2003 assassination of a prime minister from this country's Democratic Party is believed to have been planned by the Zemun ("ZEH-moon") Clan. This country is home to the "turbo-folk" singer Ceca ("TSAY-tsah"). In 2008, protesters marched in this country's capital in response to a declaration of independence issued by Hashim Thaci ("THAH-chee"). The "Bulldozer Revolution" overthrew a leader of this country who died of a heart attack while being tried for war crimes along with his ally Radovan Karadzic ("KAH-rah-jeetch"). For 10 points, name this country led in the 1990s by Slobodan Milosevic ("mee-LOH-shay-veetch").
items.a: Serbia [or Srbija; or Republic of Serbia; accept Serbia and Montenegro; prompt on Federal Republic of Yugoslavia or FR Yugoslavia; reject "Montenegro"; reject "Srpska" or "Serb Republic"] (The assassinated prime minister was Zoran Dindic.)

items.q: The slogan "he's finished" was created by this modern-day country's Otpor youth movement, which led a campaign to overthrow its leader. 16 employees at this country's Radio Television HQ were killed in a NATO operation that earlier accidentally bombed the Chinese Embassy. This country's "Bulldozer Revolution" overthrew a leader who was later put on trial for war crimes committed with his ally Radovan Karadzic ("KAH-rah-jeech"). In 2006, Montenegro seceded from a union with this country. This country, which has refused to recognize the independence of Kosovo, was led in the 1990s by Slobodan Milosevic ("mee-loh-SHAY-veech"). For 10 points, what country is ruled from Belgrade?
items.a: Serbia [or Srbija or Republic of Serbia; accept Serbia and Montenegro; prompt on Federal Republic of Yugoslavia or FR Yugoslavia; reject "Montenegro"]

items.q: After helping to treat a typhus epidemic ravaging this country's army, British nurse Flora Sandes enlisted and fought as an infantryman. An eight-year-old in this country's army was made a corporal after winning the Battle of Cer ("sehr"). The most decorated female soldier in history fought in this country's army and won her first award after the victorious Battle of Kolubara. This country's forces evacuated to Corfu under its king Peter I, who came to power after army officers led by Apis killed its king Alexander. This country was invaded after it rejected the July Ultimatum, which also led its ally Russia to mobilize. The Black Hand was founded in, for 10 points, what Balkan country invaded by Austria-Hungary at the start of World War I?
items.a: Serbia [or Kingdom of Serbia; reject "Kingdom of Yugoslavia"; reject "Kingdom of Serbs, Croats, and Slovenes"] [The second line refers to Momcilo Gavric and the third line refers to Milunka Savic]

items.q: A future president of this modern-day country gave an inflammatory St. Vitus' Day speech on the 600th anniversary of a 1389 battle. A Chinese embassy in this modern-day country was accidentally bombed during Operation Allied Force. A future president of this country campaigned against the KLA, and that president was toppled in the Bulldozer Revolution. The predecessor to this modern-day country fought a (*) 1999 war to retain control over Kosovo, and Montenegro broke away from this country in 2006. For 10 points, name this modern-day Balkan nation that was once led by Slobodan Milosevic ["mee-LOW-seh-vich"], with a capital at Belgrade.
items.a: Serbia (accept Serbia and Montenegro before mention; prompt on Kosovo or Montenegro until mention; Yugoslavia by asking, "Which constituent republic of Yugoslavia?") [Editor's note: That 1389 battle is the Battle of Kosovo.]

items.q: This country is home to many red and white cave paintings of animals in its Tsodilo Hills. Prehistoric stone tools have been found at Kubu Island in this nation, which sits in the middle of its Makgadikgadi salt pans. This country's northern city of Maun provides tourist access to the world's largest inland delta, the (*) Okavango. This country shares the world's only quadripoint with Zambia, Zimbabwe, and Namibia. For 10 points, what landlocked country that contains the majority of the Kalahari desert is located directly north of South Africa?
items.a: Botswana

items.q: This country has a 590 foot border with its northern neighbor that can be crossed by the Kazungula bridge near the confluence of Chobe and a much larger river. Francistown and Molepole are cities in this country, which contains the Makadikadi ("Muck-guh-dee-guh-dee") salt pans. The Mormobi game reserve is found in a notable wildlife attraction of this country that doubles in size in a yearly flood cycle. This country is home to the largest population of indigenous (*) San Bushmen, who inhabit an inland delta known as the Okavango delta. This largest diamond producing country in the world, has a flag consisting of a light blue background with a black horizontal band with a white outline. For ten points, name this southern African nation that contains the majority of the Kalahari desert and is led from Gaborone.
items.a: Botswana

items.q: Daniel Baxter's memoir One Life at a Time records his eight years treating HIV in this country. This modern-day country's "founding fathers" were dispatched on an 1895 mission to meet with Minister Joseph Chamberlain in London in a successful bid to maintain its independence. A monarch of what became this modern-day country was deemed capable of ruling "but for his unfortunate marriage" to (+) Ruth Williams, an English woman he met at Oxford. Festus Mogae took over control of this country in 1998. This country's first post-independence leader originally returned to the country as a private citizen rather than a royal and was named (*) Seretse Khama. In 1999, the International Court of Justice ruled that this country was the legal owner of Kasikili Island, resolving a dispute over the Caprivi Strip. For 10 points, name this African country whose border is partly defined by the Limpopo River with South Africa.
items.a: Botswana

items.q: In 2000, Spain returned the remains of a man thought to have been born in this country that had been stuffed for taxidermy display in Banyoles until 1991. Tourists to this country are often taken across water bodies in canoe-like boats called mokoro. Translations of names associated with this country include "rain" for its currency, the pula, and "place of small stones" for Jwaneng, a city home to the world's richest (*) diamond mine. A literary character operates the No. 1 Ladies Detective Agency in this country. Englishwoman Ruth Williams's marriage to this country's first president may have influenced the choice of its national animal, the zebra. That leader, Seretse Khama, oversaw a rapid rise in literacy in this country, which contains the delta of the Okavango River. For 10 points, what country's border with South Africa is 15 kilometers from its capital Gaborone?
items.a: Botswana [or Republic of Botswana]

items.q: Trade unions in what is now this country opposed the seizure of power by Saye Zerbo. A leader of this country's Committees for the Defense of the Revolution was often referred to as "Africa's Che Guevara." That leader from this country carried out a series of Popular Revolutionary Tribunals against "lazy" officials. Blaise Compaore [[kahm-pow-REH]] was a longtime president of this country, whose majority ethnic group is the Mossi. This country was once known as the Republic of the Upper Volta. For the point, name this landlocked country which was ruled by Thomas Sankara.
items.a: Burkina Faso (prompt on "Upper Volta" before mentioned)

items.q: In this country, a newspaper called L'Independant investigated the death and torture of a chauffeur for the president's brother Francois. A coup in this country installed a "triumvirate" of Jean-Baptiste Lingani and two other leaders of the Front Populaire. Riots broke out in this country's capital after the suspicious death of the investigative journalist Norbert Zongo. A dictator of this country began a campaign of inoculating millions of its citizens against meningitis and used a phrase that translates as "The Land of the Upright Men," for this country's current name. In the so-called "Christmas War," it skirmished with its northern neighbor over the resource-rich Agacher Strip. In this country, Captain Blaise Compaore overthrew a socialist dictator sometimes known as "Africa's Che Guevara." For 10 points, Thomas Sankara once ruled what country after consolidating his power in Ouagadougou ("wah-guh-DOO-goo")?
items.a: Burkina Faso

items.q: Which country's name means "Land of Upright Men?" It acquired this name in 1984 under the presidency of Thomas Sankara; before this name change it was known as Upper Volta. Bordered to the north by Mali and to the south by Ghana, its capital is Ouagadougou.
items.a: Burkina Faso

items.q: The rapper Smockey organized the Citizen's Broom movement in this country. This country fought its northern neighbour over the Agacher Strip in a conflict often dubbed the "Christmas War." One president of this country known as "Africa's Che Guevara" wrote its national anthem "Une Seule Nuite." That man was one of two presidents of this country who were in the jazz band Tout-a-Coup Jazz; the vocalist in that group (*) Blaise Compaore killed the guitarist Thomas Sankara in a 1987 coup, three years after Sankara had changed the name of this country to a name meaning "land of upright men". For 10 points, Compaore was overthrown in a 2015 coup in which country formerly known as Upper Volta.
items.a: Burkina Faso (accept Upper Volta before mention)

items.q: A leader of this country labeled Kurt Waldheim as "an imperialist pimp" after he protested the brutal beating of burglars. After a debate over his spending, a leader of this country killed Alexandre Banza, who had conspired with him in the Saint-Sylvestre coup. A leader of this country temporarily converted to Islam to obtain funds from Muammar Gaddafi. The gift of two diamonds by a leader of this country to (*) Valery Giscard d'Estaing ("zhees-KAHR dess-TANG") contributed to the latter's 1981 electoral defeat. After a leader of this country killed elementary students for protesting mandated school uniforms, Operation Barracuda restored David Dacko to power. This country was declared an "empire" under a dictator who was accused of cannibalism. For 10 points, name this African country that was ruled by Jean-Bedel Bokassa.
items.a: Central African Republic [or CAR; or Republique Centrafricaine or Centrafrique or Kodorosese ti Beafrika; accept Central African Empire]

items.q: A 1981 election in another country was lost partly because one candidate was implicated with a leader of this country in the 'diamonds affair'. That leader introduced a law to this country stating that thieves would have an ear cut off for the first two offenses they committed and a hand for the third. A president of this country was removed from power for the second time by General Andre Kolingba; that man, who served as both the first and third president of this country, was David Dacko. For 10 points, name this landlocked African country which between 1976 and 1979 was briefly made an empire under Jean-Bedel Bokassa and whose present-day capital is Bangui.
items.a: Central African Republic [or CAR; or Kodorosese ti Beafrika; or Republique centrafricaine; or Centrafrique] <FL>

items.q: The regional peacekeeping force MISAB entered this country in 1997 in the wake of three army revolts. The epithet la colonie poubelle - or, the trashcan colony - was applied to the territory that would become this country. This country's Yakoma people include Andre Kolingba, who became its leader in a 1981 coup. The Muslim state Dar al-Kuti sold slaves from its base in Ndele [in-DAY-LAY], in this modern-day country. Operation Barracuda toppled this country's Emperor (*) Bokassa I, who had named it an "empire." A central plateau in this country and the river that forms most of its border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo are called Ubangi. For 10 points, what landlocked African country is governed from Bangui [BONG-ghee]?
items.a: Central African Republic (or CAR)

items.q: A leader of this country acknowledged his paternity with a Vietnamese concubine of two daughters, one of whom gave birth to a baby that was murdered by the doctor husband of the other. In the 1990s, the police in this country created a special Squad for the Repression of Banditry. This country is the site of long-lasting economic tensions between the poor "northerners," made up of the Gbaya people, and the wealthy "southerners," consisting of the Yakoma. In this country, whose official political party is known as (*) MESAN, a leader was deposed and replaced by his cousin on the feast day of St. Sylvester, or New Years' Eve. A leader of this country who forced schoolchildren to buy school uniforms from a factory he owned was overthrown by Operation Barracuda and replaced with David Dacko. Christian anti-balaka groups arose in this country after its president Francois Bozize was overthrown in 2013 by the mostly-Muslim Seleka coalition. For 10 points, name this former French colony in Africa ruled by the cannibal dictator Jean-Bedel Bokassa.
items.a: Central African Republic [or CAR; or Kodorosese ti Beafrika; or Republique centrafricaine]

items.q: A leader of this country established the state-run marketing board Caistab to regulate prices of its primary export. This country's top military commander Robert Guei ("GWAY") took power after a Christmas Eve coup removed its president Henri Konon Bedie ("bed-YAY"). The New Forces revolted against this country's president in its first civil war, though a cease-fire was reached following its qualification for the (*) 2006 World Cup. Laurent Gbagbo served as a president of this country, where French forces intervened during its second civil war to assist its current president Alassane Ouattara ("wa-TAH-ruh"). Despite a crash in cocoa prices, this country's president Felix Houphouet-Boigny ("HOO-fway BWAH-knee") spent millions on building the Basilica of Our Lady of Peace in its capital. For 10 points, name this West African country governed from Yamoussoukro.
items.a: Ivory Coast [or Cote d'Ivoire]

items.q: Comoe National Park is located in the northeastern corner of this country in its Zanzan and Savanes Districts. The largest church in the world, The Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, is located in this country's capital city. Queen Abla Pokouis the legendary (*) founder of this country named for a product that is now mostly illegal to trade. For 10 points, name this country that is bordered on the east by Ghana and whose capital is Yamoussoukro.
items.a: Ivory Coast [accept:Cote d'Ivoire]

items.q: The Cavally River forms the bottom of this nation's western border, and the Sassandra River runs throughout this country. This country's only mountain range literally translates as the "Eighteen Mountains," which include Mont Nimba. This nation's Baoule people are part of the Kwa language group-speaking Akan. This nation's longest river, the Bandama, was dammed to create the artificial Lake Kossou, and both the Bandama and Sassandra flow into the Gulf of (*) Guinea. This nation's president Felix Houphouet-Boigny moved the capital to his hometown in 1983. For 10 points, name this former French colony between Ghana and Liberia on the Gulf of Guinea, with capital at Yamoussoukro.
items.a: Ivory Coast (accept Cote d'Ivoire)

items.q: One president of this country put on trial the president of the Supreme Court, Ernest Boka, for conspiring against him. He also claimed that Jean-Baptiste Mockey tried to assassinate him using voodoo, which he called the "black cat conspiracy."This country was originally claimed for France by Louis Gustave Binger, the grandfather of Roland Barthes. Its frst president granted shelter to the conspirators who led the coup against Kwame Nkrumah, and granted refuge to Jean-B´edel Bokassa, and also pursued cooperation with France in a policy he called Franc¸afrique. That president, F´elix Houphou¨et-Boigny, used his hometown in this country as the site of the Basilica of Our Lady of Peace, the world's largest church. More recently, France helped Alassane Ouattara oust this country's president Laurent Gbagbo. For 10 points, name this country whose capital was moved from Abidjan to Yamoussoukro.
items.a: Ivory Coast [or C ˆote d'Ivoire]

items.q: This country's first President failed to retire in 1992, as popular support demanded he run again; that leader, Dawda Jawara, was overthrown in a coup in 1994. Recent conflict in this country was averted when Ousman Badjie refused to commit his troops. In January, longtime strongman Yahya Jammeh refused to leave power in this country, prompting a military intervention from neighboring Senegal. Adama Barrow was recently elected president of, for the point, what West African Islamic Republic with capital at Banjul?
items.a: the Gambia

items.q: This country's "Ancient Ksour of Ouadane ("wah-DAHN"), Chinguetti, Tichitt and Oualata ("wah-LAH-tah")" comprise a World Heritage Site. In 1816, the French ship Medusa ran aground at this modern country's Arguin Bank. This country's Haratin plurality could be enslaved without repercussions until 2007, despite it abolishing (*) slavery in 1981 as the last country to do so. This country's Adrar Plateau contains an eroded geological dome called the Richat Structure, the "eye of the Sahara." For 10 points, name this country directly north of Senegal whose capital is Nouakchott.
items.a: Mauritania [or Islamic Republic of Mauritania]

items.q: This country's oasis city of Chinguetti is one of UNESCO's most endangered world heritage sites. It's not Ghana, but one national park in this country is centered around an island that was colonized by the Duchy of Brandenburg in the 17th century. That migratory bird hotspot is Banc d'Arguin. This country's national anthem was written by its national poet, Baba Ould Cheikh, and this country added two red bands to its flag in 2018. This country's ruling (*) Zeydane caste is also known as its "white" moors. This country's Haratin people could be enslaved by the Zeydanes without facing legal repercussions until 2007. For 10 points, name this West African country with its capital at Nouakchott.
items.a: Mauritania

items.q: After an ancient king of this region was murdered in Rome, his household slave Aedemon started a popular revolt here supported by the chief Sabalus. That king of this region married a woman named Julia Urania and requested the help of the governor Publius Cornelius Dolabella to fend off the revolt of Tacfarinas and Garamantes. That final king of this region was Ptolemy, while a more famous earlier king secretly betrayed his son-in-law to Lucius Cornelius Sulla. A modern state by this name was run under a one-party system by Moktar Daddah, who lost power to a bloodless coup led by Mustafa Salek when this country's Zouerate Railway system was attacked. This country's control of the Rio de Oro led it to join Morocco in being plunged into a guerilla war with the Polisario Front. Two ancient kings named Bocchus ruled, for 10 points, what region that shares its name with a modern African nation located to the south of Western Sahara?
items.a: Mauritania [or the Islamic Republic of Mauritania; also accept Mauri Kingdom or the Moorish Kingdom]

items.q: The world's longest train passes from the coast of this country to the mining town of Zouerate (zoo-WARE-aught) in the interior. This country's namesake Thirty Years' War from 1644-1674 failed to bring the Sanhajas to power here. The historical ruins of Awdaghost and Kumbi Saleh, historical centers of the Ghana empire, are found within this country. It is home to people speaking a dialect of Arabic known as Hasaniya as well as French, and cities such as Tidjikdja, Nouadibhou, and Nawakshut. For 10 points, name this large West African country bordered by Western Sahara, Algeria, Mali, and Senegal.
items.a: Mauritania

items.q: In this modern-day country, George Goldie's UAC formed a commercial monopoly through treaties with local leaders. A businessman from this country was exiled to St. Vincent by the consul Harry Johnston. Johnston supported the rival king George Pepple, who converted to Christianity and abolished the monitor lizard as the sacred symbol of the Kingdom of Bonny in this modern-day country. This country's name was popularized through an article in (*) The Times written by Flora Shaw; she would later marry the administrator Frederick Lugard, who wrote a book about his experiences with indirect rule in this country and oversaw the unification of its north and south. In this country, Jaja founded a school in Opobo using his earnings as a middleman in the palm oil trade. For 10 points, name this country home to the majority of Igbo people.
items.a: Nigeria [or Federal Republic of Nigeria]

items.q: The protagonist of a novel from this country searches for his dead tapster in Dead's Town and is addicted to palm wine. In another novel from this country, a clan ties a bicycle they call an "iron horse" to a tree. A character (emphasize) born in this country writes about her experiences with racism in her blog "Raceteenth." Several (*) yam festivals in this country are attended by a man who wrestled Amalinze the Cat. After accidentally shooting a boy at Ezeudu's funeral, the protagonist of a novel from this country is exiled from Umuofia. Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie is from, for 10 points, what home country of the author of Things Fall Apart, Chinua Achebe?
items.a: Nigeria [or Federal Republic of Nigeria] (The novel in the firstline is The Palm-Wine Drinkard by Amos Tutuola)

items.q: This country's namesake Television Authority was modernized by a group led by early Black CBS journalists Barbara Lamont and Randy Daniels called Jacaranda. The first president of this country founded the "Pilot" newspaper and was nicknamed "Zik."After journalist Isioma Daniel compared contestants in a Miss World pageant to the wives of Muhammad, riots broke out in this country's city of Kaduna. (*) Newswatch founder Dele Giwa was killed by a bomb supposedly ordered by this country's president Ibrahim Babangida. The family of the founder of this country's Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People, journalist Ken Saro-Wiwa, sued Royal Dutch Shell for causing his death. For 10 points, name this country which fought a civil war with Biafra.
items.a: Nigeria [or the Federal Republic of Nigeria; accept Nigerian Television Authority]

items.q: In this country, Charles Thurstan Shaw unearthed a sculpture of a vase surrounded by imitation ropework alongside artifacts depicting humans with scarification known as ichi. It's not the Netherlands, but a Neolithic Scots pine dugout canoe from Dufuna in this country is the second-oldest known boat. This country's sites of Taruga and Samun Dukiya characterize a culture known for clay sculptures with triangular eyes and perforated pupils. Walls called Sungbo's Eredo surrounded this country's Ijebu Kingdom, whose founder hailed from a city known for sculpting grooved heads cast using the lost-wax method. Kings known as eze("ay-zay")ruled an ethnic group in this modern-day country, whose attempted secession was opposed by Yakubu Gowon. For 10 points, the iron-smelting Nok culture was from what country, whose Ife Empire was founded by the Yoruba?
items.a: Nigeria [or Federal Republic of Nigeria or Jamhuriyar Tarayyar Najeriya or O hanjiko O haneze Naijiriya or Orile-ede Olominiira Ijoba Apapo ile Naijiria or Fediral Repoblik of Naija] (The first clue refers to Igbo-Ukwu.)

items.q: A former military officer's service in this country inspired him to create the Will to Intervene project at Montreal's Concordia University. In this modern-day country, Catholic priest Leon-Paul Classe promoted race-based colonial discrimination in alignment with the ubuhake system. The names of a notable radio station and hotel in this country include the French term for "thousand hills." The (*) Arusha Accords failed to stop a conflict in this country whose refugees sparked a [emphasize] different conflict that toppled Mobutu Sese Seko. Radio broadcasts in this country encouraged "cut down the tall trees" to incite violence among Interahamwe members after a plane was shot down with President Juvenal Habyarimana on it. For 10 points, name this neighbor of Burundi whose largest ethnic groups are the Hutu and Tutsi.
items.a: Rwanda [or Republic of Rwanda]

items.q: A 2015 play by Katori Hall set in this country dramatizes a 1980s Marian apparition in Kibeho. The Girinka program provides livestock to poor families in this country, where bars devoted to ikivuguto and other kinds of milk are common. Nyungwe National Park contains the northern part of a rainforest in this country, which has a prominent border crossing with its southeastern neighbor at waterfalls near Rusumo. This country on the eastern shore of Lake Kivu is accused of supporting a neighboring country's M23 rebels. In 2023, this country released former hotel manager Paul Rusesabagina from prison after international pressure on its longtime president Paul Kagame. For 10 points, Kigali is the capital of what country where Tutsis were the target of a 1994 genocide?
items.a: Rwanda [or Republic of Rwanda or Repubulika y'u Rwanda or Republique du Rwanda or Jamhuri ya Rwanda]

items.q: This country destroyed many Batwa pygmies' homes in a campaign against thatched roofs. This country currently chairs the Commonwealth of Nations; it held the 2022 summit at which the Commonwealth welcomed the first members since this country joined in 2009. This country denies supporting an insurgency in a neighboring country, M23. Like Sierra Leone, this country requires citizens to (*) clean on the last Saturday of each month. In 2022, the U.K. signed a deal with this country to deport asylum seekers to it. Former president Pasteur Bizimungu was imprisoned in this country, the so-called "Singapore of Africa," by a politician from the RPF who has led it since 2000. For 10 points, name this country whose president Paul Kagame created "reconciliation villages" after a 1994 genocide.
items.a: Rwanda

items.q: Jan Vansina's book on "antecedents" to this modern-day country describes Tsobe ritualists backing its ruler Sentabyo, who caught smallpox from a cloth from Gisaka. This country's Nyiginya dynasty was abolished in 1961 after the "Wind of Destruction," an anti-pastoralist "social revolution" led by Gregoire Kayibanda. This country's army funded the Rally for Congolese Democracy by forcing Kivu's Walikale people to mine coltan in the Second Congo War. Leaders of this country's "Patriotic Front" met in Tanzania to end its civil war in the Arusha Accords before an assassin shot down its president Juvenal Habyarimana ("hob-gyah-ree-mah-nah"). Paul Rusesabagina's ("roo-say-sah-bah-gyee-nah's") Hotel des Mille Collines ("oh-tell day meel kaw-leen") saved people from the Interahamwe in this former Belgian mandate north of Burundi. For 10 points, what country's president Paul Kagame ("kah-GAH-may") led a Tutsi force during its 1994 genocide?
items.a: Rwanda [or Republic of Rwanda or Repubulika y'u Rwanda or Republique du Rwanda or Jamhuri ya Rwanda; accept Kingdom of Rwanda; or Ubwami bw'u Rwanda or Royaume du Rwanda; accept Rwandan Genocide; accept Rwandan Civil War; accept Rwandan Patriotic Front; accept Rwandan Revolution or Revolution rwandaise; accept Antecedents to Modern Rwanda; prompt on Ruanda-Urundi]

items.q: J. F. Easmon treated this colony's rampant "blackwater fever" a century after Anna Maria Falconbridge narrated "two voyages" during its deadly rainy seasons. Jamaican Maroons crushed a Methodist rebellion against this colony's monopolistic namesake company, which bought land from Naimbana of Koya around the Rice Coast's cotton tree. This colony's Anglican Fourah Bay College educated Samuel Ajayi Crowther and Africanus Horton. Bai Bureh led 1898 resistance to a hut tax in this colony, which was conceived by Granville Sharp to relieve London's poor. This colony's Vice-Admiralty Court judged the Preventative Squadron's "recaptives" after an 1807 act. Thomas Peters, a founder of this colony's Krio elite, left Nova Scotia in 1792. For 10 points, 35 Amistad mutineers and many Black Loyalists resettled what British colony bordering Liberia?
items.a: Sierra Leone [or Salone; accept Freetown or Province of Freedom; accept Granville Town until "Granville" is read; accept Sierra Leone Colony (and Protectorate), Sierra Leone Protectorate, Colony of Sierra Leone and its Dependencies, Sierra Leone Company, or Friendly Society of Sierra Leone; prompt on British West Africa or British West African Settlements or British West African Territories] (The West Africa Squadron formed after the Slave Trade Act 1807.)

items.q: The kamajors, a group of traditional hunters in this country, were used as its paramilitary Civil Defence Forces in the late 20th Century. Civilians in this country's capital were killed indiscriminately in 1999 during Operation No Living Thing. In 1992, a military officer became the youngest head of state in the world when he seized power in this country: that officer was (*) Valentine Strasser, who overthrew Joseph Momoh. Milton Margai became this country's first Prime Minister after he led it to independence from Britain. The Abidjan Accord and Lome [LOH-may] Agreement attempted to end this country's civil war in which the Revolutionary United Front forced child soldiers to mine diamonds. For 10 points, name this country with capital at Freetown.
items.a: Sierra Leone [accept Salone]

items.q: A group based in this country supposedly rubbed cocaine into their soldiers' open cuts to make them fearless during fighting. Loyalists from this country's army supported that group during a looting spree colloquially known as "Operation Pay Yourself." This country's capital was evacuated by British forces in Operation Palliser. The memoir A Long Way Gone by (*) Ishmael Beah describes this country's civil war, which led to the signing of the Lome Accords. Foday Sankoh led a rebel group in this country that was supported by a neighboring country's NPFL under Charles Taylor. That group, the Revolutionary United Front, used child soldiers to mine diamonds during this country's civil war. For 10 points, name this southeastern neighbor of Liberia led from Freetown.
items.a: Sierra Leone

items.q: In 2000, the British military was horrified to discover that it had paid for the retraining of an infamous sadist from this country, a female militia leader named Adama Cut-Hands. A rebel leader from this country was fond of giving menacing colloquial nicknames to military actions, like "Operation Pay Yourself" and "Operation No Living Thing." This country used IMF funds to pay South African mercenary firm Executive Outcomes to terrorize its citizens. The Abidjan and Lome Accords attempted to end a civil war in this country driven by Foday Sankoh and the Revolutionary United Front, backed by Liberia under Charles Taylor. For 10 points, name this West African country whose rich diamond mines have led to various wars to control Freetown.
items.a: Sierra Leone

items.q: In this country, nonviolent, pro-democracy protestors chanted the slogan Silmiya, meaning "peaceful," while orchestrating sit-ins and rallies in the face of violent repression. A coup in this country that overthrew the Hamdok government violated a power-sharing agreement made between the FFC and TMC. Over 400 doctors and patients were massacred in a Saudi-funded maternity hospital in this country in El Fasher. General Hemedti's Rapid Support Forces have utilized their access to lucrative gold reserves in this country to obtain UAE support against the rival SAF. In 2019, pro-democracy protests triggered a military coup that ousted this country's longtime dictator Omar al-Bashir. For 10 points, former members of the Janjaweed militia are orchestrating yet another genocide in what country's region of Darfur?
items.a: Sudan [or Republic of the Sudan; or As-Sudan or Jumhuriyat as-Sudan; reject "South Sudan"]

items.q: Ending a conflict in this country was the goal of the most recent Treaty of Jeddah. The support of one group in this country by the United Arab Emirates led Macklemore to cancel a concert in Dubai. Two factions in this country had originally worked together to depose Omar al-Bashir. A military force in this country absorbed the remnants of the Janjaweed militia under its leader, (*) Hemedti. This country has seen the massacre of Masalit people in its region of Darfur. This country's army, led by Abdel al-Burhan, is fighting the Rapid Support Forces. For 10 points, name this country whose ongoing civil war has included the Battle of Khartoum.
items.a: Sudan [or Republic of the Sudan or Jumhuriyah as-Sudan; accept Sudanese Civil War]

items.q: A conflict in this country was mediated in Saudi Arabia by the 2023 Treaty of Jeddah. The Rapid Support Forces, a rebel coalition led by Hemedti and other Janjaweed militia forces, is fighting a civil war in this country against the ruling general Abdel Fattah al-Burhan; that civil war has caused extreme famine in the (*) Darfur region. For ten points, name this African country with capital Khartoum that, in 2011, had its southern portion breakaway as an independent country.
items.a: Sudan (accept Republic of theSudan; do notaccept or prompt on "South Sudan")

items.q: This country's company GSK Advance has been sanctioned for secretly purchasing Russian drones from Aviatrade LLC. In this country home to Radio Dabanga, the Tagadum coalition dissolved after failing to broker a peace deal. This country's internationally-recognized Transitional Sovereignty Council is led by general Abdel Fattah (*) al-Burhan. The Masalit people in this country have been targeted by the US-sanctioned commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti. Antony Blinken issued sanctions against this country's Rapid Support Forces, which developed from the Janjaweed militias, on charges of genocide against non-Arabs. For 10 points, name this country whose civil war has heavily impacted Darfur and Khartoum.
items.a: Sudan [or Republic of the Sudan; or Jumhuriyyat as-Sudan; accept New Sudan; reject "South Sudan"]

items.q: A leader in this modern-day country was assassinated while playing a board game after nationalizing clove plantations. That leader in this modern-day country came to power during a revolution led by the divinely inspired John Okello. This country's ruling Chama Cha Mapinduzi ("CHA-mah cha mah-peen-DOO-zee") party formed after the (*) Afro-Shirazi ("shi-RAZ-ee") party merged with another party whose official ideology was "familyhood." This country's first leader issued the Arusha Declaration and developed the principle of "Ujamaa." ("oo-JAH-maa"). This country formed after Abeid Karume ("ah-BEYD ka-RUH-me") led Zanzibar to merge with its western mainland neighbor. For 10 points, name this East African country once led by Julius Nyerere ("nyeh-REH-re").
items.a: Tanzania [accept United Republic of Tanzania or Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania]

items.q: This country established one of the first wildlife land trusts in the world along a corridor from its Lake Manyara National Park. This country's highest peak is made up of the Kibo, Mwanzi, and Shira volcanic cones. A nomadic ethnic group that lives in the northern portion of this country were relocated to Ngorongoro Crater, which also contains a site of early (*) human remains at Olduvai Gorge. The Maasai people inhabited a region of this country home to a Great Migration of zebra wildebeests. For 10 points, name this East African country home to the Serengeti and Africa's highest peak, Mount Kilimanjaro.
items.a: Tanzania

items.q: Over 1.5 million wildebeest and zebras migrate in a clockwise loop from this country to its northern neighbour during an annual "Great Migration." This country's island of Unguja ("oon-GOO-yah") contains its historic Stone Town, whose architecture reflects the influence of Arab and Indian merchants. By 2050, Africa's last glaciers are expected to disappear on a large freestanding stratovolcano in this country. This country's western border is partly formed by Lake (*) Tanganyika ("TAN-gan-YEE-kah"), which also names a British territory that was merged with Zanzibar to form this country. For 10 points, Dar es Salaam is the largest city in what East African country where Mount Kilimanjaro is located?
items.a: Tanzania [or United Republic of Tanzania; or Jamhuri ya Muungano wa Tanzania]

items.q: Oyster Bay, a neighborhood in this country's largest city, was the birthplace of Tingatinga paintings, which use layers of bicycle paint. Homo habilis remains have been found in the Olduvai Gorge in this country, which also contains the world's largest intact caldera, Ngorongoro ("en-gorong-goro") Crater. A four-year-long war between the Kahama and Kasakela chimpanzee communities occurred in this country's Gombe National Park, where Jane (*) Goodall conducted her research. Two million wildebeest and zebra migrate across the Serengeti annually in this country. This country moved its capital to Dodoma from its largest city, Dar es Salaam. Africa's tallest peak, Mount Kilimanjaro, is found in, for 10 points, what country, formed from the union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar?
items.a: Tanzania

items.q: A leader of this country controversially planned to turn over 25 percent of its land to build an agrarian utopia together with the Maharishi Mahesh Yogi. That leader of this country enumerated eight principles, blending Marxism and Christianity in this country's namesake "Humanism." Officials in this country engaged in gunfights with Alice Lenshina's syncretic Lumpa movement. A schoolteacher in this country failed to convince its first leader to try and spread Christianity to (*) Mars via a space program. Mainza Chona founded this country's socialist UNIP party, which ended up in major debt to the IMF due to mass nationalizations in the Mulungushi Reforms. This country's first president was succeeded by Frederick Chiluba and nationalized its critical copper mining industry. For 10 points, name this country once led by Kenneth Kaunda from Lusaka.
items.a: Zambia [accept Zambian Humanism]

items.q: It's not Gabon, but a five-foot-tall former president of this country remarked "power is sweet" upon winning its first democratic election. One opposition leader in this country is under arrest for treason due to an incident in which he failed to stop for the presidential motorcade. The sudden death of one of this country's leaders led to the accession of Sub-Saharan Africa's first (*) white head of state since apartheid, Guy Scott. His caretaker government held power after the death of Michael Sata. The privatization of this country's copper mines in the early 2000s was bungled by the government of Frederick Chiluba, who was acquitted of corruption charges in 2009. For 10 points, name this country where Edgar Lungu won an election by less than one percentage point over Hakainde Hichilema to take power in Lusaka.
items.a: Zambia

items.q: After independence, this country arrested Alice Lenshina, whose Lumpa Church had caused deadly conflicts nationwide. Schoolteacher and failed mayoral candidate Edward Nkloso trained people in rolling in a barrel and walking on their hands for this country's unofficial space program in the 1960s. This country's 1996 elections were boycotted by the UNIP after an amendment was passed limiting the presidency to children of citizens, forcing a Malawi descended candidate out and ensuring the victory of Frederick (*) Chiluba. This country was led from independence to 1991 by a man who developed a national "humanism" and cut off trade with his southern neighbor Rhodesia. For 10 points, Kenneth Kaunda led what landlocked African country with capital at Lusaka.
items.a: Zambia

items.q: This archipelago is the first place whose natives were struck by a disease called modorra. A Catholic convert named Anton identified a statue venerated on these islands as the Virgin Mary. This archipelago's first documented European resident was Genoese sailor Lancelotto Malocello. Indigenous leaders called menceys ("men-SAYS") ruled independent territories on this archipelago's largest island. One theory for why these islands' indigenous population lacked seafaring ability is that (*) Juba II first populated these islands as a Numidian penal colony. These islands' native inhabitants, who disappeared after their conquest was completed by Alonso Fernandez de Lugo, were the Guanche people. This archipelago was Christopher Columbus's last stop in the Old World. For 10 points, name this archipelago that was conquered by Castile in the 15th century.
items.a: Canary Islands [or Islas Canarias]

items.q: Black specks characterize the PGI bananas grown on Fyffes plantations in this archipelago, whose port city of Arguineguin ("ar-GEEN-ee-GEEN") has become an ad hoc camp for migrants. Apollo 17 astronauts trained near the Fire Mountains in Timanfaya National Park in this archipelago, which is the most populous archipelago in Macaronesia ("mah-cah-ro-NEE-shuh"). In a 2019 Romanian film, mobsters travel to this archipelago to learn (*) "silbo," a whistle language used by its indigenous Guanche people. Half of this archipelago is governed by the province of Las Palmas. These islands south of the Madeira Islands were the last Old World stopping point on Columbus's voyages. For 10 points, Tenerife is part of what Spanish-controlled islands off the northwest African coast?
items.a: Canary Islands [or Islas Canarias; accept Canaries; prompt on Spain or the Atlantic before "Madeira Islands" is read]

items.q: During bajadas in this region, traditional stick fighting honors the Virgin of Candelaria, a Black Madonna venerated at a sanctuary in the Cave of San Blas. Uncooked onion scoops are used to eat purees of this region's toasted flour, gofio. In this region, people in El Hierro adopted the whistle language of Silbo created by shepherds in the mountains of La Gomera. This region's name derives from Roman observations of dog worship among its Guanche ("GWAHN-chay") people. A "mega-tsunami" theory centers on the collapse of this archipelago's Cumbre Vieja ("KOOM-bray vee-AY-hah") volcano on its island of La Palma. Tenerife is the largest island of, for 10 points, what Spanish archipelago off the coast of Morocco whose name identifies a certain species of yellow bird?
items.a: Canary Islands [or the Canaries or Las Canarias; accept Tenerife or La Gomera before read; prompt on Atlantic Ocean by asking "where?"]

items.q: The Valencian romance Tirant lo Blanc describes a king from this region named Abraham invading England and taking Kenilworth Castle. James III of Majorca sent multiple expeditions to this region, beginning a period of slave trading that was continued by Aragon. The Second Battle of Acentejo happened in this region, after which the mencey Bentor supposedly killed himself by falling down a hill. In what was unofficially known as the "tribute of blood", settlers known as islenos, who had largely replaced peoples like the (*) Guanche, were relocated to Spanish colonies in the 18th century. Horatio Nelson's right arm had to be amputated after his failed attempt to take the port of Santa Cruz de Tenerife in this archipelago. For 10 points, name this Spanish-owned archipelago off the coast of northwest Africa.
items.a: Canary Islands [accept Islas Canarias]

items.q: It's not the US or Iran, but in this country, unfabricated, threatening "night letters" were nailed to doors and posted on public buildings to threaten perceived traitors. The 2022 documentary Retrograde has come under heavy criticism for creating an unintentional "hit list" within this country due to its failure to blur faces. Citizens of the UK and this country were the main targets of Operation Pitting. Prior to its closure, the CARE Office provided support for the processing of SIVs for citizens of this country. Operation Allies Refuge occurred within this country, where dozens of C-17s airlifted out foreign collaborators like Dari interpreters and minesweepers, out of Hamid Karzai International Airport. For 10 points, the US evacuated what country's capital of Kabul in August 2021?
items.a: Afghanistan [or Islamic Republic of Afghanistan or Jamhuriye Islamiye Afghanistan]

items.q: The Carter administration pulled millions in aid to this country after US Ambassador Adolph Dubs was killed during a hostage rescue attempt. A conflict in this country was the origin of the term "Cargo 200" for flights in which soldiers were returned in zinc coffins. In 2004, this country adopted a new constitution at a loya jirga. A young refugee born in this country named Sharbat Gula gained global fame in a 1985 Steve McCurry cover photo for (*) National Geographic. Texas's Charlie Wilson helped get Stinger missiles delivered to this country's mujahideen in a conflict often dubbed the "Vietnam" of the Soviet Union. For 10 points, name this country invaded in 2001 by the US following the September 11 attacks.
items.a: Afghanistan [or Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan or Kingdom of Afghanistan or Republic of Afghanistan or People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan]

items.q: This country's monarchy was overthrown during the Coup of 26 Saratan with the aid of the Parchamis. The Unity Party, or Hezbe Wahdat, was formed as a merger between Iranian-funded factions from this country like the Tehran Eight. An invading force stormed this country's Tajbeg palace in Operation Storm-333. This country's (*) Barakzai dynasty, last led by Mohammad Daoud Khan, was deposed during the Saur Revolution. A conflict in this country led 66 countries to boycott the Moscow Summer Olympics. Operation Cyclone gave Stinger missiles to guerrillas in this country who forced a Soviet occupation to withdraw in 1989. For 10 points, name this country where some Mujahideen warlords went on to become leaders of the Taliban.
items.a: Afghanistan [accept the (Democratic) Republic of Afghanistan; accept the Kingdom of Afghanistan; accept the Islamic Emirate of Aghanistan]

items.q: In a novel set in this country, the jailer Atiq escorts a prostitute to her execution. That Yasmina Khadra novel is titled for The Swallows of [a city in this country]. The narrator of another novel from this country feels spring approaching after the orphan Sohrab gives off a lopsided smile. A servant from this country is told "For you, a (*) thousand times over!" after he is assaulted by the bully Assef. The Hazara boy Hassan performs the title action with Amir in that novel from this country. For 10 points, Khaled Hosseini's The Kite Runner depicts the rise of the Taliban in what country?
items.a: Afghanistan [or Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan] (the first two lines clue The Swallows of Kabul)

items.q: Mau Mau veteran Ian Henderson was called the "butcher of" this country due to his long career as its director of state security which included resisting a mid-1990s uprising that helped force the National Action Charter of 2001. An athlete from this country was arrested and tortured for allegedly throwing Molotov cocktails at a police station, despite literally playing in a televised soccer match at the same time. Hakeem al-Araibi was nearly deported to this country while vacationing in Thailand, despite having been granted asylum by Australia. This country also jailed Sayed Adnan, who missed a penalty against New Zealand that could have qualified it for the (*) 2010 World Cup. Sheikh Salman, a native of this country, had his campaign for FIFA president derailed by this country's "Bloody Thursday" crackdown on protestors in its Pearl Roundabout. For 10 points, name this island country ruled by the Khalifa family and connected by the King Fahd Causeway to Saudi Arabia, whose capital is Manama.
items.a: Bahrain [or Kingdom of Bahrain]

items.q: In December 2025, this country's space agency launched BlueBird Block-2, the heaviest foreign satellite ever launched from this country. One aerospace scientist from this country declared "very many individuals with myopic vision questioned the relevance of space activities", and later served as this country's president. In 2023, one spacecraft from this country became the first to land near the lunar south pole, that spacecraft's name translates as (*) "mooncraft three". In May 2025, this country's first human spaceflight program completed its final test and is named the Gaganyaan program. In September 2023, this country's first solar probe was launched from Sriharikota spaceport and was named Aditya-1. For 10 points, identify this country whose ISRO national space agency is responsible for the Chandrayaan program.
items.a: India [or Republic of India or Bharatiya Ganarajya, accept ISRO or Indian Space Research Organisation before mentioned]

items.q: A composer from this country named John Mayer founded a quintet partially named for this country with the saxophonist Joe Herriott. A pianist and a saxophonist from this country's diaspora collaborated on albums like Tragicomic and Architextures. A Handful of Beauty is a collaboration between an American guitarist and three musicians from this country's diaspora, one of whom invented the double violin. A cover of "Somewhere" from West Side Story is included on (*) Historicity, an album by a pianist from this country's diaspora. A singer from this country's diaspora included covers of "Fleurette Africaine" and Horace Silver's "Peace" on her album Day Breaks. A musician from this country collaborated with Yehudi Menuhin on the album West Meets East. For 10 points, name this country whose diaspora includes Norah Jones and her father, Ravi Shankar.
items.a: India [or Republic of India; or Bharat Ganarajya] (The unnamed pianist and saxophonist are Vijay Iyer and Rudresh Mahanthappa.)

items.q: The Palace of Assembly in this country features a hyperbolic tower designed by Iannis Xenakis. Buildings that comprise a Capitol Complex in this country were designed to reflect the "five points of architecture." Most of Edwin Lutyens' non-UK buildings are in this country, including a ceremonial arched war memorial called this country's namesake Gate. A series of Open Hand Monuments were built for a (*) planned city in this country whose design was based on the concept of a "Radiant City." Le Corbusier was commissioned to design a city in this country, where a white mausoleum is topped by an onion-shaped dome. For 10 points, name this country home to the Taj Mahal.
items.a: India [or Republic of India or Bharatiya Ganarajya]

items.q: One thinker from this country used a word that translates to "the uplift of all" in a translation of John Ruskin's Unto This Last. That man from this country also coined a term that is often translated as truth-force. The sixfold strategy is part of a political treatise composed by (*) Kautilya in what is now this country, where the term samsara influenced the writings of Arthur Schopenhauer. For 10 points, name this country where the sanskrit term Satyagraha was utilized by Mahatma Gandhi.
items.a: India [accept Bharat]

items.q: In a 1997 film, upside-down shots of this city appear as a character who works at a restaurant and tango bar mentions his homesickness. In a film set in this city, a man narrates that "the most intimate distance I had with her was 0.01 centimeters" over a freeze frame. At the end of a film, a character from this city whispers a secret into a hole at Angkor Wat. A policeman copes with his breakup by buying canned pineapples in a film from this city, which repeatedly features the song (*) "California Dreamin'." In a film, a man and a woman in this city often pass by each other in narrow apartment hallways as they realize their spouses are having an affair. For 10 points, Chunking Express and In the Mood For Love are set in what home city of director Wong Kar-Wai?
items.a: Hong Kong [or Xianggang; or Heunggong] (The lead-in is from Happy Together.)

items.q: In a film from this city, two neighbors in an apartment building bond after discovering their spouses are cheating with each other. This city is the birthplace of a comedic stunt actor who starred in The Drunken Master and Police Story. The protagonist of a film from this city appears in a yellow and black jumpsuit while fighting up the floors of a pagoda; that film, (*) Game of Death, stars an actor who created jeet kune do and starred in Enter the Dragon and Fist of Fury. For 10 points, Jackie Chan and Bruce Lee popularized martial arts films through the industry of what "special administrative region" of China?
items.a: Hong Kong [or Hong Kong Special Administrative Region or Heung Kong Takpit Hangching Ku]

items.q: In this city, stations named for Richard MacDonnell and Arthur Kennedy appear on a line transporting passengers to the scenic Lugard Road. A station serving Diamond Hill connects two of the ten lines on this city's public transport system, one of which terminates at a station named for Whampoa Garden. In this city, a gondola lift adorned with "crystal cabins" allows views of a bronze statue affectionately called "The (*) Big Buddha". The Central Elevated Walkway spans this city's thoroughfare ofConnaught Road. A unique fleet of double-decker trams can be found in this city, which is home to an outdoor escalator connecting its Mid-Levels to its 'Central' district. The Star Ferry carries passengers across this city's Victoria Harbour. For 10 points, name this Asian city whose Mass Transit Railway connects its namesake island to the Kowloon Peninsula.
items.a: Hong Kong [or HK] (The first line references the Peak Tram funicular.)

items.q: A film series about this city features the violent priest "Lethal Weapon" and a gang including "Smartie" and "Chicken." In the finale of a film set in this city, a man's son watches him barbarically kill a companion with a rock on a fishing trip. The series Young and Dangerous is set in this city. The Mexican standoff that ends a 1987 film whose title refers to this city as "on fire" was copied by Quentin Tarantino for Reservoir Dogs. In another film, a flashback to a religious blood oath for brotherhood sworn by a gang's kingpins contrasts with their war for a (*) baton to become their leader. Scriptural verses about "continuous hells" bookend a film set in this city in which a man says "I'm not afraid of light" while handcuffing his enemy at gunpoint on a rooftop. This city was replaced with Boston as the setting of that film's remake by Martin Scorsese, The Departed. For 10 points, Johnnie To's Election and Andrew Lau's Infernal Affairs trilogy are about what city's triads?
items.a: Hong Kong [or HK; or Hong Kong Special Administrative Region; or HKSAR] (The unnamed films are Johnnie To's Election and Ringo Lam's City on Fire.)

items.q: An average of 100 religious burials per day take place in this country's Valley of Peace. A religious group mostly found in this country uses phragmites ("frag-MY-teez") reeds to construct a building called a mudhif ("moo-deef"). A modern tradition in this country involves men wearing chains and whip handles around their necks as drums beat and celebrants symbolically (*) hurt themselves. The majority of Ahwaris or Marsh Arabs live in this country, where 25 million people travelled in 2023 for Arba'in. One city in this country is the burial site of Ali ibn Abi Talib. This country is home to the Shia pilgrimage cities of Najaf and Karbala. For 10 points, name this country whose religious minority of Sunni Kurds were persecuted by Saddam Hussein.
items.a: Iraq [or Republic of Iraq or Jumhuriyyat al-'Iraq]

items.q: This modern-day country contains the giant stone arch Taq Kasra near the riverside town of Salman Pak. This is the southernmost country the Great Zab river flows through as it passes near the Neanderthal site Shanidar Cave. This is the westernmost country in which mashoof canoes are used by Ahwaris or Marsh Arabs, who were targeted by this country's minority Sunni government in the 1990s. In this modern-day country, a river supposedly ran black with ink after a Mongol attack destroyed the "House of Wisdom." This country's city of Basra is located near the Shatt al-Arab's mouth on the Persian Gulf. For 10 points, the Tigris flows through what country's capital of Baghdad?
items.a: Iraq [or Republic of Iraq; or Jumhuriyyat-al-'Iraq]

items.q: The body of the former prime minister of this country was shown on live TV in a segment titled The End of the Criminals after the Ramadan Revolution. As part of the Al-Anfal campaign, this country carried out the Halabja massacre using chemical weapons. Soldiers from this country were bombed on the "Highway of Death" in Operation (*) Desert Storm during the First Gulf War. Weapons of mass destruction were used to justify this country's invasion by George W. Bush. For 10 points, name this country that Saddam Hussein led from Baghdad.
items.a: Iraq

items.q: In a 2007 Leor Halevi book, a city in this modern-day country was said to be "padlocking the women" in it by cracking down on wailing in funerals. Elizabeth Warnock Fernea published a 1965 ethnography of a village in this country, which is also the site of an event often commemorated by beating one's chest in the practice of matam. This country's "valley of peace" is often claimed to be the world's largest cemetery. An event that occurred in this country is recounted in (*) ta'ziyeh passion plays. The first hawza was founded in this modern-day country by Shaykh Tusi. The Arbaeen pilgrimage commemorates Husayn's death in this country and occurs 40 days after Ashura. For 10 points, the holy city of Najaf is located in what country where Shi'a rituals were banned by Saddam Hussein?
items.a: Iraq [or Republic of Iraq or Jumhuriyyat al-ʿIraq or Komari Eraq] (The Halevi book is Muhammad's Grave. Fernea's ethnography is Guests of the Sheik.)

items.q: The first president of Asia's Olympic Council died defending this country's Dasman Palace. April Glaspie is sometimes accused of tacitly approving an invasion of this country. Under the pseudonym "Nurse Nayirah," the daughter of a diplomat from this country falsely testified about babies thrown from (*) incubators. This country was accused of slant-drilling into a neighbor's Rumaila oil fields. Soldiers fled this country on the Highway of Death, which was bombed by Norman Schwarzkopf's forces during Operation Desert Storm. For 10 points, Iraq's invasion of what country provoked the Gulf War?
items.a: Kuwait [or State of Kuwait]

items.q: This country's government-in-exile indirectly hired PR firm Hill & Knowlton to raise American support for their restoration. A girl from this country testified before Congress about seeing babies ripped from incubators, but she was lying and was actually the daughter of this country's ambassador to the United States. Carl Sagan oddly predicted that scorched earth actions taken by retreating forces to ruin this country's economy would cause a nuclear winter; in reality, a 1.5-billion-dollar (*) firefighting effort stopped hundreds of blazes in the Burgan ("bur-GAHN") Field. This is the southernmost country where soldiers were bombed along the "Highway of Death." This country was liberated by the Norman Schwarzkopf-led Operation Desert Storm. For 10 points, name this country that Saddam Hussein invaded in the Gulf War.
items.a: Kuwait [or State of Kuwait or Dawlat al-Kuwayt]

items.q: The Oecobius (o-KO-bee-us) disc-web spider and the cerastes sand viper are endemic to this nation. Bubiyan and Al-Warbah are large but unpopulated islands off the coast of this country. The Al Rawdatayn well provides rare fresh water to this country, and its Al-Jahra Oasis provides its only permanent natural source of water. Another product is distributed by gravity aided by its Zawr Escarpment. This country deported 90% of its Palestinian population in the 1990s; the remainder of its foreigners live mostly in its capital's suburbs of Hawalli and Al-Shalimiyya (al-sha-li-MEE-ya). This nation's merchant class is the Banu Utub, whose chief member rules from Seif Palace. Water is distributed by a monument in which two obelisks pierce three blue tanks in the shape of spheres in this country's capital. An invasion of this country was halted at Khafji. For 10 points, name this nation on the Persian Gulf whose oilfields were set afire during an invasion by its northern neighbor, Iraq.
items.a: Kuwait

items.q: Tankers from this country used American flags while they were escorted by warships during Operation Earnest Will. After Operation Vantage, this country skirmished with its northern neighbor at the Sanita border post. This country's ruling al-Sabah family has denied citizenship to many stateless Bedoon people who once dominated its military. This country's Dasman Palace was raided during a conflict that began due to disputes over slant drilling by the INOC. Foreign invading forces in this country, which included the al-Medina and Hammurabi divisions, fired SCUD missiles at Israel and Saudi Arabia. In this country, vehicles were abandoned along the Highway of Death during a retreat from an American-led U.N. coalition. For 10 points, name this small country that was invaded by Iraq in 1990, triggering the Gulf War.
items.a: Kuwait [or State of Kuwait; or Dawlat al-Kuwayt] (The INOC is the Iraq National Oil Company.)

items.q: In this country's system of electoral symbols, the two typically largest parties use a sun and a tree, while another major party uses the jato grinder. The mayor of this country's largest city, a former rapper, displayed a map with a "Greater" version of this country with land it lost in the Treaty of Sugauli. A group called Hami participated in protests in this country against the (*) UML party. Protesters in this country used Discord to support a former Supreme Court justice after criticizing "nepo babies" in the prior leadership.
