Restrictions on social media led to protests that caused this country's Prime Minister Sharma Oli to resign. For 10 points, name this country where Gen Z protests led to a new government based in Kathmandu.
items.a: Nepal [or Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal or Sanghiya Lokatantrika Ganatantra Nepala]

items.q: 7. Protests in this country burned a Ministry of Health building designed by Louis Kahn and chased a finance minister into a river. It's not Indonesia, Madagascar, or the Philippines but protesters in this country flew the Straw Hat Pirates' flag from One Piece. The #NepoKid hashtag trended in this country, where Sushila Karki ("SOO-shill-uh KHAR-kee") was appointed as interim prime minister after a vote on (*) Discord. This country banned social media in 2025. For 10 points, name this Asian country where Gen Z protests racked its capital of Kathmandu.
items.a: Nepal [or Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal or Sanghiya Lokatantrika Ganatantra Nepala]

items.q: Soldiers from this modern-day country killed an officer who is celebrated by Ireland's only public Masonic monument, Rollo Gillespie. This country was analogized to "a yam between two boulders" in a "celestial counsel" written between 1774 and 1775 that also expressed one king's desire to make peace with the Malla kings. The 1846 Kot Massacre took place in this country, and was organized by a mukhtiyar who resumed the salt trade with its northern neighbor via the Treaty of Thapathali ("tah-PAH-tuh-lee"). Twenty-four petty kingdoms were subdued by a king from this country's Shah dynasty. It's not India, but the motto "Better to die than to be a coward" was used by an elite regiment made up of kukri-wielding soldiers from this country who have fought for the British since 1815. For 10 points, name this mountainous country home to the Gurkhas.
items.a: Nepal [or Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal; accept Kingdom of Nepal] (The second clue refers to the Divyopadesh by Prithvi Narayan Shah.)

items.q: This nation's Seke tongue is endangered due to emigration which is so geographically concentrated that fully one sixth of its speakers now live in a single apartment building in Ditmas Park in Brooklyn. This country is also the home of the Kaike people, who harvest a fungus which sprouts from mummified ghost-moth larvae, which is used as the performance-enhancing drug yarsagumba, grown in their native Tichurong Valley. The dzo-herding Walung people hosted a 1774 treaty which set one of its kingdom's boundaries at the (*) Kankai River, which that kingdom of Lembu then violated by invading Ilan. This country's Andha Galchi Gorge is a source of Shaligram shells which are gathered by its Thakali population for worship by devotees unable to make pilgrimages. Another gorge of religious significance in this country, the Chovar, was cut by a flaming sword to relieve its central valley of a serpent infested marsh which surrounded the thousand-petaled lotus Svayambhu. That lotus is central to the religion of a people for whom this country is named, which merged from tribes like the Licchavi, Malla and Kosala to form an empire native to the branching canyons of its Pahal region before being conquered by the Gurkhas. FTP, name this country which contains the birthplace of the Buddha at Lumbini, peaks like Makalu and Kanchenjunga, and its capital city of Kathmandu.
items.a: Nepal

items.q: A painter from this country known for her abstract hand-painted automobile exteriors, such as a Porsche 911 displayed at the Louvre, is currently being tried in France for human trafficking charges. A style of bright color, abstract wall painting traditionally done by women and named for a southwestern province of this country was inscribed as a form of intangible cultural heritage by UNESCO. An exhibition of women artists from this country called Soft Power was displayed at its first contemporary art museum, the Alaan Artspace. A 2011 installation of 200 fiberglass doves called Suspended Together criticized this country's use of (*) permission-to-travel documents. A 2023 art world controversy erupted over Pittsburgh's Andy Warhol Museum lending of artwork to this country, which has been accused of artwashing with its AlUla arts center. In 2017, a bidder from this country spent a record 450 million dollars to purchase Leonardo's Salvdor Mundi, supposedly at the behest of this country's crown prince. For 10 points, name this country where the super-tall buildings Center Point and the King's Road Towers stand respectively in Riyadh and Jeddah.
items.a: Saudi Arabia

items.q: In 2022, this country invested 2 billion dollars into the private equity firm Affinity Partners. This country is constructing the Trojena ski resort to host the 2029 Asian Winter Games. Several WWE superstars were trapped in this country in 2019 over a possible payment dispute after the Crown Jewel show. A company owned by this country will jointly form the tentatively named "NewCo" after agreeing to a merger of an organization led by Jay Monahan. This country's Vision 2030 program seeks to grow its sovereign wealth fund to two trillion dollars and diversify away from dependence on its state owned company Aramco. For 10 points, name this country whose sovereign wealth fund has bought Newcastle United and sponsored the LIV Golf tour as part of the economic goals of its Crown Prince Mohamad Bin Salman.
items.a: Saudi Arabia [or Kingdom of Saudi Arabia or KSA or Al-Mamlakah al-ʿArabiyah as-Suʿudiyah]

items.q: A leader of this country is served by the Tiger Squad and may have forced Saad Hariri to resign as Lebanese Prime Minister in 2017. This country's "Vision 2030" plan includes the construction of a carbon-neutral, 110-mile-long city called The Line. This country's Operation Decisive Storm emerged from its role leading the anti-Houthi coalition in (*) Yemen. In 2018, women in this country gained the right to drive. The 2018 murder of vocal critic Jamal Khashoggi was ordered by this country's Crown Prince Mohammad bin Salman. For 10 points, name this authoritarian Middle Eastern country whose capital is Riyadh.
items.a: Saudi Arabia [prompt on Arabia; prompt on Saudi Vision 2030]

items.q: This country's government planned the construction of the Trojena mountain resort and a 170 kilometer long linear city in its Neom project. Members of this country's Tiger Squad potentially carried out the assassination of dissident journalist Jamal Khashoggi. The initial public offering of (*) Aramco, this country's national oil company, was proclaimed by its crown prince, Mohamed bin Salman. For 10 points, name this oil-rich country governed from Riyadh.
items.a: Saudi Arabia

items.q: In this modern-day country, the Zengid emir Nur ad-Din founded an early hospital named for himself. Ibn Battuta claimed the "greatest mosque on earth" was one in this country, where columns from a Temple of Jupiter were used to support the Dome of the Treasury. This country's Masyaf Castle is where the "Old Man of the Mountain" commanded the Assassins. Al-Walid I constructed a mosque in this country, which contains (*) John the Baptist's head. The Crusader Krak des Chevaliers castle in this country was shelled during the 2013 Siege of Homs. A city in this country names a type of wootz steel with teardrop patterns and was the seat of the Umayyads. For 10 points, name this country that contains Aleppo and Damascus.
items.a: Syria [or the Syrian Arab Republic]

items.q: A religious group whose largest population is in this country believes in a fixed number of souls that are reincarnated through the process of taqammus. Another religious group that mostly lives in this country prefers using a name coined by Ibn Nusayr instead of the term Nusyari. Conversion to a faith predominantly residing in this country has not been permitted since 1043. This country has the largest population of a faith that reads the Epistles of Wisdom, reveres the caliph Al-Hakim as an incarnation of God, and uses the symbol of a (*) five-coloured star. Members of a non-Islamic faith that venerates Ali have chiefly served in a civil war on behalf of this country's former Baathist regime. For 10 points, name this country with the largest populations of the Druze and Alawite faiths, the latter followed by the al-Assad family.
items.a: Syria [or the Syrian Arab Republic]

items.q: A volunteer group called this country's "Civil Defense" was the subject of the first Netflix-distributed film to win an Oscar, 2016's The White Helmets. The creation of the amphetamine Captagon funded the government of this country, where 2025 fires hit its Latakia region. Former High Negotiations Committee member Hind Kabawat serves in this country's government, hoping to quell tensions with the Druze and the once-favored Alawites. HTS rebels in this country's Idlib region were led by Ahmed al-Sharaa, who now heads the government after a former ophthalmologist's late 2024 overthrow. For 10 points, Bashar Al-Assad once ruled what country from Damascus?
items.a: Syria [or Syrian Arab Republic or al-Jumhuriyyah al-ʿArabiyyah as-Suriyyah; accept Syria Civil Defense]

items.q: During a 2025 meeting, this country's de facto leader refused to shake the hand of German Foreign Minister Annalena Baerbock. Despite the appointment of a woman to lead this country's central bank, Obaida Arnaout issued several contradictory statements on women's rights. A shock military offensive in this country beginning in the Idlib Governorate was led by (*) HTS. One leader fled this country for Russia after the fall of Homs. After winning a civil war in this country, a leader who dropped the alias "Al-Jolani" created a transitional government. For 10 points, name this country that was led by Bashar Al-Assad until 2024.
items.a: Syria

items.q: To regulate water use, a kingdom based in this region constructed five wewas for an artificial "sea" dated to the 4th century CE. This region's holiday of Poson commemorates a meeting between King Tissa and Mahinda. The first kingdom of an ethnic group from this region was named for the copper sand that stained its founder's hands upon his arrival; that founder was Prince (*) Vijaya. Attendees of a non-Sarvastivada "Fourth Council" held in this region transcribed the Tripitaka onto palm leaves. Per the Mahavamsa, this region was home to a mythical fort ruled by the demon king Ravana. This region's Kingdom of Anuradhapura fell following invasions by the Chola Empire to the north. For 10 points, name this Buddhist-majority island country primarily inhabited by the Sinhalese.
items.a: Sri Lanka [or Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka or Sri Lanka Prajatantrika Samajavadi Janarajaya or Ilangai Jananayaka Sosalisak Kudiyarasu; accept Lanka; accept Ceylon] (The unmentioned kingdoms in the first and third lines are the Kingdoms of Polonnaruwa and Tambapanni.)

items.q: The SS Oronsay leaves this country for England in the novel The Cat's Table by an author [emphasise] born in this country. That author wrote about their father Mervyn's time as a soldier in this country in the memoir Running in the Family. Wisden chose "the greatest cricket novel of all time" from this country, which ends with Garfield finding the bowler Pradeep Mathew. A novel from this country originally titled Chats with the Dead features Helpers who guide spirits towards "the Light". During the titular (*) week of afterlife, a character from this country enlists the Crow Man to help him contact Jaki from beyond the grave. That photographer, Maali Almeida, later relates an attack he witnessed on Jaffna during this country's civil war. For 10 points, name this country, the birthplace of authors Shehan Karunatilaka ("KAH-roo-nah-tee-LAH-kuh") and Michael Ondaatje ("on-DAH-chuh").
items.a: Sri Lanka [prompt on Ceylon]

items.q: A festival in this country begins after sandalwood-scented water is sprinkled over a newly planted jackfruit tree. An 1885 committee named for this country's largest city produced the five-colored International Buddhist Flag with the help of Henry Steel Olcott. In a rainmaking festival from this country, acrobats and fire jugglers accompany an elephant procession while paying homage to an object that was hidden within a princess's hair. A meeting between King Tissa and Prince Mahinda on Mount Mihintale introduced this country to Buddhism. Many Buddhists claim that the Buddha's footprint is imprinted on Adam's Peak while his left canine tooth is held within a temple in this country's city of Kandy. For 10 points, the 1885 Colombo Committee was held in what island nation?
items.a: Sri Lanka [accept Democratic Socialist Republic of Sri Lanka; accept Sri Lanka Prajatantrika Samajavadi Janarajaya or Ilankai Cananayaka Cocalicak Kutiyaracu]

items.q: This country's Freedom Party and LSSP backed a prime minister who was the subject of a 1962 coup by F. C. de Saram. That politician from this country, married to the "Silver Bell," was a party leader during 1983 pogroms called Black July. A 1971 JVP-led insurrection against a female prime minister of this country led one group to attack the Temple of the Tooth. This country was the first to elect a female prime minister, Sirimavo Bandaranaike. This country tried ending a civil war against the LTTE, who fought to create a state partly named Eelam. The Rajapaksa ("RAH-juh-puck-shuh") family has led politics in this island country. For 10 points, name this Asian country where Sinhalese forces fought the Tamil Tigers.
items.a: Sri Lanka [or Ceylon; or Ilankai or Illangai]

items.q: Archaeologists in this country hope to find all fifty of the "Elliq-Qala," or "Fifty Forts," including castles at Guldursun and Toprak. Toxic dust storms cause chronic illnesses in this country's depopulated city of Moynaq, home to a "cemetery of boats." Most of the Karakalpak people live in this country around a river delta home to the cities of Nukus and Urgench. This country's main ethnic group speaks the second most widely-spoken Turkic language, which is closely related to Uighur. The city of Andijan lies in this country's section of the Ferghana Valley. Before the effects of irrigation for cotton growing, the Amu Darya met the Aral Sea in this country. For 10 points, what most populous country in Central Asia contains cities like Samarkand and Tashkent?
items.a: Uzbekistan [or Republic of Uzbekistan; or O'zbekiston Respublikasi]

items.q: A group of aristocratic intellectuals called the jadids pushed for modernization in this country, and one Islamist movement in this country was founded by a former math teacher. That movement was attacked in the (*) Andijan Massacre. This country's language is a modernized form of Chagatay Turkish, and this country faces a separatist movement led by the Karakalpaks. This country is the home of the Tughril Beg Madrasa. It's not India, but one insect-infested jail cell in this country's city of Bukhara was known as its "black hole". The daughter of this country's first post-independence leader, Gulnara Karimova, has been missing for years. For ten points, name this Central Asian country with capital Tashkent.
items.a: Uzbekistan

items.q: A defunct oppositon group in this country was the Forum of Democratic Forces led by Shukrullo Mirsaidov. At this country's Jaslyk Prison, Muzafar Avazov was killed by being dropped into boiling water. The British ambassador Craig Murray was recalled from this country after becoming increasingly outspoken about Western complicity in torture here. In one event in this country, Chulpon Avenue was closed and hundred of people in (*) Bobur Square were killed in a protest blamed on the Islamic group Akramia. This location of the Andijan massacre has the longest-serving post-independence president of any former Soviet republic. For 10 points, name this Central Asian state ruled since 1989 by Islam Karimov.
items.a: Uzbekistan

items.q: This country's capital is home to a green domed market called the Chorsu Bazaar. One of its traditional foods is a lamb and rice dish called plov. One of the world's largest gold mines is located in the north of this country at Muruntau in the Kyzl Kum Desert. Many members of its Karakalpak ethnic group have been emigrating from the nominally autonomous region in this country's west to its northern neighbor. A fortress called The Ark and the great Kaylan minaret can be found in its city Bukhara. This country contains the mouth of the Amu Darya River and the majority of the Fergana valley. The site of the historic city of Samarkand, it shares the shrinking Aral Sea with its northern neighbor Kazakhstan. For 10 points, name this Asian country with capital Tashkent.
items.a: Uzbekistan

items.q: A 1971 Sorcery Act passed by this nation's parliament banned black magic, with over a hundred men and women dying annually from accusations of witchcraft. A type of encephalopathy named kuru is common among the Fore [["foray"]] tribe of this nation due to their practice of funerary cannibalism. This Asian nation, which uses the creole "Tok Pisin," was once split into German and British dominated spheres. For the point, name this nation once administered by its neighbor across the Torres Strait, Australia.
items.a: Papua New Guinea (or Papuaniugini; prompt on "Papua"; do not accept or prompt on "New Guinea" or "Guinea")

items.q: This country's "highlands highway" supplies coffee and gold to its most important port. The river basin of this country's longest river contains the April Salumei Rainforest, which is a pilot project of the UN's R-E-D-D scheme. The largest river in the world without a dam in its catchment is this country's Fly River, although that river was polluted by the collapse of a tailings dam in 1984 at the (*) Ok Tedi mine. One eruption in 1937 prompted the colonial administration to move to this country's city of Lae, the last place Amelia Earhart was seen alive. A major 1994 eruption caused the evacuation of a former provincial capital in this country, when both Vulcan and Tavurvur erupted. That eruption destroyed the city of Rabaul on this country's island of New Britain. For 10 points, name this island country with capital Port Moresby, which shares half of its namesake island with Indonesia.
items.a: Papua New Guinea

items.q: This country's efforts to join ASEAN have been hampered by its recent history of anti-Chinese riots, such as those that devastated warehouses in its city of Mount Hagen. Featuring on its flag and national emblem is this country's national bird, the Raggiana bird-of-paradise. Many of this country's Fore people formerly suffered from the neurodegenerative disease (*) kuru, which likely spread when villagers ate a man's brain. This country borders a province formerly known as Irian Jaya to its west. Though most of this country's residents speak English, they more commonly use a pidgin language called Tok Pisin, which contains many Melanesian words. For 10 points, name this country that shares its namesake island with Indonesia with its capital at Port Moresby ("MORZ-bee").
items.a: Papua New Guinea [or Papua Niugini or Independent State of Papua New Guinea; do not accept or prompt on "New Guinea"]

items.q: The first word in this country's name comes from a term used to describe hair meaning "frizzled." The most widely used language in this country is the English-based creole Tok Pisin. This country's flag, which is divided diagonally into black and red halves, includes the Southern Cross and a yellow bird. Natives of an archipelago that currently belongs to this country were the subject of Malinowski's book Argonauts of the Western Pacific. This country owns the eastern half of its namesake island, the western half of which belongs to Indonesia. For 10 points, name this country with capital at Port Moresby.
items.a: Papua New Guinea [or PNG; or Papua Niugini; do NOT accept just "New Guinea"]

items.q: A group of airlines in this country was inspired by the Berlin airlift to create the world's first air shuttle service. Mexican aviator Ralph O'Neill founded Panair, which was this country's largest airline until it was abruptly shut down by the government in 1965. In the 1930s, flights from Germany on the Graf Zeppelin primarily went to this country. An airship designer from this country won the Deutsch prize of 100,000 francs by flying around the (*) Eiffel Tower. In this country, it is widely taught that that inventor conducted the first airplane flight and not the Wright brothers. This country's air force commissioned the EMB-110, which was the first airplane built by what is now the third-largest aircraft manufacturer in the world. For 10 points, name this native country of aviation pioneer Alberto Santos-Dumont and manufacturer Embraer.
items.a: Brazil [or Federative Republic of Brazil or Republica Federativa do Brasil]

items.q: One ethnography of this country said mothers would not raise children who lacked a knack for life and recorded everyday violence in this country. A thinker from this country analyzed how different areas handled miscegenation in The Mansions and The Shanties. Nancy Scheper-Hughes's book Death without Weeping is about this country, which is home to a thinker who wrote about racial democracy in The Masters and the Slaves. Another theorist from this country criticized the banking model of education in (*) The Pedagogy of the Oppressed. Daniel Everett claimed that a language from this country lacked recursion, and Claude Levi-Strauss chronicled peoples of this country in Tristes Tropiques ("treest TROH-peek"). For 10 points, name this country home to the Piraha and Yanomami in the Amazon rainforest.
items.a: Brazil [or Brasil] (The Mansions and the Shanties and The Masters and the Slaves are by Gilberto Freyre.)

items.q: A house named for this country in Accra's Jamestown district was built by Mama Nassau. People who migrated from this country built the Ilojo Bar building and are called Tabom or Tabon in Ghana. The Popo Aguda of Lagos Island is a quarter named for people from this country, much of whose Yoruba population moved to Nigeria after the (*) Male Revolt. Orixa worship is a major component of this country's Umbanda religion. Slaves in this country developed the martial art of capoeira ("kah-poo-EY-ruh") and escaped to quilombo settlements. The Golden Law abolished slavery in this home country of Candomble under Isabel, the regent of its emperor Pedro II. For 10 points, the last country in the Americas to abolish slavery was what country that includes Rio de Janeiro?
items.a: Brazil [or Brasil]

items.q: A 60-million-dollar painting from this country depicting a group of beavers beneath a sunset was discovered hidden under a bed after it was stolen from an elderly widow by a fake psychic. A painting from this country depicts a purple tentacle wrapped around a red thorn and an egg. This country's "Group of the Five" included an artist whose painting depicting a toad, caterpillar, bird, and forest spirit was once covered in imitation snakeskin by Pierre Legrain. A student of Fernand Leger ("lay-ZHAY") from this country, who painted The Egg and A Cuca, helped found a group that organized the landmark Modern Art Week. A painting from this country's modernist movement depicts an orange figure with an enormous foot beside a cactus. For 10 points, name this home country of Tarsila do Amaral ("tar-SEE-la doo ah-ma-RALL"), whose work inspired Oswald de Andrade's ("OHZ-vald jee ahn-DRAH-jee's")Cannibal Manifesto.
items.a: Brazil [or Brasil; or Federative Republic of Brazil or Republica Federativa do Brasil] (The first sentence refers to the theft and recovery of Tarsila's painting Setting Sun.)

items.q: It's not Venezuela, but a phase of a war in this country was called a "War to the Death" for the ruthless violence that occurred in the La Frontera region. Mariano de Osorio aided the colonial "reconquista" of this country for Spain following the Royalist victory at the Disaster of Rancagua. That result led to the dismantling of this country's First Junta ("hun-tuh") and the end of its "Old Fatherland" period. In 1820, this country parlayed victories at Chacabuco and Maipu into a campaign that resulted in the annexation of Osorno and (*) Valdivia. This country, whose independence was secured by Bernardo O'Higgins, obtained nitrate reserves from Peru and Bolivia in the War of the Pacific. For 10 points, what country's navy and army are respectively headquartered in Valparaiso and Santiago?
items.a: Chile [or Republic of Chile or Republica de Chile]

items.q: Musicians from this country often performed under a banner reading "There is no revolution without songs." The untitled final song attributed to a musician from this country laments, "How hard it is to sing / when I must sing of horror / Horror which I am living, horror which I am dying." The singer of "Gracias a la Vida" pioneered this country's namesake variant of nueva cancion. A song by this country's folk band Quilapayun ("kee-la-pa-YOON") inspired a massive set of variations by Frederic Rzewski ("ZHEFF-skee") on the song "The People United Will Never Be Defeated." A musician from this country composed songs like "Te recuerdo Amanda" before being tortured and killed in a soccer stadium. For 10 points, Violeta Parra and Victor Jara ("HA-ra") were from what South American country whose jazz guachaca style incorporates influences from its eastern neighbor's tangos?
items.a: Chile [or Republic of Chile or Republica de Chile]

items.q: In this country, a computerized economic planning system called Project Cybersyn was developed. In Operation Colombo, this country's DINA secret police disappeared many dissidents. Singer Victor Jara was tortured and murdered in a sports stadium following a coup in this country. After giving a radio speech in this country, a leader was found dead holding an AK-47 in (*) La Moneda Palace. Milton Friedman educated a group of economic advisors in this country dubbed the "Chicago Boys." A 1973 coup in this country overthrew Salvador Allende. For 10 points, name this country formerly led by Augusto Pinochet.
items.a: Chile [or the Republic of Chile or Republica de Chile]

items.q: 12. A leader of this country was defeated by Mariano Osorio at Rancagua ("ran-KAH-wa"). The Carrera family led this country during the Patria Vieja ("PAH-tree-uh vee-AY-haa"). After independence, this country was led by a Supreme Director who previously joined the Lautaro ("low-TAR-oh") Lodge and helped win the Battle of Chacabuco ("CHAK-uh-BOO-koh"), named (*) Bernardo O'Higgins. This country was Britain's main source of sodium nitrate, or saltpeter. This is the westernmost of two countries home to the Mapuche ("muh-POO-chay"). For 10 points, name this South American country with capital at Santiago.
items.a: Chile [or Republic of Chile or Republica de Chile]

items.q: In 1987, two earthquakes struck on the same day in this country's Coca Valley, now home to the sinkhole-plagued Coca Codo Sinclair Dam. The ancient Canari city of Tumebamba in this modern-day country sat at the confluence of four rivers and is mostly buried under its city of Cuenca. This country's most populous city is on the west bank of the largest Pacific-discharging river in South America. Tourists can head to the Teleferico district in this country's capital to take a gondola up the (*) Pichincha Volcano. Another volcano in this country is home to the farthest point from the Earth's center and can be seen from Guayaquil. For 10 points, name this country home to Cotopaxi and Chimborazo, whose capital is Quito.
items.a: Ecuador [or Republic of Ecuador]

items.q: A volcano in this country repeatedly destroyed the city of Latacunga ("lah-tah-KOON-gah") and was depicted erupting in an 1862 painting by Frederic Edwin Church. An archipelago controlled by this country is home to marine iguanas, the now-deceased tortoise Lonesome George, and (*) Darwin's finches. This country contains the farthest point from Earth's center, Mount Chimborazo ("chim-boh-RAH-zoh"). The Galapagos islands are part of, for 10 points, what South American country with capital Quito ("KEE-toh")?
items.a: Ecuador [or Republic of Ecuador]

items.q: In this modern-day country, Stephen Rosain used LIDAR to uncover the cities of Kilamope and Sangay in its Upano Valley. Betty Meggers controversially argued that Jomon fishermen influenced the pottery of this country's Valdivia culture. A pair of skeletons known as the Amantes de Sumpa were found buried together in a cemetery belonging to this country's Las Vegas culture. The general Ruminahui burned a city in this modern-day country after losing to Sebastian de Belalcazar in a battle that ended with the (*) eruption of a nearby volcano. Huayna Capac's heart was buried in a city in this modern-day country, which he established as a second Incan capital. Legendarily, two members of this country's Huancavilca people that committed suicide after being captured name its second-largest city. For 10 points, name this country whose capital was named after the Quitu people.
items.a: Ecuador [or Republic of Ecuador]

items.q: A recent president of this country has used a wheelchair since being injured in a robbery of a bakery in 1998. Another former president of this country is currently in exile in Belgium after he was charged with having a rival kidnapped; during that man's presidency, he relied on Chinese financing for $3.7 billion in building eight new hydroelectric dams through the firm Sinohydro. One president of this country deliberately underinvested in its (*) oil sites as part of a campaign to force an oil company to pay $10 billion in environmental cleanup. 30,000 residents of this country suffered birth defects due to Chevron dumping oil into the Amazon. In April 2019, police entered this country's embassy in London to arrest longtime asylum-seeker Julian Assange. For 10 points, name this country once ruled by Rafael Correa and Lenin Moreno, whose current president is Guillermo Lasso.
items.a: Ecuador

items.q: This country began an offensive by capturing Fort Boqueron. In a speech on the Senate floor, Huey Long supported the war effort of this country and accused Standard Oil of backing its northwestern neighbor. Lino Oviedo allegedly threatened General Andres Rodriguez with a grenade to convince him to lead a coup in this country. A department in this country is named for Rutherford B. Hayes because he arbitrated a border dispute in this country's favor. For 35 years, this country was under the dictatorship of Colorado Party leader Alfredo Stroessner, who was of partial Guarani descent. This country fought a war with Bolivia over the supposedly oil-rich Gran Chaco. For 10 points, name this South American country whose party feuds intensified after its loss in the War of the Triple Alliance.
items.a: Paraguay [or Republic of Paraguay; or Republica del Paraguay]

items.q: This country promoted George Thompson to be its chief military engineer while he oversaw a fortress nicknamed its "Gibraltar." This country annually celebrates 3000 soldiers who died at Acosta Nu ("a-cost-uh" NEW). Eliza Lynch was a mistress to a ruler of this country who lost the fort of Humaita ("oo-my-TAH"). This country's indigenous (*) Guarani ("gwah-ruh-NEE") people served as spies in a conflict where its leader died at the battle of Cerro Cora. This country ceded Mato Grossoafter a war where many thousands died as child soldiers. Francisco Solano Lopez ruled, For 10 points, what nation that fought Argentina, Brazil, and Uruguay in the War of the Triple Alliance?
items.a: Paraguay [or Republic of Paraguay or Republica del Paraguay]

items.q: An author from this country wrote about the government doorman turned jewel thief Espinoza, the country lawyer turned drunk and gambler Ramon, and the malicious gossip-monger Dona Angela in the social realist novel The Slug. The elite but cowardly Miguel Vera and the Christlike peasant Cristobal Jara are contrasted in a 1960 novel from this country called Son of Man. In another novel from this home country of Gabriel Casaccia, a forged declaration nailed to the door of a cathedral demands that the head of a leader be removed from his corpse and placed on a pike in the public square. A historical woman's experience in this non-European country features in an (*) Anne Enright novel titled for that woman's "pleasure." The amanuensis Policarpo Patino edits and comments on the declarations of the title figure in a novel from this country. An author born in and exiled from this country, Augusto Roa Bastos, wrote that classic dictator novel I, the Supreme. For 10 points, authors from what South American country often reflected on the legacies of Francisco Solano Lopez and Alfredo Stroessner?
items.a: Paraguay

items.q: A leader of this country had all bushes on his riding routes uprooted out of fear of assassins and insisted that executions be held under an orange tree outside his house. Secret police in this country brought prisoners to the "chamber of truth", while other prisoners could be sent to the penal colony of Tevego. Rousseau's Social Contract inspired an isolationist leader of this country who employed a secret police called the "Harry Feet" and essentially required (*) interracial marriage by banning people of Spanish heritage from marrying each other. The Irish woman Eliza Lynch shacked up with a leader of this country, who cried "I die with my nation" at the Battle of Cerro Cora. This country's first leader upon independence was Jose Rodriguez de Francia, or "El Supremo". For 10 points, name this country that was led into a disastrous war with three neighbors by Francisco Solano Lopez.
items.a: Paraguay
items.s: 2024 History of the World Part II

items.q: Certain villages in this non-French speaking nation may participate in direct democracies known as krutu, which take the place of councils like the lo lanti under urgent situations. Those councils are found in native capitals like Langatabiki and Witagron, home to the Matawai and Kwinti, who are primarily of African descent. Another African people group in this nation once dwelled in the former plantation Klaverblad, but were evicted with the discovery of bauxite. Native peoples like the Tiriyo and Wayana often do not recognize village hierarchies, but had leaders called (*) Granman appointed for them in the 20th Century. The Eilerts de Haan Mountains are a protected portion of this nation's principal mountain range, which also includes the large granite dome, the Voltzberg, found above the Raleigh Falls on the Coppename River. This country's religious architecture includes the largest wooden church in the western hemisphere, as well as the Neveh Shalom Synagogue, which sits across Keizer Street from its largest mosque, and a Hindu temple which caters to its large Javanese population. Creoles like Taki-Taki are used to communicate between this nation's diverse ethnicities. A portion of this country southwest of the Corentyne River is the source of a border discrepancy with its western neighbor. FTP, name this Dutch-speaking South American nation with capital Paramaribo.
items.a: Suriname

items.q: An important mining region in this country was found in Operation Grasshopper, a 1959 effort to find natural resources from the air led by Frank Essed. For a year and a half, both the offices of president and prime minister of this country were held on behalf of a military dictator by Henk Chin A Sen. The Moiwana Massacre was an attack on the hometown of a former bodyguard of one of this country's leaders after they formed the guerilla group Jungle Commando. The non-American (*) Henck Arron was deposed first as Prime Minister, then as Vice President, in two separate coups in this country that installed the same military officer as the de facto leader. The December Murders were carried out at a non-Taiwanese Fort Zeelandia to eliminate fifteen political opponents of Desi Bouterse ("BOW-ter-suh"). For 10 points, name this South American country that gained full independence from the Netherlands in 1975.
items.a: Suriname [or Republic of Suriname, Republiek Suriname, Ripoliku Sranan]

items.q: This nation's districts are called ressorten , and they include Livorno and Centrum. The Johan Adolf Pengel International and Zong en Hoop airports are in this nation, which is the headquarters of Caricom Airlines and Gum Air. The Jules Wijdenbosch Bridge is also in this nation. The English-based creole (*) Sranan Tongo is a lingua franca used in this country home to Juliana Top. Brazil is bordered to the south and Guyana is bordered to the west by, for ten points, what nation with a Dutch-language majority which has capital at Paramaribo?
items.a: Suriname

items.q: The most significant primary source related to this country's colonial history relates how its author married the slave woman Johanna and saw a rebel hanged by his ribs. That source was written by the Scottish mercenary John Gabriel Stedman. Stedman's account also provides the first speech sample from this country's Saramaccan language, which developed from English after a colony led by Hugh (*) Willoughby failed, leading Willoughby's slaves to escape into this country's jungles. This country's Muslim population is primarily descended from Javanese indentured laborers, and this country was traded for possession of New York in the Treaty of Breda in 1667. For 10 points, name this South American country with its capital at Paramaribo.
items.a: Suriname

items.q: This country became the first to legalize marijuana in 2013. By duration, this country has the longest national anthem of any country on Earth. A sculpture of fingers jutting from the sand can be found in this country's resort town of Punta del Este. This country's Estadio Centenario hosted the first FIFA World Cup in history, which this country won. This "Oriental Republic" is separated by the widest river in the world from from a neighbor's capital of (*) Buenos Aires. For 10 points, name this South American country whose capital of Montevideo is seperated by the Rio de la Plata from Argentina.
items.a: Uruguay [or Oriental Republic of Uruguay or Republica Oriental del Uruguay]

items.q: In this country, a national holiday on May 18th celebrates the Battle of Las Piedras, where Jose Artigas commanded troops fighting for its independence. The words "LIBERTY OR DEATH" appear on a flag flown by this country's Thirty-Three Orientals. The nickname (*) "Hero of Two Worlds" was given to Giuseppe Garibaldi for fighting in this country's civil war. Argentina and Brazil formed the "triple alliance" with this country that became independent from Brazil in the 1820s. For 10 points, what nation is led from Montevideo?
items.a: Uruguay [accept Oriental Republic of Uruguay or Republica Oriental de Uruguay; accept Eastern Republic of Uruguay]

items.q: Mauricio Rosencof and Eluterio Fernandez Huidoboro were among nine prisoners kept in squalid conditions in this country as depicted in the film A Twelve-Year Night. Dan Mitrione, an American official, was kidnapped and executed in this country where he had been supporting government forces in defeating the left-wing Frente Amplio. Raul Sendic led communist revolutionaries known as the (*) Tupamaros in this country; this country's former president Jose Mujica used to be a Tupamaro. Roberto Canessa ran to be President of this country after surviving the crash of one of its Air Force flights in the Andes as depicted in the film Alive. For 10 points, name this South American country whose civic-military dictatorship sent many political prisoners south across the Rio de la Plata to be killed in neighbouring Argentina.
items.a: Uruguay

items.q: British forces under Samuel Auchmuty captured the capital of this modern-day country in 1807.After the first naval battle of WWII, the Admiral Graf Spee sheltered in the port of this country's capital. This country was briefly known as the Cisplatine Province until an insurrection led by the Thirty-Three Orientals. The Italian Legion was raised in this country by the "Hero of Two Worlds," who fought in this country's civil war with the Colorados against the Blancos. For the point, name this country whose capital lies on the Rio de La Plata at Montevideo.
items.a: Uruguay

items.q: This present-day country's site of Idehd ("ih-dead") contains a midden of turtle shells, which were offered by priests to a great eel. A city in this country was conquered by a hero born to the thunder god Nan Sapwe ("nahn sahp-way"), named Isokelekel ("ee-soh-keh-leh-kel"), and was built as an altar to the god of agriculture by two sorcerers named Olosohpa ("oh-loh-soh-pah") and Olosihpa ("oh-loh-sih-pah"). By tradition, the man Anagumang ("ah-nah-goo-mahng") taught people in this country to use quarried rock from foreign lands to make large wheel-shaped objects. The Saudeleur ("saw-deh-lur") dynasty ruled a city in this country which was linked by canals built atop that city's central lagoon. Another group in this country created rai, large stones used as money. It contains the site of Nan Madol, known as the "Venice of the Pacific." For 10 points, name this country which contains the islands of Yap, Pohnpei, and Chuuk and whose capital is Palikir.
items.a: Federated States of Micronesia [or FSM]

items.q: A state in this modern country was supposedly founded by the twin sorcerers Olisihpa and Olosohpa who built an altar to the agriculture god Nahnisohn Sahpw with the help of a dragon. That state in this modern country was ruled from the city Nan Madol. The island of Kosrae ("coe-SHY") in this country contains the ruins of the city of Leluh and may have been the place from where Isokelekel launched his successful invasion of Pohnpei to overthrow the Saudeleur Dynasty. Truk Lagoon in this modern country was one of Japan's most important naval bases in WWII, and after the war, this country, along with (*) Palau and the Marshall Islands, was administered by the US until declaring independence in 1979. For 10 points, what is this modern country, which shares its name with a region of the Pacific north of Melanesia?
items.a: Federated States of Micronesia

items.q: Lissant Bolton wrote about how in the 1990s, a belief system in this country expanded to include women's knowledge in the book Unfolding the Moon. A female deity from this country called Le-Hev-Hev guards the underworld and erases half of a maze drawn in the sand as a soul approaches, requiring the soul to redraw the other half. A movement in this country splintered and devolved into armed conflict in 2004 because of the actions of a Christian separatist named Prophet Fred. A leader in this country named Jimmy Stevens claimed to be Moses while leading the separatist (*) Nagriamel movement. A type of magic practiced in several traditions in this country is called kastom. The Anglican preacher Father Walter Lini was the first Prime Minister of this country. A group in this country flew the Union Jack at half-mast outside a nakamal after the 2021 death of a foreign royal they venerated. For 10 points, name this Pacific nation home to the Prince Philip and John Frum cargo cults.
items.a: Vanuatu

items.q: In this country, divers can view a porcelain statue of a woman riding a unicorn called "The Lady" by diving into the wreck of the SS President Coolidge. This country's national dish, which consists of a paste of taro, yam, banana, and breadfruit baked in banana leaves, is known as lap-lap. A tomb on this country's island of Eretoka features a UNESCO World Heritage Site centered around the burial ground of chief Roi Mata. Jimmy Stevens led this country's Nagriamel movement which fought the (*) Coconut War in an attempt to win independence for its largest island, Espiritu Santo. The tradition of gol, or land diving, is practiced on this country's island of Pentecost. This country's Tanna Island is home to cargo cults that worship Prince Phillip and a US serviceman known as John Frum. For 10 points, name this Pacific Island country whose capital is Port Vila.
items.a: Vanuatu [or New Hebrides]

items.q: In 1980, Jimmy Stevens, head of this nation's Nagriamel movement, declared the independence of Espiritu Santo Island in the Coconut War, leading to the deployment of Papua New Guinean soldiers. This nation served as a joint Condominium between Britain and (+) France, and was nicknamed the "Pandemonium." Rapid U.S. withdrawal from this nation in 1945 led to the John Frum "cargo cult." Antoine de Bougainville named the islands that are now this nation the Great Cyclades, and they were (*) renamed the New Hebrides by Captain Cook. For the points, name this South Pacific archipelago.
items.a: Vanuatu

items.q: One language from this modern-day nation was first translated by John Geddie and his wife, and the inhabitants at that time venerated spirits called Natmasses. The crazy libertarian Phoenix Foundation supported Jimmy Stevens' formation of the breakaway State of Vemerana in this nation, leading this nation's Prime Minister Walter Lini to ask for foreign intervention, resulting in the Coconut War. This nation's colonial system was dubbed the Pandemonium, because it was a really wasteful condominium system shared by (*) Britain and France. This nation, whose anthem Yumi Yumi Yumi is written in the Creole Bislama language, is home to a group that builds fake runways in order to attract their savior, who is a synthesis of John the Baptist, Santa Claus, and Uncle Sam. For 10 points, name this nation formerly known as the New Hebrides, an island nation in the South Pacific home to the John Frum Cult.
items.a: Vanuatu [accept New Hebrides before mention]

items.q: The central character of this country's literature is "The Victim" according to a survey that serves as a "Thematic Guide" to this country's literature. It's not the United States, but this country is the setting of a novel where Simon Jordan interviews a murderess, which exemplifies the subgenre of "Southern Gothic" literature of a region in this country. This country, home to the writer of the literary survey (*) Survival, is also home to a literary critic who analyzed works of William Blake in the collection Fearful Symmetry. Alias Grace is set in this country, as is a short story where Janet visits a planetarium with her terminally ill father. For 10 points, name this country home to the writer of The Moons of Jupiter, Alice Munro.
items.a: Canada

items.q: In a novel from this country, the sociobiologist Wilfred Limpkin keeps notes from meetings in cipher. An author from this country based the character Edwin on her grandfather, who hears the same violin noises as Olive Llewellyn 291 years later. That author from this country wrote an article about books with Girl in the title, with the girl being more likely to die if the author's male. American criminal Bernie Madoff was the inspiration for (*) Jonathan Alkaitis, who runs a Ponzi scheme in a novel from this country. In a novel from this country, a presentation about "Problems of Authentication in Reference to [that novel]" is given in the year 2195 by Professor Pieixoto ("p'yay-SHOT-oh"). Agnes Jemima is one of three protagonists of a novel from this home country of Emily St. John Mandel. For 10 points, name this home country of Margaret Atwood.
items.a: Canada

items.q: This country weathered the October Crisis, a dual kidnapping by separatist terrorists that led its leader to quip "just watch me" and employ the War Measures Act during peacetime. The "fuddle duddle" controversy delighted a leader of this country, who later retired after taking a "long walk in the (*) snow." The nationalist party Bloc Quebecois[block keh-bay-KWAH]is active in, for ten points, what North American country, once led by Pierre Trudeau and later by his son Justin?
items.a: Canada

items.q: This country's Operation Snatch confined children to New Denver and sent their parents to Oakalla Prison Farm. Support from James Mavor and Clifford Sifton helped the followers of a man who was killed in a train explosion, Peter Verigin, move to this country. In this country, Paul Yuzyk pushed for the Multiculturalism Act and chronicled the forced labor of Ukrainians at concentration camps like (*) Castle Mountain and the Stanley Barracks under the War Measures Act. In this country, a spiritual Christian movement called the Sons of Freedom gained notoriety for nude protests and arson. The Doukhobors principally settled in this country, where a find at Bonanza Creek turned Dawson City into a boomtown. For 10 points, name this country where many Ukrainians settled in Manitoba.
items.a: Canada

items.q: A 1968 film explores the legacy of this country's colonial period through three women of decreasing social class who are all named Lucia. This country's first female director died of asthma at age 31 while editing the docu-romance One Way or Another. The protagonist of a 1968 film from this country walks out on his teenage girlfriend due to her boredom at the "books and dead animals" in an American author's house. In some of the 2000 photos of this country that make up a 1963 documentary co-narrated by Michel Piccoli, hand-drawn speech bubbles show the lyrics of Benny (*) More songs. In the 1960s, this country's ICAIC board commissioned a film by Agnes Varda and produced films by Sara Gomez, Humberto Solas, and the director of Memories of Underdevelopment, Tomas Gutierrez Alea ("ah-LAY-ah"). A 1999 Wim Wenders documentary depicts a Carnegie Hall concert of songs from this country, like "Chan Chan." For 10 points, name this home country of Buena Vista Social Club.
items.a: Cuba [or Republic of Cuba; or Republica de Cuba; or Erekusu] (The author is Ernest Hemingway, whose house is featured in Memories of Underdevelopment.)

items.q: This country was led by Fulgencio Batista until 1959, when a revolution that began at the Moncada Barracks six years earlier finally succeeded. Playa Giron[ply-uhhee-ROHN]was the site of a failed invasion of this country. (*) Che Guevara assisted this country's futuredictator, who survived dozens of assassination attempts and repelled the Bay of Pigs Invasion. For ten points, name this Caribbean country where Fidel Castro ruled for five decades from Havana.
items.a: Cuba (or Republic ofCuba; accept RepublicadeCuba)

items.q: A poem from this country ends by describing the resounding wood of "the tree we planted for communism." A boy from this country is warned not to fall in love with a "'Merican gal" in the poem "Don't Know No English." The speaker descends a blue mountain "to put an end to capitalists and usurers, / to generals and bourgeois" in a poem from this non-Senegal country titled "Black Woman." Langston Hughes translated a poet from this country who wrote the collection Motifs of (*) Son ("SOHN"). The refrain "¡Mayombe-bombe-mayombe!" is chanted in a poem from this country about the sacrifice of a snake, "Sensemaya." A poem from this country begins "A sincere man am I / From the land where palm trees grow." For 10 points, name this home country of Nancy Morejon, Nicolas Guillen, and Jose Marti, who wrote "Guantanamera."
items.a: Cuba [or Republic of Cuba; or Republica de Cuba]

items.q: In this country, the Sergeant's Revolt established the oppressive Pentarchy of 1933. This country fought the Ten Years' War for independence under the leadership of Carlos Manuel de Cespedes. After his attack on the Moncada Barracks, a leader of this country stated (*) "History will absolve me." That leader would later overthrow Fulgencio Batista. Theodore Roosevelt and the Rough Riders fought the Battle of San Juan hill in this country four months after the USS Maine sank off this country's coast. For ten points, what Caribbean island nation was taken over by Che Guevara and Fidel Castro in 1959?
items.a: Cuba

items.q: The electric guitar was first introduced to a style of music from this country in the song "Consejo a las mujeres" by Blas Duran. That style was popularized through Radio Guarachita, and its first recording was "Borracho de amor" by Jose Manuel Calderon. It is not Cuba, but the three main rhythms of that music are the derecho, majao, and mambo. According to legend, this country's national dance evolved from enslaved workers dragging their chained legs along the ground. The tipico (TEE-pee-co), or (*) cibaeno (see-ba-EH-nyo), subtype of the music for that dance uses the tambora drum and guira (GWEE-ra) scraper alongside accordion, in contrast to a similarly-named style from this country's Francophone western neighbor. For 10 points, name this Caribbean country home to the music and dance styles of bachata and merengue.
items.a: Dominican Republic [or the DR or Republica Dominicana] (The "similarly-named music" is Haitian Meringue.)

items.q: Kongo is unable to accept Felice's humanity because of her birthmark in a novel primarily set in this Spanish-speaking country. A novel set in this country describes how a devout Catholic nicknamed Turk is tortured and executed by Ramfis. In this country, the primary setting of The Farming of Bones, Urania Cabral confronts her father about his former role as "Egghead" and her rape by this country's leader. This country is the setting of Peruvian author Mario Vargas Llosa's (YO-sas) The Feast of the Goat. A car crash kills three of the four protagonists of Julia Alvarez's In the Time of the Butterflies, in which the Mirabal sisters oppose this country's dictator, the Chief. For 10 points, name this Caribbean country and birthplace of Junot (JOO-noh) Diaz, whose novelists wrote about the Trujillo (troo-HEE-oh) regime.
items.a: Dominican Republic [or Republica Dominicana]

items.q: One dictator of this country issued 5 million dollars known as the "papeletas de Lilis" that led to the collapse of its economy. That dictator, Ulises Heureaux, gained the support of the 1868 Restoration War hero Gregorio Luperon by pitting this country's Bolos party against then-president Francisco Billini. In the aftermath of hurricane San Zenon, this country's capital was renamed after another dictator known as El Jefe. A resistance group in this country known as (*) "the Butterflies" was named for the Mirabal sisters. A dictator from this country ordered a botched assassination attempt on Romulo Betancourt. That dictator of this country carried out the Parsley massacre as part of his program of anti-Haitianism. For 10 points, name this Caribbean nation once led by Rafael Trujillo.
items.a: Dominican Republic [or Republica Dominicana; do NOT prompt or accept "Dominica"]

items.q: In the lyrics that accompany a dance in this country, "Americans" are called "intruders" and "abusers"; that dance is "La Protesta" by Nico Lora. The "Yankee-style" form of a dance from this country, which was inspired by imitating the bad dancing of American soldiers, was renamed pambiche. Instruments that accompany a dance from this country, whose variants include the "ripped parrot," include the two-headed tambora drum and the steel (*) guira ["GWEE-rah"] , which is scraped. A hip thrust on every fourth step characterizes another dance from this country called the bachata. In a simple dance originating in this country's Cibao Valley, the dancers drag one of their feet while shaking their hips. For 10 points, name this Caribbean country where the merengue was made the national dance by Rafael Trujillo.
items.a: Dominican Republic [or Republica Dominicana] <WG>

items.q: The first woman elected to this country's National Assembly was Gwendolyn Lizarraga, known as Madam Liz, from the People's United Party. The Battle of St. George's Caye took place in what is now this country during the Anglo-Spanish War. George Cadle Price served as this country's first prime minister after its independence in 1981. During the Caste War, many Maya fled from the Yucatan Peninsula to this country's town of Orange Walk. For the point, name this Central American country, formerly known as British Honduras.
items.a: Belize (accept British Honduras until "what is now this country")

items.q: This country was prompted to move its capital inland due to the destruction caused by Hurricane Hattie in 1961. The archeological site of Caracol is located in this modern-day country, which shares the Maya Mountains with its western neighbor. The second-largest (*) barrier reef in the world is located off the coast of this country, which is the only English-speaking nation in Central America. For 10 points, name this Central American country that has its capital at Belmopan.
items.a: Belize

items.q: Philip Goldson helped to found both of this country's major political parties and names an airport in this country's former capital. That city, which shares a name with this country, lost its status as capital after Hurricane Hattie damaged it in 1961. The Maya Mountains are shared by this country and (*) Guatemala, which did not recognize this country until 1991 because of claims to what was once British territory. This country changed to its current name in 1973 after being known as British Honduras. For 10 points, name this only English speaking country in Central America, with capital at Belmopan.
items.a: Belize [accept British Honduras until "shares a name with this country"]

items.q: This country celebrates a pair of holidays called the September Celebrations, which includes its Independence Day and the Battle of St. George's Cay Day. Among its extensive coastal reefs (*) is a large submarine sinkhole called the Great Blue Hole, and its current capital is a planned city created in 1970 after the destruction of its previous capital by Hurricane Hattie. For 10 points, name this Central American country that moved its namesake capital to the interior city of Belmopan and was formerly known as British Honduras.
items.a: Belize

items.q: A war in this modern day country began after Ibrahima Sori symbolically slashed sacred drums used by the Yalunka people. That state centered on a plateau in this modern country was founded by the deeply religious Karamokho Alfa. After a leader of this country declared "we prefer poverty in liberty to riches in slavery", retreating colonizers spent 2 months cutting telephone lines and burning files. Because this country's capital was harboring members of the PAIGC, it was attacked in a 1970 raid that also freed European POWs held in its notorious (*) Camp Boiro. This modern country, home of the Futa Jallon Imamate, was the only one to vote no in a referendum to join the French Community in 1958; because of that vote, this country became the second sub-Saharan nation to gain independence under the leadership of Ahmed Sekou Toure. For 10 points, name this country whose name is also given to a historical coin minted with African gold in England.
items.a: Guinea [accept Guinea-Conakry]

items.q: Note to moderator: Read the answerline carefully. The Imamate of Futa Jallon ("foo-tuh juh-LOAN") was based in the highlands of this name east of the Rivieres du Sud ("ree-VYAIR doo sood"). The first president of a country with this name descended from the founder of the Wassoulou ("wah-SOO-loo") Empire, Samori ("sah-MOAR-ee"). This word names a country where prisoners starved at Francisco Macias Nguema's ("mah-SEE-ahss n'GAY-mah's") Black Beach. This word names a mainland country led by Joao Bernardo Vieira ("zh'WOW bair-NAR-doo vee-AY-ruh") after he deposed the PAIGC leader Luis, the half-brother of Amilcar Cabral ("ah-MEEL-kar kah-BRAHL"). This word names a bauxite-exporting country led by Ahmed Sekou Toure, coins made with gold from Britain's Royal African Company, and the domesticated Senegambian "fowl." A gulf of this name contains Bioko and Sao Tome and Principe west of Rio Muni, part of a Spanish-speaking "Equatorial" country. For 10 points, what word names West African countries led from Bissau and Conakry ("koh-nah-KREE")?
items.a: Guinea [accept guineafowl; accept Gulf of Guinea; accept Guinea-Conakry or French Guinea; accept Equatorial Guinea or Spanish Guinea; accept Guinea-Bissau or Portuguese Guinea; accept Guinea Highlands; prompt on Bissau or Equatorial by asking "what other word is that country named for?"; prompt on Ghana or Djenne or aguinaou by asking "that may be the etymology of what country name?"] (The PAIGC is the African Party for the Independence of Guinea and Cape Verde.)

items.q: In one short story from this country, Lena bullies her schoolmate, Else ("ELL-suh"), by asking her if she's going to be a servant when she grows up. Later in that story from this country, Else and Lil are invited to see the title object before being kicked out by Aunt Beryl. In another short story from this country, seeing a "lovely as ever" pear tree causes the protagonist, (*) Bertha Young, to feel the titular emotion. This country, the setting of "Bliss", is also the setting of a story where two sisters discover that their neighbour, Mr. Scott, had died outside the gate of their house. That story set in this country ends with Laura Sheridan saying, "Isn't life-?" to her brother, who replies with, "Isn't life darling?". For 10 points, identify this country that is the setting of "The Garden Party", a short story by Katherine Mansfield.
items.a: New Zealand [or Aotearoa]

items.q: Activists in this country formed "Campaign Half Million" to successfully lobby for the closure of its only nuclear reactor. After losing a vote on banning nuclear weapons, a leader of this country called the "Schnapps Election" on live TV while drunk. Fernando Pereira was killed in the harbor of this country's largest city after a ship was bombed. The nuclear ships policy was at the center of 1984 debates in this country that included David (*) Lange. The Rainbow Warrior was bombed in this country to stop Greenpeace protesting nuclear trials, which occurred a year after Robert Muldoon left office. For 10 points, Polynesian weapons testing inspired anti-nuclear activism by what country's Maori people?
items.a: New Zealand [or Aotearoa]

items.q: A woman from this country who directed the documentary Patu! was often known simply as Merata. A kinetic sculptor from this country painted and scratched directly on film stock for the short films A Colour Box and Free Radicals. Len Lye pioneered animation in this country, where a director created a drug addict Vietnam vet frog, Heidi the Hippo, and other Jim Henson-esque puppets called the "Feebles" for a 1989 film. That director from this country made a film in which Lord Crumb leads vomit-eating aliens. A 1992 film from this country required 300 liters of fake (*) blood for a scene in which a lawnmower obliterates zombies infected by a Sumatran rat-monkey. Letterboxd is headquartered in this country. Splatter films like Bad Taste and Braindead brought fame to a director from this country who had the Imperial War Museum's World War I footage colorized for the documentary They Shall Not Grow Old. For 10 points, name this home country of Peter Jackson.
items.a: New Zealand [or Aotearoa; accept NZ] (The filmmaker in the first line is Merata Mita.)

items.q: In this country, the popularity of a slogan that translates to "damn the dam" led to the appointment of Alan Mark to preserve Lake Manapouri. In this country, a group named for the Black Panthers occupied Bastion Point and chanted around politicians' homes in protest against the Dawn Raids. This country's "mother of all budgets" spawned the nickname "Ruthanasia," which followed this country's policy of (*) Rogernomics. This country was accused of violating the Gleneagles Agreement after the South African Rugby Team was allowed to tour. Francois Mitterrand ordered the sinking of a Greenpeace ship docked in this country, the Rainbow Warrior. For 10 points, Robert Muldoon was a Prime Minister of what country home to the Maori people?
items.a: New Zealand

items.q: In 1998, this country's future Prime Minister once used a block of cheese to staunch the bleeding from a bullet wound. This country's Ramush Haradinaj led its namesake (*) Liberation Army prior to the country's independence. For 10 points, name this country that unilaterally declared independence from Serbia in 2008.
items.a: Kosovo

items.q: The city of Prizren in this country was made an imperial capital by Dusan ("DU-shan") the Mighty and later saw a league created there opposing the Treaties of San Stefano and Berlin. A 1389 battle named for this country saw Murad I killed on the Field of Blackbirds but solidified (*) Ottoman rule in the Balkans. A war in this country saw unauthorized intervention when NATO forces bombed Yugoslavia, earning flak for Bill Clinton, following the killing and deportation of ethnic Albanians by Serbian forces. For 10 points, name this newest European country with capital Pristina that split off from Serbia in 2008.
items.a: Kosovo

items.q: The Kachak movement in this province was suppressed following the death of Azem Galica. In 1981, student protests in this province led to the ouster of Mahmut Bakalli. Along with Vojvodina (pr. voy-VOH-dee-nuh), this province had its autonomy rescinded in 1989. The failure of the Rambouillet (pr. ram-boo-yay) Conference led to NATO bombing campaigns against one side in this province's civil war, which pitted its ethnic Albanian majority against the forces of Slobodan Milosevic. For the point, name this former Yugoslavian province that declared independence from Serbia in 2008.
items.a: Kosovo [or Kosova; or Republic of Kosovo; or Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija; or Socialist Autonomous Province of Kosovo]

items.q: This country's capital is the site of the Gadime Marble Cave and Batllava Lake, as well as a monument consisting of the word "NEWBORN" spelled out in large yellow letters. This country is the source of an ongoing exodus of the Gorani people. This country's governance is subject to the Ahtisaari Plan, and the Clint Williamson investigation has indicted several of its politicians for war crimes. What is now this country was the subject of Operation Noble Anvil, the first NATO mission ever undertaken without United Nations approval. The western part of this country, known as the Metohija, is still disputed with its western neighbor, from which this country declared independence in 2008. For 10 points, name this republic which was the target of ethnic cleansing attempts by the Slobodan Milosevic regime in the late 1990s and is now independent from Serbia.
items.a: Kosovo

items.q: For a ritual formerly performed in this region, 40 male and 60 female youths approach across a street and kiss until doused with water. For a daily offering in this region, betel leaf, lime, and gambier ("GAM-beer") representing the Trimurti are put in small leaf-woven baskets. This region's temples had an empty padmasana ("pahd-MAH-suh-nuh") or lotus throne added by the Shaivite reformer Nirartha ("nee-RAR-thuh"). This region's dead are cremated in ornate towers called wadah. This region's New Year's Eve is a day of silence that follows the burning of huge, monstrous butakala statues representing adharma. Curved bamboo poles used in this region's festivals are said to resemble the tail of its panther-like king of the spirits, Barong ("BAH-rong"). The supreme god Acintya ("uh-CHINT-yuh") is worshipped in this region due to the monotheism requirement of Pancasila ("pan-chuh-SEE-luh"). For 10 points, what island is the only Hindu-majority province of Indonesia?
items.a: Bali [prompt on the Sunda Islands or the Lesser Sunda Islands; prompt on Indonesia until read; prompt on Nusantara or Maritime Southeast Asia]

items.q: The indigenous people of this island use a calendar with 10 concurrent weeks of different lengths and 210 days a year. A loophole in the Hays Code allowed Deane H. Dickason to release a quasi-pornographic documentary about "Virgins of [this island]." An anthropologist working on this island documented "child nurses" and modes of kinesthetic learning in a book containing over 700 photographs. Colin McPhee's study of the musicology of this island, where he lived in the 1930s, was included in a documentary depicting a group of women stabbing themselves with kris daggers. Gregory Bateson and Margaret Mead used the participant-observation method to write a book about this island's "Character." For 10 points, name this predominantly Hindu island in Indonesia.
items.a: Bali [accept Balinese Character; accept Trance and Dance in Bali; accept Virgins from Bali]

items.q: According to legend, the founder of a religious order on this island gifted one of its rulers a single hair from his head to cure a plague after traveling to this island on top of a pumpkin. The Danish businessman Mads Lange ("MASS LAHNG-uh") was known as the "King" of this island and acted as a mediator during a series of campaigns provoked by its people's custom of plundering any shipwreck found in this island's waters. It's not in Japan, but people from this island dressed in white and stabbed themselves with daggers as part of a ceremonial last stand called a (*) puputan. After the fall of Gelgel, the Dewa Agung of Klungklung became the most powerful ruler of this island's nine constituent kingdoms. When the Demak Sultanate conquered the Majapahit Empire, the Majapahit royal family emigrated to this island because its people shared the same religion. For 10 points, name this majority-Hindu island that is directly to the east of Java.
items.a: Bali

items.q: A notable cliff carving on this landmass is Yeh Pulu, which depicts a man's hand being bitten by a boar, and it also contains the Goa Gajah cavern, which contains carvings attributed to the giant Kebo Iwa, which is entered through the mouth of a demon and located in its ancient capital of Bedulu. Villages on this island are divided into kaja and kelod ends, and each have temples dedicated to the puseh, or origins, the desa, and the dalem, dedicated to the dead. The main temple on this island is Pura Besakih on its highest point, the volcano Gunung Agung. Most of this island's cultural festivals take place in its central city of Ubud, which is home to its Legong dance stages. This island's Hindu culture dates to the 9th Century. For 10 points, name this island, the westernmost in the Lesser Sunda Archipelago, whose largest city is Denpasar.
items.a: Bali

items.q: It's possible to see Fallen Jerusalem Island from this territory's Devil's Bay and The Baths National Parks. Bubbly Pool is a naturally occurring "hot tub"-style swimming hole on the northeast shore of Jost Van Dyke in this territory. Anegada is a geologically distinct region of this territory, being composed of carbonate reef deposits. This territory's highest peak is Sage Mountain on (*) Tortola. Since 2013, Richard Branson has lived in this territory, which shares part of its name with Branson's conglomerate. In 1741, this territory's capital was moved to its current location at Road Town. For 10 points, name this former crown colony and current overseas territory in the Caribbean located to the east of its American counterpart.
items.a: British Virgin Islands [or BVIs]

items.q: One of them is shaped as two rectangles joined by a small spit, and another was the birthplace of one of a designer of the U.S. Capitol, William Thornton. Minor parts have names such as Norman, Peter, and Cooper, while the four principal components of this territory are Gorda, Jost Van Dyke, Anegada and the population center of Tortola. The largest settlement in this riverless territory is Road Town, and the group comprises the eastern extremity of the Greater Antilles. Found to the northeast of a similarly-named American territory, they received internal autonomy in 1977. For 10 points, name these islands which constitute a Caribbean colony of the United Kingdom.
items.a: British Virgin Islands [prompt on partial answer]

items.q: According to legend, the introduction of a single pregnant rabbit to a portion of this region by an Italian settler led to the destruction of its entire agricultural plantings. This was the [emphasize] smallest region to be covered in a 16th century work roughly translating to "Sorrows of the Earth". One legend claims that the name "Henry the German" was adopted by Wladyslaw [vwah-dee-suave] III after fleeing to this region after the Battle of Varna. The modern Rare Wine Company names their wines from this region after Boston, New York, Savannah, and several (*) Founding Fathers to honor its popularity in colonial America. North African slave labor was used to build aqueducts throughout this region called levadas. (*) Christopher Columbus met and married his wife Felipa in this region, which by that time had become an important sugar producer since its confirmed discovery in 1419 by Joao Goncalves [zhwao gone-sahl-vays] Zarco and Tristao Vaz Teixeira [tris-tao vahz tay-shay-rah]. For 10 points, name this common stopping point for trips across the Atlantic, a Portuguese-owned archipelago governed from Funchal.
items.a: Madeira [accept Autonomous Region of Madeira or Regiao Autonoma da Madeira]

items.q: John Hancock's ship Liberty was importing this territory's most notable product when it was seized for evading the Townshend Acts. Canals called levadas supply water for this territory's thriving sugar cane production. The bolo de mel honey cake from this island is often confused with an unrelated English sponge cake named for it. The Hawaiian ukulele was derived from the (*) cavaquinho [kah-vah-KEEN-yo] used by this island's musicians. This territory, whose laurisilva forests are designated as a World Heritage Site, uses terraces called poios similar to those in the Douro River valley on the mainland to grow grapes. This island's capital city is Funchal. For 10 points, name this island owned by Portugal, known for a namesake type of wine.
items.a: Madeira

items.q: 2. It forms part of an island group with the Ilhas Desertas, the Ilhas Selvagensas and Porto Santo. The Romans knew about it but it had to be rediscovered by Zarco and Texeira in the 15th century. The British briefly occupied it in the 19th century and used its main port of Funchal, and the Spanish ran it from 1580 to 1640, but otherwise since Henry the Navigator's time the Portuguese have controlled, FTP, what island near Morocco that is best known for a very nice kind of wine.
items.a: Madeira

items.q: The government of this country partnered with the Israeli firm Neema to issue the SOV, the world's first sovereign cryptocurrency. In 2014, activist Kathy Jetnil-Kijiner received a standing ovation at the U.N. after she read a poem stating that her seven-month-old baby would outlive this country. The U.S. Department of Energy stores large amounts of radioactive debris under a concrete dome on this country's Runit Island. Tyson Foods employs a large diaspora of people from this country living in (*) Springdale, Arkansas, who immigrated there thanks in part to the Compact of Free Association, signed alongside Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia. Either Kiribati ("KEE-ree-bass") or this country will likely be the first to be fully submerged due to rising sea levels. Majuro is the capital of, for 10 points, what Pacific island country where the U.S. tested the hydrogen bomb on Bikini Atoll?
items.a: Marshall Islands [or Republic of the Marshall Islands; or Aolepan Aorokin Majel ]

items.q: The snorkeling "Fantastic Grandmothers" found sea snakes in this territory's Baie des Citrons. This territory's Pindai Caves held fossils of birds like Sylviornis, the pile-builder megapode, and the kagu. A September 24th "Citizenship Day" celebrates the 1853 annexation of this territory, whose huts topped with fleches faitieres ("flesh fet-YAIRS") inspired Renzo Piano's Jean-Marie Tjibaou ("chee-BAO") Cultural Centre. The type site of the Lapita culture is in this nickel-exporting archipelago, whose penal colony held Communards like Louise Michel and the Kabyle ("kah-BEEL") "Algerians of the Pacific." This sui generis collectivity is home to intelligent qua-qua crows and the Kanak people, who boycotted its 2021 independence referendum under the Noumea ("noo-MAY-uh") Accord. For 10 points, what overseas French territory in Melanesia is named for a Latin term for Scotland?
items.a: New Caledonia [or Nouvelle-Caledonie; accept New Caledonian crow; accept Grande Terre; accept Loyalty Islands or Iles Loyaute; accept Chesterfield Islands or Iles Chesterfield; accept Belep archipelago; accept Isle of Pines or Ile des Pins or Kunyie]

items.q: In this region, the door jambs of houses built on artificial mounds feature male-female pairs of figures with large noses called jovo or tale. A set of buildings in this region feature programmable glass louvers and slats made from iroko wood imported from Africa, and are divided into three "villages" each based around a "Great House." Houses in this region feature spires called fleches faitieres ("flesh fet-YAIR"). "Cases" with jutting ribs make up this region's (*) Jean-Marie Tjibaou Cultural Centre, one of the signature designs of Renzo Piano. In this region, conical thatched roofs characterize the architecture of the Kanak people. For 10 points, name this special collectivity of France in the Pacific Ocean whose capital is Noumea.
items.a: New Caledonia [or Nouvelle Caledonie; prompt on Melanesia or Oceania]
items.s: 2023 "Questions Based on Wikipedia Links Ophir Sent Me"

items.q: All members of the Rhacodactylus genus are found in this territory, including the world's largest gecko. The Amborella plant genus native to this territory was one of the first to branch off from the angiosperms. A family of flightless birds endemic to this territory possess unique "corns" covering their nostrils, can use their wings to help them climb trees, and are called kagus. A (*) crow found in this territory has been observed trimming twigs off branches to make them better suited for probing anthills in an unusual example of avian tool manufacture. This territory will hold an independence referendum in November 2018 in accordance with an agreement with its native Kanak people. For 10 points, name this French overseas territory with its capital at Noumea.
items.a: New Caledonia [accept Nouvelle-Caledonie]

items.q: Houses in this archipelago are topped with wooden spires carved into faces, which are called fleche faitiere [FLETCH "fight"-ee-"AIR"]. This island group's wildlife includes the world's largest gecko and a flightless bird called the kabu. The ore garnierite was named after the discoverer of this island group's massive nickel deposits. Many Kabyle [kuh-"BILE"] people on this archipelago were taught by a woman who became notorious as the "Red Virgin of Montmartre." An independence movement in this archipelago culminated in a hostage crisis at a cave in (*) Ouvea. The Kanak people are the indigenous residents of this archipelago, which held participants in the Paris Commune during its time as a penal colony. For 10 points, name this special collectivity of France, south of VanuatuinthePacificOcean.
items.a: New Caledonia

items.q: One politician from this country is known for wearing a cowboy hat that was a gift from George W. Bush. That man directed a series of abductions from his opponent's hometown of Leer before a peace agreement created the post of First Vice President for that opponent. For one referendum in this country, images of clasped and open hands were used on ballot papers for this country's largely illiterate population. This country disputes the oil-rich (*) Heglig region with its Northern neighbor, and this country's pending relocation of its capital to Ramciel was first proposed by John Garang.
