Augustus (*) Pugin ("pew-JAN") and Charles Barry were responsible for rebuilding this location in a Gothic Revival style after an 1834 fire captured by J.M.W. Turner. A tower in these buildings, renamed after Elizabeth, contains the recently restored Big Ben. For 10 points, name this building that contains the House of Commons and the House of Lords.
items.a: Palace of Westminster [or Westminster Palace; accept Houses of Parliament; prompt on House of Commons or House of Lords before read; prompt on London]

items.q: After this group of buildings was completed, one of their robing rooms was filled with frescoes modeled on the art of Pinturicchio ("peen-too-REEK-yo") by William Dyce. The architect of these buildings used a similar steep, steel roof in his design for Halifax Town Hall. The interiors of these buildings were modeled on sketches by the historian Augustus Pugin ("PYEW-jin"). Charles Barry designed these buildings in the (*) Gothic Revival style. The "effects of fog" on these buildings are shown with strokes of blue, purple, and orange in a series by Claude Monet. A tower in these buildings was renamed the Elizabeth Tower in 2012, and is currently silent due to ongoing renovations. Big Ben is part of, for 10 points, what set of buildings along the River Thames ("tems") that house the British legislature?
items.a: Houses of Parliament [or Palace of Westminster; or Westminster Palace; prompt on palace or parliament or British parliament or Westminster or buildings of parliament]

items.q: A gallery in this building contains a set of eight gilded Caen stone statues by John Birnie Philip and a pair of faded frescoes by Daniel Maclise. A set of frescoes depicting virtues made by William Dyce hang in this building's "Robing Room". A man whose title is often shortened to "Black Rod" is responsible for maintaining this building, which was designed by Charles Barry and Augustus Pugin. Four bells in this building play a chime melody (*) named for it that gets longer every quarter hour. Its predecessor is on fire in a J. M. W. Turner painting which shows it to the left of Waterloo Bridge. Its Elizabeth Tower features a four-faced clock and the bell Big Ben. For 10 points, name this complex facing the River Thames that contains meeting rooms for the Lords and the Commons.
items.a: Houses of Parliament [or the Palace of Westminster; prompt on Westminster]

items.q: Specific name or common nickname acceptable. The photobook 1972/accumulations highlights the individuality of this building, despite most photos using the same large aperture lens with a composition anchored on a window in the center. A "white ark" installed in a park was part of a program started in 2014 to allow monthly rentals of sections of this building. This building was commissioned by and named for the president of a real-estate company after seeing the architect's designs at the 1970 (+) World Expo. One section of this asbestos-laden building, dubbed A1302, was recently acquired by the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art, and has a built-in reel-to-reel tape deck in the wall. An unsuccessful years-long campaign to save this building was led by (*) Tatsuyuki Maeda. High-tension bolts connected the 140 units of this Metabolist building to the two central structures; those elements were designed to be replaced as needed by architect Kisho Kurokawa. For 10 points, name this building commonly named for its 100-square-feet rooms.
items.a: Nakagin Capsule Tower [accept Tokyo Capsule Tower; prompt on Nakagin building]

items.q: The center including this building contains a Glenna Goodacre sculpture showing some playing children and a frog-themed fountain in honor of Mark Twain, both found in Redwood Park. This building's exterior is covered in quartz, giving it a white color. It's two so-called "wings" that emerge after the 29th floor were necessitated to house elevator shafts, and its original design shape was motivated by a shadow restriction law that necessitated a surface area to height ratio. Designed by William Pereira, its height was limited in order to preserve views of the sea from (*) Nob Hill, and its 48th floor conference room gives a panoramic view of San Francisco. For 10 points, name this skyscraper designed for an insurance company with a pointed shape evocative of an Egyptian funerary building.
items.a: Transamerica Pyramid

items.q: The site that this building currently occupies was once the office of Sun Yat-Sen's Young China newspaper. Its exterior color is due to a coat of cast quartz applied to the building. Conceived by John R. Beckett after viewing trees in a public park, it was designed by the William Pereira firm which wanted to make it taller but were not allowed to break the line of sight between Nob Hill and the nearby bay. From the twenty-ninth floor to the top, elevators and a smoke tower are supported by the prominent "wings" and, until the construction of the Aon Center, it was the tallest building west of the Mississippi. FTP, name this building found in the Montgomery Financial District of San Francisco; the oddly shaped former headquarters of an American financial concern.
items.a: the Transamerica Pyramid (or the Transamerica Tower)

items.q: The architect Hans Kopp reported that this building was too "flimsy" for a bell to be hung in its tower, which was constructed to be wide open on three sides on the ground floor. In the 16th century, a large bell called "Patronus" and a smaller bell named for the king's son were mounted in this building. The San Frediano in Lucca may have inspired the commission of this building's Last Judgement mosaic, likely designed by Nicoletto Semitecolo ("nick-o-LET-oh sem-ee-TECK-o-loh") of Venice, by a ruler who employed Matthias of Arras ("a-RAH") to design its layout. Rulers travelling to coronations in this building would pass through the (*) Powder Tower separating the Old and New Town. Peter Parler designed this building's net-vaults, working at the behest of Holy Roman Emperor Charles IV. For 10 points, name this Gothic cathedral, the seat of the Archbishop of Prague.
items.a: St. Vitus Cathedral [or Metropolitan Cathedral of Saints Vitus, Wenceslaus and Adalbert, or metropolitni katedrala svateho Vita, Vaclava a Vojtecha; accept St. Vitus alone after "cathedral" is read and prompt before]

items.q: This artist photographed a row of women lifting rakes into the air and an iron puddler as part of the Eyes of Russia collection for Fortune. This artist dubbed the helicopter a "flying tripod" and captured a picture of people inside the Statue of Liberty's Crown. Annie Leibovitz claimed she had this artist's "shadow" over her as she stood atop Bill, a gargoyle on the Chrysler Building. This artist photographed a line of flood victims under a sign reading "World's Highest Standard of Living." This artist photographed the collection You Have Seen Their Faces, whose text was written by her partner Erksine Caldwell. This war correspondent photographed the Fort Peck Dam as the first cover for Life magazine. For 10 points, name this American photographer who captured Gandhi at his spinning wheel.
items.a: Margaret Bourke-White [prompt on Margaret Bourke]

items.q: A work by this artist prominently features the slogan, "World's Highest Standard of Living," which is juxtaposed against a line of people seeking refuge from a Kentucky flood. This photographer's depictions of the Fort Peck dam were featured in the first issue of an iconic photojournalism magazine. After surviving numerous near-death experiences, including a helicopter crash in the Chesapeake bay, this person was given the epithet "the Indestructible). With (*) Erskine Caldwell, this person created a "pictorial survey" of the Southern United States. This photographer captured her most iconic subject for Life magazine, hours before his assassination. For 10 points, name this first female war correspondent and influential photographer of Gandhi at his spinning wheel.
items.a: Margaret Bourke-White

items.q: For one shot, this artist was only permitted to use three flashbulbs, but lost one to the heat and moisture and forgot to pull the slide on another, leaving only one flash usable. Aerial photographs by this artist include one in which a DC-4 flies over Manhattan. Though not Annie Leibovitz, this artist is shown seated on one of the sculpted eagles of the Chrysler Building in another photo. This artist took a shot of Montana's Fort Peck Dam which appeared on the first cover of (*) LIFE magazine following its 1936 relaunch. Together with her onetime husband Erskine Caldwell, she documented the lives of sharecroppers in the Deep South in the book You Have Seen Their Faces. She was the first female photographer to cover World War II. For 10 points, name this American photojournalist who photographed Mahatma Gandhi at his spinning wheel.
items.a: Margaret Bourke-White

items.q: This photographer highlighted sweat dripping down the bare chests of two gold miners in one of the first widely-seen images of apartheid South Africa. A grinning man slings an axe over his shoulder as the hand of an unseen man holds up a severed head in an image by this photographer. Alfred Eisenstaedt documented this photographer's treatment for Parkinson's disease, the subject of the autobiography Portrait of Myself. After surviving a helicopter crash, a torpedoing, and a stranding in the Arctic while on assignment, this photographer was nicknamed "the Indestructible." Emaciated men stand behind barbed wire in the best known of this photographer's images of the Allied liberation of Buchenwald. This woman's photograph of the construction of Fort Peck Dam graced the first cover in the history of Life magazine. She interviewed her best-known subject hours before his 1948 assassination. For 10 points, name this first female war correspondent, who photographed Gandhi at his spinning wheel.
items.a: Margaret Bourke-White [accept Maggie the Indestructible until "the Indestructible" is read]

items.q: In Forty-One False Starts, Janet Malcolm describes a portrait by this photographer of a woman in a Bedouin-like scarf near Lake Ediza and muses on this photographer's "grandly eclectic taste in P. H." This photographer spent two weeks photographing a toilet from below so that it resembled the Victory of Samothrace ("SAM-oh-thrace") for the photo Excusado ("ex-koo-SAH-doh"). This photographer's Daybooks describe a trip to Mexico with Tina Modotti. The Oceano ("oh-say-ANN-oh") dunes were frequented by this photographer and his muse Charis ("carris") Wilson, who hides her face and holds her crossed legs in a nude portrait taken in Santa Monica. This co-founder of f/64 ("F-stop sixty-four") captured the stark white opening of the title shell head-on and against a dark background in his photo Nautilus. For 10 points, name this American photographer of abstract and erotic still lifes such as Pepper No. 30.
items.a: Edward Weston [or Edward Henry Weston]

items.q: In this photographer's Armco Steel, Ohio, a domino-like set of seven smokestacks rise like the Flatiron Building above the namesake factory. At the bottom of one picture by this photographer, a fern frond brushes against the leg of a woman who lounges on a sofa while wearing a gas mask. This photographer of that satire, Civilian Defense, also shot a picture of a man whose left arm appears raised to his chest to unbutton a final shirt button, as he lies on the ground. That shot, Dead Man, Colorado Desert, was taken during a cross-country trip this photographer made as part of a Guggenheim Fellowship. A woman crosses her left leg over her right while sitting on the floor, with her unseen face resting on her left knee, while her hands clasp around her right knee in this photographer's 1936 Nude. For 10 points, two sides curve together to touch one another at the top of the sexually suggestive Pepper No. 30, a work by what photographer, whose head-on shot of a nautilus shell is one of the most expensive photos ever sold?
items.a: Edward Weston

items.q: One work by this artist features an ad for "Hot Coffee", and he depicted his own toilet in Excusado. Another work by this artist features his assistant sitting nude as she holds her knee and tucks her head down; that depiction of Charis Wilson signaled his transition from depicting single body parts to entire nude figures. This man depicted a shell standing on end in his Nautilus, and an exhibition of this man's work inspired the creation of the group f/64. This person's most famous work involved the use of the opening of a tin funnel to create a better contrast and a third dimension. For 10 points, name this Pictorialist photographer who depicted a misshapen and partially rotten vegetable in his Pepper, No. 30.
items.a: Edward Weston

items.q: One of his works features a fluorescent light labeled T3 shining down on Karl Struss, who operates a video camera. His portraits include those of Ivanos and Bugatti and one of the sculptor William Edmonson with his hands folded across his chest. This photographer frequently employed split trees in his works, such as the one in the background of "Wrecked Car" and the one next to the titular locale in "Lake Van Norden." Favorite subjects include Lake Tenaya and Tina Modotti, both mentioned in his Daybooks, and he depicted a New Mexico graveyard in "St. Barnard Cemetary." Imogen Cunningham depicted him alongside Margrethe Mather, and this man's other works include a depiction of his son Cole on a wheelbarrow, and his pictures of nature include "Dunes, Oceano." For 10 points, identify this photographer, a founding member of f/64 best known for his nudes and botanical shots, like "Pepper #30."
items.a: Edward Weston

items.q: This artist composed a Symphonic Set for Piano and Orchestra, which he premiered alongside conductor Dean Dixon in Venice. This composer of Martin documented the Causey family, who then were forced to leave town for their safety after the publication of "The Restraints: Open and Hidden." Before working at Life magazine, this person bought a camera from a pawnshop, learned how to use it, and worked for the FSA. This artist used a low angle to photograph a child who points at a white doll in (*) Doll Test. In one of this person's photographs, a man peers towards the right as he holds a manhole cover angled over his head. That photo by this man was part of a collaboration with Ralph Ellison for two largely unpublished essays and was titled The Invisible Man. For 10 points, name this artist who took a photo of a government cleaning woman called American Gothic, and who also directed the movie Shaft.
items.a: Gordon Parks

items.q: One photograph by this artist depicts the fingers and face of a man emerging from a manhole. He wrote a book of poetry titled after another of his photographs, which depicts a malnourished Brazilian boy named Flavio. He photographed three black clad women with unfocused faces in the background as a white-blouse wearing Ingrid Bergman stares into the camera. On his first day of employment with the Farm Security Administration, he took his famous photograph of a janitor standing in front of an American flag holding a broom and a mop. This photographer of (*) "American Gothic" was the first African-American staff photographer for Life magazine. For 10 points, name this photo-essayist who adapted his own coming of age novel in the film The Learning Tree and also directed Shaft.
items.a: Gordon Parks

items.q: An early painting by this artist is titled The Ruins of Holyrood Chapel. A statue of Jupiter Tonans stands in front of drapery in a "still life" by this artist once housed at Kynzvart Castle. Another work by this artist depicts a man getting his shoes shined at the corner of a seemingly empty street. A feud between this artist of Boulevard du Temple and Henry Fox Talbot spawned after the latter introduced "salted paper" to one art form. This artist slowly phased out (*) bitumen use to improve one art form while working with Joseph Nicephore Niepce. In 1835, this artist invented a technique in which mercury fumes are exposed to an iodized silver-coated plate until an image appears. For 10 points, what Frenchman is the namesake of the first publicly available method of photography?
items.a: Louis-Jacques-Mande Daguerre [accept daguerreotype]

items.q: In response to state support of this artist, Hippolyte Bayard wrote a fictional third-person suicide note on the back of his Self-Portrait as a Drowned Man. This artist and Charles Bouton painted wraparound tableaux shown at their diorama theaters. One of this artist's works shows a man getting his shoe shined along an empty boulevard. Britain was forced to pay for this man's otherwise free invention due to a patent war with Henry Fox Talbot. This photographer partnered with the inventor of the Heliograph, Nicephore Niepce ("nee-EPS"). Iodine vapors sensitize a silver-plated sheet of copper in a process invented by this photographer. For 10 points, name this inventor of a namesake early photographic process.
items.a: Louis-Jacques-Mande Daguerre [or Daguerreotype]

items.q: Hippolyte Bayard melodramatically protested the government's positive treatment of this other artist by depicting himself lying dead in a morgue in Self Portrait as a Drowned Man. An early work by this artist depicts three shelves of neatly piled Shells and Fossils. A still life by this artist depicts a framed print of an embracing couple and a cast of a ram's head on the wall behind two casts of putti on a table and a hanging wicker flask. In another of his photographs, a shadowy man having his shoe polished stands in front of a row of trees receding up an empty avenue. This man began a rivalry with Henry Fox Talbot years after the end of his coded correspondence with Joseph Nicephore (*) Niepce. This photographer of Still Life in Studio and Paris Boulevard developed a process in which a silver-plated sheet of copper is treated with fumes of iodine and mercury. For 10 points, name this French artist whose namesake "-otype" was the first method for creating photographs.
items.a: Louis-Jacques-Mande Daguerre

items.q: This photographer grouped his photos into categories such as "Body of a Woman" and "Pleasures" and stopped taking photos after the death of his editor at Harper's Bazaar, Carmel Snow. This artist declared the photographer should be "an impartial witness" who also has a "sense of the magic beneath the surface of reality" in a photobook where he was "eager to penetrate [an] other world ... of (+) mobsters, outcasts, toughs, pimps, whores, addicts, inverts." In a photobook originally published as a spiral-bound edition by Peginot, this artist presented photos he took alongside figures such as Raymond Queneau and Henry Miller. Because they were so heavy, this man was only able to carry 24 plates at a time when making photos in a technique he learned from compatriot (*) Andre Kertesz. This artist disowned a book containing some of his raciest photographs of prostitutes due to a dispute with the publisher; it wasn't re-issued until 1976 as The Secrets of Paris of the '30s. For 10 points, name this mononymous Hungarian photographer of Paris by Night.
items.a: Brassai [or Gyula Halasz]

items.q: One of this man's photographs highlights the winding, S-shaped path followed by an open gutter. This artist examined "the gigantic photograph constituted by In Search of Lost Time" in his book Proust in the Power of Photography, which is illustrated with some of his photographs of operagoers and balletgoers. More of those high society photographs appear in this artist's book titled for a "secret" city "of the thirties," alongside a photograph of a woman nicknamed "Bijou" interlacing her heavily jeweled fingers. He captured the reflections of an embracing couple in mirrors to their back and side in his photograph Lovers in a Small Cafe, near the Place d'Italie. This man, whom Henry Miller nicknamed "the eye of Paris," compiled many photographs of the city's brothels in his best-known series. For 10 points, name this author of the photobook Paris by Night, a Hungarian-born photographer who went by a single name.
items.a: Brassai [or Gyula Halasz; or Jules Halasz]

items.q: For over 40 years, many expansions of this institution were based on a master plan laid out by Kevin Roche. Calvert Vaux's red brick design for this institution was derided as a "mausoleum" and was replaced in a few years by Richard Morris Hunt's Beaux-Arts design. From 2015 to 2020, this institution operated a branch in a Marcel Breuer-designed building after The Whitney moved out. Fort Tryon Park is home to a (*) medieval-art-focused branch of this institution called the Cloisters. "Superfine" was the theme of the 2025 edition of this institution's annual gala organized by Anna Wintour. For 10 points, name this largest art museum in New York City.
items.a: Metropolitan Museum of Art [accept the Met; accept the Met Cloisters or the Met Breuer]

items.q: The so-called "Islamic Wing" of this institution was designed by Kevin Roche, the architect who has been responsible for all its expansions, and who created a new master plan for it in the 1970s. After Calvert Vaux's design for this building was criticized in 1871, a Beaux Arts-style grand stairway and facade designed by Richard Morris Hunt was installed near the end of the 19th century. A part of this institution in Fort Tryon Park devoted to subjects from the Middle Ages is called The (*) Cloisters. This institution's main collection, which includes David's (dah-VEED's) The Death of Socrates and Winslow Homer's The Gulf Stream, is in a set of buildings on Fifth Avenue, between 81st and 84th streets. For 10 points, name this largest art museum in New York City.
items.a: Metropolitan Museum of Art [or The Met]

items.q: Designed by J.W. Mould and Calvert Vaux, the Thomas J. Watson library was added by McKim, Mead, and White. Noted contributors through the years included Andre Meyer and Robert Lehman and it features a Costume Institute. Robert Campin's Merode Altarpiece is housed in its other branch, The Cloisters, while the permanent collection includes David's The Death of Socrates and the Temple of Dendur. For 10 points identify this institution that opened in 1880 and sits on Central Park facing Fifth Avenue.
items.a: the Metropolitan Museum of Art [or the Met]

items.q: A Madonna nicknamed after this location is unusually set in front of an open window facing a seascape and features two angels. This location, with a notably long internal courtyard, holds an Annunciation by a student of Andrea del Verrocchio in which Mary reads from a book on a veil on the right. Filippo Lippi's most famous painting is held at this museum, which also contains a tondo Madonna featuring a pomegranate. Another painting at this Giorgio Vasari-designed museum depicts an impossible pudica pose of a goddess identified as Aura. That painting at this museum shows Zephyrus and Chloris next to the title goddess standing on a sea shell. For 10 points, name this Florentine art museum home to The Birth of Venus.
items.a: Uffizi Gallery

items.q: In 1993, the Niobe Room of this building was damaged in an early-morning car bombing. A busy painting of this building shows the amusingly named Other Winsdor standing beside the artist. Johann Zoffany was hired by King George III to paint this building's Tribuna. Giorgio Vasari built a corridor that connects this building with the Palazzo (*) Pitti. This museum holds the Venus of Urbino. The name of this museum derives from the fact that it was constructed by Cosimo de' Medici to house administrative offices. This museum holds major works by Botticlli, such as Primavera and The Birth of Venus. For 10 points, name this major art museum in Florence.
items.a: Uffizi Gallery [or Galleria degli Uffizi]

items.q: This museum houses a clock pavilion that was previously a medieval moat, and a marble statue of Nike divides its Daru staircase. A large floating dome representing shaded palm fronds sits atop a satellite of this museum in Abu Dhabi, while the home campus contains a controversial steel and glass (*) pyramid design. This museum is separated into Dennon, Sully, and Richelieu wings, and its galleries include the Venus de Milo and Mona Lisa. For 10 points, identify this largest art museum in the world, located in Paris, France.
items.a: the Louvre [or Musee du Louvre]

items.q: To reconstruct a sculpture by this artist, Adolf Furtwangler ("FYOORT-vain-glur") attached a head from the Pelagio Palagi to a body kept in Dresden. An inscription calling a wrestler beautiful appears on the little finger of a statue by this artist. Although this artist likely didn't use the number, Mark Barr referenced this sculptor's name when he symbolized the golden ratio. A Lawrence Alma-Tadema painting depicts this artist presenting a frieze of the Panathenaic ("pan-uh-thuh-NAY-ic") games to his friends. Alan LeQuire recreated a sculpture by this artist in the naos of a William Crawford Smith project in Centennial Park, Nashville. This artist and his patron Pericles appear on the shield of a chryselephantine ("chris-ell-uh-FAN-tin") sculpture by him wearing gold and holding a small Nike. For 10 points, name this Athenian sculptor of the Statue of Zeus at Olympia and of the Athena in the Parthenon.
items.a: Phidias [or Pheidias]

items.q: According to Plutarch this man died in prison after he was accused of embezzling gold for one of his projects. This man was once commissioned to sculpt a group of heroes from the Battle of Marathon, including an image of Miltiades. One of his works was Aphrodite of Elis and this teacher of Alcamenes and Agoracritus also created a work which has a relief of the birth of Pandora on its pedestal. Another one of his works shows a figure holding a small statue of Nike in one hand and an eagle on a scepter in the other. For ten points, name this sculptor of Athena Parthenos and Zeus at Olympia.
items.a: Phidias

items.q: In one work by this sculptor, the subject wears a helmet with a central Sphinx-like figure surrounded by a griffin on each side. One of his works was a colossal bronze statue of a goddess standing between the Propylaea and the Parthenon and is titled the Athena Promachos. A more famous statue holds a shield in its left hand and a figurine of Nike in its right, and was once covered with gold. The creator of the Athena Parthenos is, for 10 points, what Greek sculptor who created the Statue of Zeus at Olympus?
items.a: Phidias

items.q: One of this man's works was probably modeled after Pantarces and was set up at Olympia, Anadumenus. This student of Hegeladas and rival of Hegias created a work in which a bare-headed figure holds a helmet with her extended right hand. One of his sculptures lay between the Propylaea and a building which housed another of his sculptures. That sculpture has the tale of Pandora's birth in relief on its pedestal, holds a small statue of Victory, and has a sphinx on her helmet and Medusa's head on her breastplate. For 10 points, identify this Greek sculptor of numerous Athenas such as Athena Promachos and Athena Parthenos.
items.a: Phidias

items.q: In plants, this organelle is where branched-chain components of the cell wall, such as hemicelluloses and pectins, are synthesized. This organelle is where phosphocholine is attached to ceramide ("SAIR-uh- mide") to produce sphingomyelin. This organelle is the primary site of O-linked glycosylation, which produces proteoglycans ("pro-tee-oh-GLY-cans"). Brefeldin A prevents intracellular transport to this organelle by blocking COPII ("cop-two"). This organelle tags (*) proteins with mannose-6-phosphate to signal transport to the lysosome. This organelle's cisternae ("siss-TER-nee") move between its "cis" and "trans" networks. This organelle directs vesicles to the cell surface for secretion. For 10 points, name this organelle that serves as the packaging center of the cell.
items.a: Golgi apparatus [or Golgi body or Golgi complex]

items.q: Congenital defects in enzymes localizing to this organelle cause a type II pattern in a CDT assay. A process primarily occurring in this organelle uses four "major" and four "minor" core structures. In this organelle, the enzymes FUT2 and FUT3 create the Lewis secretor phenotype, and the H antigen is elaborated into the A or B antigens. In this organelle, a nearby proline often determines sites of its mucin-type modifications to serine and threonine residues. By inhibiting the nucleotide exchange factor GBF1 and thus inhibiting Arf1p, brefeldin A causes this organelle to disappear by inhibiting COPI ("cop-one") trafficking. This organelle adds mannose-6-phosphate to lysosomal hydrolases and operates via cisternal maturation across cis, medial, and trans portions. For 10 points, name this stack of flattened cisternae that packages and sorts proteins.
items.a: Golgi apparatus [or Golgi body]

items.q: This organelle synthesizes all GAGs ("gags") except hyaluronic ("hy-uh-loo-RON-ik") acid. Sphingomyelin ("sfing-goh-MY-uh-lin") synthase localizes to this organelle, which disappears after inhibiting Arfᐧ1ᐧp with brefeldin ("breh-FELL-din") A. In sperm, the acrosome ("AK-ruh-sohm") is derived from this organelle. O-linked glycosylation ("gly-koh-suh-LAY-shuhn") primarily occurs in this organelle. This organelle receives COPII ("cop-two")-coated vesicles from the (*) endoplasmic reticulum. This organelle is made of flattened discs called cisternae ("sis-TUR-nee"). For 10 points, name this organelle that packages proteins, named for an Italian.
items.a: Golgi apparatus [or Golgi body or Golgi complex]

items.q: ADP-ribosylation factors in this structure are blocked by Brefeldin A. Derivatives of galactose are added to serine and threonine residues via O-linked glycosylation (glyke-AH-sil-AY-shun) in this structure. This organelle tags proteins destined for the lysosome with (*) mannose-6-phosphate. Vesicles coated with COPII (cop two) transport proteins to the cis network of this organelle after folding in the endoplasmic reticulum. This organelle is composed of flattened sacs called cisternae (sis-TER-nee). For 10 points, name this organelle that serves as the "packaging center" of the cell.
items.a: Golgi apparatus [or Golgi body or Golgi complex]

items.q: These structures can have alternating bands called lines of Zahn. These structures form aberrantly in antiphospholipid syndrome. AT-III deficiency and a condition named for Leiden increase the probability of forming these structures. Estrogen-containing contraceptive pills increase the risk of forming these structures compared to progestin-only pills. These structures are made of cross-linked fibrin. Mutations in Factor VIII impair the formation of these structures, resulting in hemarthrosis and hemophilia. For 10 points, platelets and coagulation factors cause the formation of what structures in response to bleeding?
items.a: blood clots [or thrombus or thrombi or embolus or emboli; prompt on clots or clotting]

items.q: Women with an increased risk or history of these structures are recommended to take progestin-only or non-hormonal birth controls in part due to the effects of estrogen on levels of plasminogen. Tissue factor activates the extrinsic pathway that forms these structures. The formation of these structures is impaired in (*) von Willebrand disease, which may lead to menorrhagia. Heparin and the Vitamin K-antagonist warfarin may be administered to inhibit the formation of these products and treat deep vein thrombosis. Hemophilia is characterized by an impairment in the ability to form, for 10 points, what gel-like coagulations of blood?
items.a: blood clots [accept venous blood clots or arterial blood clots; accept thrombus before "thrombosis,"prompt afterward; prompt on pulmonary embolism or embolus]

items.q: Women with an increased risk or history of these structures are recommended to take progestin-only or non-hormonal birth controls in part due to the effects of estrogen on levels of plasminogen. Tissue factor activates the extrinsic pathway that forms these structures. The formation of these structures is impaired in (*) von Willebrand disease, which may lead to menorrhagia. Heparin and the Vitamin K-antagonist warfarin may be administered to inhibit the formation of these products and treat deep vein thrombosis. Hemophilia is characterized by an impairment in the ability to form, for 10 points, what gel-like coagulations of blood?
items.a: blood clots [accept venous blood clots or arterial blood clots; accept thrombus before "thrombosis,"prompt afterward; prompt on pulmonary embolism or embolus]

items.q: These structures are overproduced in patients with ATIII ("a-t-3") deficiency. In some cases, the improper migration of these structures can be prevented with an IVC filter. The breakdown of these structures can produce D-dimers. The drug alteplase, a synthetic form of TPA, is typically used to break down these structures, whose formation can be inhibited by apixaban. These structures may form via either the (*) "extrinsic" or "intrinsic" pathway, which use over 10 different numbered "factors". In the synthesis of these structures, the enzyme thrombin converts fibrinogen to fibrin, which is then cross-linked to form a solid mesh. Aggregation of platelets causes the formation of, for 10 points, what structures which form in response to blood vessel injury?
items.a: blood clots [accept thrombi]

items.q: Sacrifices of cows and oxen are prohibited during celebrations of this figure's birthday on lunar April 26th, which are often accompanied with incense and fireworks. One account of this figure's birth states that his mother, Andeng (ahn-dung), lay with a dragon, which is why he is sometimes shown with the head of a dragon but the face of a man. This figure made an accidental discovery when a bush caught on fire and the wind blew leaves and twigs into a tripod cauldron. This figured died from consuming a poisonous yellow weed and failing to take a tea antidote in time. This mythical figure is the traditional author of The Classic of Herbal Medicine, which was likely compiled in the 2nd century AD. This figure's common name means "god-peasant." He taught such skills as acupuncture and using fire to clear fields in his role as the second of the Three Sovereigns, along with Fuxi (foo-shee) and the Yellow Emperor. For 10 points, name this Chinese agriculture deity who was also known as the "God of Five Cereals."
items.a: Shennong [or Wugushen or Wuguxiandi; accept answers that refer to a God of Five Grains or God of Five Cereals before the "Five"]

items.q: In one story, this being was held to have followed a beam of light at the end of which were two sisters, whom this being invited to stand on two mountains, thereby creating the sun and moon. In another legend, this being molded an ox out of clay and saliva and set it to carry the earth; so that the ox would not fall asleep, this being also created a clay rooster to keep watch on the ox. First described in the book A Chronicle of the Five Circles of Time as having the body of a snake and the head of a dragon, more common depictions of this deity have him as a giant with a horn on his head, which was supposed to get soft when it was his time to die. This being is one of the few who can send rain without the permission of the Jade Emperor, and according to the Wuyun Linianji, at his death this god's body became the extremes of the earth while insects on it became people. Originally held to have hatched from a primordial egg, for 10 points, identify this creator deity of Chinese myth, often considered the first man.
items.a: Pangu or Pengu

items.q: This deity ended an event that may have been caused by the destruction of the Hollow Mulberry or by a king's uncontrolled sexual libido. The tribal chief in Mount Emei [UH-may]injured himself because he was ashamed to lose a battle to this deity, who was often depicted with a builder's compass. This deity invented music and was rewritten as an example of the "Way of the True Person" to impose modesty and humility on (*) women in the Daoist tradition. This deity smelted five colors of stone to make the sky blue and uses ashes from burning reeds to end one catastrophe. The sun, moon, and stars moved northwest and the rivers flowed east after this deity restored the four limits and killed a black tortoise. During a fight with Zhuanxu [jwen-shew], Gonggong headbutted Buzhou [boo-JOH] Mountain, causing a flood that this goddess ended by "mending the heavens." For 10 points, name this goddess who created aristocrats out of yellow clay, then made other humans by swinging a rope over her head in Chinese creation myths.
items.a: Nuwa [accept Nugua or Nukua]

items.q: This deity took a long rope, dipped it in mud, and flung the mud in all directions to speed up the completion of one task. As part of another task, this deity took several rocks of different colors from a river and reshaped them. This goddess is frequently depicted entwined with her consort, who is credited with inventing fishing and trapping. After a water god angrily smashed his head against a mountain, this goddess cut off the legs of a giant tortoise to use as a new pillar to hold up the (*) wall of heaven before using her serpentine body to block the resulting flood. When this this wife of the first of the Three Sovereigns was lonely, she created animals for six days before using yellow clay to craft humanity on the seventh. This daughter of the Jade Emperor is married to her brother, Fu Xi. For 10 points, name this Chinese creator goddess.
items.a: Nuwa [or Nu Gua; or Nyuwa; or similar Chinese variants]

items.q: According to A Treatise on Strange Beings and Things by Li Rong, this deity was ashamed of wedding her brother and so covered her face with a grass fan. In another story, this being was indirectly responsible for the flow of rivers and the movement of stars, and this being and her brother were said to reside on Mount Kunlun. Her husband, Fu xi, was the first of the three sovereigns and according to the Fengshen Yanyi, her subordinates included the Thousand Year Vixen, the Jade Pipa, and the Nine-headed Pheasant. She is commonly cited in explanations of the mandate of heaven, as she carefully shaped some people by hand, while others she created by flinging a rope encrusted with mud droplets. A disagreement with the water god Gong Gong lead to her most famous action, which she accomplished with the use of five rainbow stones. For 10 points, name this Chinese deity who created humans from clay and patched up the sky.
items.a: Nuwa [or Nu Gua]

items.q: This figure names a cypress forest mausoleum that supposedly contains only the hat and robes he left behind. A 3rd-century BCE school of thought whose name combines this figure and Laozi ("LAO-dzuh") developed Taoism from a philosophy into a religious system. The most influential text of traditional Chinese medicine is this figure's Inner Canon. This figure fathered the drought goddess Nuba, who helped him and the war goddess Jiutian Xuannu ("jee-oh-tee-EN shwen-new") kill the mist-summoning demon Chiyou ("CHIR-yo"). This figure won the first battle in Chinese myth at Banquan ("BAHN-chwen"), where he defeated a rival named for "Flame" who is sometimes conflated with this figure's predecessor Shennong. This member of the Three Sovereigns joins four similarly-named gods of the cardinal directions to form the Wufang Shangdi. For 10 points, what figure's name became a title for the founder of the Qin dynasty?
items.a: Yellow Emperor [or Huangdi or Huangshen or Xuanyuan; prompt on Huang-Lao] (The Mausoleum of the Yellow Emperor is in Shaanxi. The Han school of thought is called Huang-Lao.)

items.q: In a battle, this figure defeats a nefarious, four-eyed, six-armed, ox-headed, fog-breathing enemy. This figure used the drought demon Nuba and invented the south-pointing chariot in order to defeat the aforementioned Chi-you (chee-YOH). This husband of the inventor of sericulture is credited with many inventions of his own, including the calendar. He goaded the four-eyed Cangjie (TSONG-jyeh) into inventing his people's writing. This victor at the battle of Zhuolu (JWOH-loo) also subdued the Yan Emperor to become possibly the last of the Three Sovereigns. For 10 points, name this mythical founder of Chinese civilization, named for the same color as one of China's key rivers.
items.a: the Yellow Emperor [or Huangdi, or really any answer that combines yellow with a type of ruler; also accept the Yan Emperor or Shennong until "chariot" is read]

items.q: This ruler is honored by the "Sorrow of Ten Thousand Stele" and the "Celebrate Longevity Stele," which are a pair of tortoise steles found at his birthplace of Shou Qiu. This leader's son was named Shaohao, although he was sometimes said to be his nephew. This ruler helped defeat the Nine Li tribes, which were led by a bronze headed tyrant named Chiyou. This figure came to power after the defeat of the last Flame Emperor, known as the Yan Emperor, although that figure is sometimes believed to be Shennong. This figure, whose birth name was (*) Xuanyuan, is typically considered the last of the Three Sovereigns, or the first of the Five Emperors. This ruler's wife Leizu invented silk working, and his four-eyed minister Cangjie allegedly created Chinese writing. For 10 points, name this legendary Chinese leader whose name is a homonym for the title for the Emperor of China.
items.a: the Yellow Emperor (or Huangdi; accept Xuanyuan before "Xuanyuan")

items.q: In one story, this man fought his enemy to a draw nine times, then went to a mountain for three days to learn the art of war from the bird-bodied Dark Lady. One of his enemies was a bull-shaped monster with a bronze head and iron eyebrows who was the first to create metal weapons. This man made a drum from the skin of a one-legged lightning monster called Kui, and he used his companions Responding Dragon and Drought Fury to defeat the war god (*) Chiyou. When Nuwa isn't counted, he's generally the last of the Three Sovereigns after Fuxi and Shen Nong. this man invented writing and the pottery wheel, and was married to Leizu, who discovered the way to breed silkworms. For 10 points, name this culture hero considered the founder of Chinese civilization, a ruler of China named for a certain color.
items.a: the Yellow Emperor [or Huangdi]

items.q: Description acceptable. A subordinate of the ruler of this place wears a hat bearing a phrase translated as "Become Rich Upon Encountering Me," while another subordinate has a hat with a phrase translated as "Arresting You Right Now." Those two men who work in this place are former dedicated police constables known as the Black and White Guard. In a story about this place, Mulian (moo-lee-EN) journeys there to find his mother and upon returning, begins a festival on the fifteenth day of the seventh lunar month. The guardians of this place are known as Ox-Head and Horse-Face, and some joss paper is known as its "money." This location is said to have "eighteen levels," with the worst being "Avici." For 10 points, the Jade Emperor put Yama in charge of overseeing what location out of which people are eventually reincarnated?
items.a: diyu [or naraka; or Chinese hell; or Buddhist hell; or Taoist hell; accept the underworld in place of "hell" in those answers; prompt on hell alone; prompt on answers involving the afterlife]

items.q: It's not the Mountain God, but this deity ordered four dragons to be trapped in mountains after they intervened in a drought without his blessing. This deity was once said to be the crown prince of the kingdom of Pure Felicity and Majestic Heavenly Lights and Ornaments. This man notably only allowed his daughter to visit her husband across a bridge of magpies spanning the (*) Milky Way on the seventh day of the seventh month each year after she married a cowherd. This deity, who asked the Twelve Zodiacs to visit him in heaven, had to deal with a monkey stealingpeaches from his orchard after he instituted him as Protector of the Peaches. This man was the wife of Xiwangmu, and he was created as Pangu created the universe. For 10 points, name this supreme ruler of Heaven in Chinese mythology, often named after a type of green ornamental mineral.
items.a: Jade Emperor [accept Yu-Huang-Da-Di]

items.q: This god spent 3,200 kalpas becoming a saint, then another hundred million kalpas cultivating the virtue needed to acquire his current position. When a dragon brought rain to a village, this god banished the dragon, beginning a custom of burning dragon-shaped figurines of incense and joss paper in this god's honor to bring rain. This god, whose birthday is on the ninth day of the first lunar month, employs ten judges to govern the underworld. He recruited the Buddha's help to imprison a troublemaker under a (*) mountain for five hundred years and organized the race of twelve animals that determined the zodiac order. This god, who figures among the Three Pure Ones in Daoist tradition, makes the mistake of letting the peaches of immortality in his palace be guarded by the monkey Sun Wukong. For 10 points, name this ruler of heaven in Chinese myth who is named for a precious green stone.
items.a: the Jade Emperor [or Yu Huang or Yu Di; prompt on Heaven or Lao t'ien-ye; do not accept or prompt on "Yu the Great"]

items.q: This person passed 3200 trials each taking at least three million years to defeat a demon and they were born on the ninth day of the first lunar month. Son Wukong is given a position as keeper of horses after meeting this deity and later becomes immortal after stealing a peach from this man's orchard. One of this person's daughters weaves colourful clouds and this person creates the Milky Way to separate that daughter from her cowherd husband. This person organised a race between 12 animals, which was won by a rat. For ten points, name the highest deity of Taoism who is named after a green stone.
items.a: Jade Emperor

items.q: Among this deity's children are a goddess who provides good eyesight and a goddess who weaves colorful clouds. This figure passed a series of 3200 trials, each taking 3 million years, in order to defeat a demon. This divine figure created the Milky Way to separate his daughter from a cowherd, but allowed them to meet annually on a bridge of magpies. He owns an orchard whose peaches grant immortality. This figure was originally a subordinate to one of the Three Pure Ones, and he once gave Monkey the job of stable boy. For 10 points name this ruler of heaven from Chinese mythology, named for a type of green stone.
items.a: Jade Emperor [or Yu-huang; or Yu Di]

items.q: They're not Bodhisattvas, but each of these beings correspond to one of the Medicine Buddha's Heavenly Generals. The Buddha summons these beings on his deathbed to say goodbye to him in one myth. These beings' most common hourly activities are used as a mnemonic for the Earthly Branches of the day. One creature barely joined this group by making a noise upon waking up from a nap. A being that failed to join this group was pushed off of an (*) Ox into a river and drowned as part of the Jade Emperor's Great Race. A cat replaces a rabbit in the Vietnamese version of this construct which also features divisions represented by the pig and the rat. For 10 points, what astrological group of twelve animals represent years and personalities in East Asian tradition?
items.a: the Chinese Zodiac [or shengxiao; or saangchiu; or shuxiang; accept Eastern, East Asian, or any specific East or Southeast Asian nationality's Zodiac; prompt on animals or pigs or cats before mention]

items.q: One 2011 paper about practices in a diaspora community focused on this system is titled 'Does fortune favor' one class of people in this system. The 2009 sale of two Italian-designed sculptures from a larger set depicting figures in this system prompted discussions of what defined a 'national treasure' in one country. A 2016 paper has suggested no evidence exists for parents deliberately selecting for and against classifications in this system, leading to more or fewer births in certain (*) years. This system, despite its translation into English, is based on the 11.6 year orbit of Jupiter. One legend about the origins of this system claims that the Cat was excluded because it was pushed into a river just before reaching the Jade Emperor. Depicted in bronze sculptures looted from the Old Summer Palace, for 10 points, name this system, which assigns animals such as Horse, Tiger and Dragon in a 12 year cycle.
items.a: the Chinese Zodiac [accept shengxiao and shuxiang, prompt on zodiac with 'from which country?', calendar]

items.q: It's not a policy, but conventional wisdom suggests that this construct explains a 2015 birth rate slump due to a saying about one in ten people achieving happiness. In a story about this construct's origin, a character claims to be late because he used his breath to help villagers put out a fire. Some Buddhists use this construct to identify an individual's patron as one of eight deities, resulting in Guanyin being identified with the (*) cardinal north. Folk traditions group components of this construct into four "triangles" of romantic compatibility. In the origin story for this system, the Jade Emperor presides over an event in which a rat jumps off the back of an ox to win a race. For 10 points, identify this Chinese astrological system of twelve animals.
items.a: Chinese zodiac [or Asian zodiac or shengxiao or shuxiang; prompt on calendar or lunar calendar or astrology]

items.q: A character in this novel uses advice from three sealed envelopes to marry a woman who initially scared him with her collection of weapons. In this novel, a character asks a cursed horse if it will obstruct him, which spurs it into miraculously jumping over a stream. A dancing maid in this novel is used in a seduction plot by her adoptive father to drive (*) Lu Bu to kill Dong Zhuo. In this novel, a character uses empty strawboats to "borrow" 100,000 arrows from the enemy. This novel depicts Cao Cao's ("TSOW-tsow") defeat at the Battle of Red Cliffs. For 10 points, three men make an oath of brotherhood in a peach garden in what classical Chinese novel that fictionalizes the conflict between the kingdoms of Wu, Shu and Wei?
items.a: Romance of the Three Kingdoms [accept Sanguo Yanyi]

items.q: A horse in this novel is said to be able to travel 500 kilometers in a day, and is known as the Red Hare. One character in this novel sits atop an open city gate playing a lute, scaring off Sima Yi [sih-mah yee] as he orders a retreat. In this novel, (*) Zhou Yu ["joe"-"you"] is depicted to be extremely jealous towards Zhuge Liang [joo-guh lee-ah-ng]. Liu Bei [lee-oo bay] defeats Cao Cao [tsow tsow] in this novel at the Battle of Red Cliffs. For 10 points, name this novel set in its namesake period following the fall of the Han dynasty, and written by Luo Guanzhong [loo-oh goo-AHN-"joe"-ng].
items.a: Romance of the Three Kingdoms [or Sanguo yanyi; reject "Records of the Three Kingdoms" or "Sanguo zhi"]

items.q: A character in this novel repeatedly escapes from battles through tricks like cutting his beard with a sword or shouting "Look over there!" before running away. A character in this novel begins playing a string instrument above the gates of an empty city to trick his enemy into thinking it is an ambush. A trio of men become sworn brothers in this novel after declaring the Peach Garden Oath. A character in this earliest written of the (*) Four Great Classical Novels places straw dummies to "borrow" arrows from his enemy; that character, Zhuge Liang ("JOO-guh LYONG"), was recruited by Liu Bei ("lyoo bay") to battle against Cao Cao ("tsao tsao"). For 10 points, name this Chinese novel by Luo Guanzhong ("lwoah GWAN-jung") about the title states of Shu, Wei, and Wu.
items.a: Romance of the Three Kingdoms [or Three Kingdoms Performing Yi or Sanguo Yanyi]

items.q: While playing a board game, a man in this novel remains composed as his bone is scraped for poison. Earlier in this novel, that character hopes to "die on the same day, in the same month and in the same year" as men he met at an inn. A ritual in this novel is performed for three days and three nights to summon an eastern wind before a battle. A strategist in this novel "borrowed" arrows for a battle whose wind he used to carry fire ships into a fleet. That crushing defeat was suffered by Cao Cao ("tsao tsao"), the main antagonist of this member of the Four Great Classical Novels. For 10 points, name this historical Chinese novel titled for the conflict between Wei, Shu, and Wu.
items.a: Romance of the Three Kingdoms [or Sanguo Yanyi]

items.q: Rather than being executed for murdering his wife, a character in this novel is tattooed on his face. One character in this novel releases fish from a cage after a fisherman doesn't sell him any, and that character gains a nickname due to his twin axes. This novel begins with the release of golden rays after a stone tortoise is moved. A character in this novel drinks (*) 18 bowls of wine and then beats a tiger dead. That character, Wu Song, inspired an erotic spinoff of this novel titled The Plum in the Golden Vase. Song Jiang leads a group of reincarnated demons against the corrupt official Gao Qiu in, for 10 points, what classic Chinese novel by Shi Nai'an about a group of 108 outlaws?
items.a: Water Margin [or Outlaws of the Marsh or All Men Are Brothers or Shui Hu Zhuan]

items.q: In this novel, a letter demanding to free a prisoner is revealed as a forgery when a craftsman uses the wrong seal. An account of the title Old Incidents inspired a scene in this novel in which characters disguised as date traders rob a convoy filled with birthday gifts. In this novel, a man disregards a warning not to drink more than "three bowls of liquor" and enters a (*) forest where he kills a tiger. Zaju operas elevated this novel's character "Black Whirlwind," or Li Kui, one of the "Heavenly Spirits" who train at Mount Liang to rebel against Gao Qiu. For 10 points, name this Yuan dynasty-era Chinese novel about a noble group of 108 bandits.
items.a: Water Margin [or Outlaws of the Marsh; or All Men are Brothers; or Shuihu Zhuan; or 水滸傳] (Water Margin took episodes from Old Incidents in the Xuanhe Period of the Great Song Dynasty.)

items.q: 1. In this novel, seven men dressed as traders spike the wine of escorts to steal birthday presents. A stone tortoise is moved in the first chapter of this novel. A flatbread-selling dwarf's wife is killed by a man who beats a tiger in this novel. The protagonists of this novel are divided into (*) Earthly Demons and Heavenly Spirits. The "Stars of Destiny" are led by Song Jiang ("sung j'yong") in this novel against the corrupt Gao Qiu ("gow chʼyoh"). For 10 points, name this classic novel by Shi Nai'an ("shurr nye-AHN") about a group of bandits.
items.a: Water Margin [or Shui Hu Zhuan or Outlaws of the Marsh or All Men Are Brothers]

items.q: One character in this novel is tattooed on the face and exiled after walking into a hall holding a rare sword. This novel opens with a series of golden rays being released after a stone tortoise is moved. One character in this novel drinks 18 bowls of wine before beating a tiger to death. The "original seven" in this novel rob a convoy of birthday gifts before retreating to Mount Liang. In this novel, the corrupt Gao Qiu ("gow chʼyoh") is opposed by the "Heavenly Spirits" and "Earthly Demons" who make up a group led by Song Jiang known as the "Stars of Destiny."For 10 points, name this classical Chinese novel by Shi Nai'an ("shurr nye-AHN") about a group of 108 bandits.
items.a: Water Margin [or Outlaws of the Marsh or All Men Are Brothers or Shui Hu Zhuan]

items.q: A character in this novel was exiled because he accidentally smashed the queen mother's crystal goblet during the peach banquet. That character, Sha Wujing [shah woo-JING], was defeated while trying to block a river crossing. A character in this novel wields a (*) staff that shrinks and grows, and would call himself the "Great Sage Equal to Heaven," angering the Jade Emperor. For 10 points, name this Chinese novel that follows the trip of Tang Sanzang [tahng san-ZAHNG] and the monkey king, Sun Wukong [soon woo-KONG], to India.
items.a: Journey to the West [accept Xiyou Ji [shee-YO jee]; prompt on Monkey]

items.q: In this work, a character is tricked into wearing a headband that can be tightened at will by another character. A character in this work is beaten 800 times for dropping a Queen's crystal goblet. One character in this work loses a bet after being unable to somersault out of a hand. A character in this work gets banished from heaven for (*) flirting with the Moon Goddess. In this novel, a character who was born from a stone egg gets trapped under a mountain for 500 years, and later joins Pigsy and Sandy in the title quest. For ten points, name this Chinese epic in which Sun Wukong and Xuanzong travel to receive Buddhist structures from India.
items.a: Journey to the West [accept Xiyou Ji, accept Monkey]

items.q: A character in this novel uses golden strings to feel the pulse of a ruler and prescribes a medicine of "black gold" for his anxiety. A character in this novel kidnaps the daughter of a village elder and exposes his identity through his insatiable appetite; that character carries a rake and is tasked with cleaning altars in this novel. A weapon from this novel was originally an iron (*) pillar owned by the Dragon King that could change size. After eating the peaches of immortality, a character in this novel is tricked by the Buddha's palm and becomes trapped under a mountain. For 10 points, name this novel that follows the title pilgrimage of the monk Tang Sanzang and Monkey King Sun Wukong.
items.a: Journey to the West [accept Xiyouji; prompt on Monkey with "what is the title of the non-abridged version of that work"]

items.q: Two characters in this novel drink from a river that causes all who drink from it to become pregnant before entering a kingdom with no men. One character in this novel loses their position as Marshal and is promoted to an altar cleaner at its end. Another character in this novel wields the (*) staff Jingu Bang and is trapped under a mountain after urinating on a pillar. For ten points, name this novel in which Sandy, Pigsy, and Sun Wukong accompany Xuanzang on the title pilgrimage.
items.a: Journey to the West (accept Xi You Ji)

items.q: An early commentator on this work had a pseudonym meaning "Inkstone Studio." John Minford helped complete the seminal English translation of this work by David Hawkes. A significant dispute in this work's namesake "-ology" centers on whether its last forty chapters were a later addition to its first eighty chapters. Feminist criticism of this work often contrasts the female-dominated space of the Grand View Garden with the patriarchal outside world and discusses the 12 Beauties of Jinling. In this novel, the Disenchantment Fairy is visited by a priest and a monk carrying the protagonist, who is reincarnated as a boy with a piece of jade in his mouth. For 10 points, the tragic love story of Jia Baoyu and Lin Daiyu is detailed in what classic Chinese novel?
items.a: Dream of the Red Chamber [or The Story of the Stone; or A Dream of Red Mansions; or Hong lou meng; prompt on Redology]

items.q: 裁判指示：如果你可以发音拼音，请看读 那个 NOTE TO MODERATOR: If you can't read the above or read pinyin, just do your best. We appreciate you! After a misunderstanding, one character in this novel wraps petals in silk and buries them. In this novel, after the protagonist's sister is made a royal consort, their family constructs the Grand View Garden. In the frame story of this novel, one character's tears water a lotus flower that is reincarnated as the protagonist's (*) love interest, one of the Twelve Beauties of Jinling. The protagonist of this novel is born with jade in their mouth, and their true love is the sickly Lin Daiyu, although they were predetermined to marry Xue (shway) Baochai by their aristocratic family. For 10 points, name this novel about Jia Baoyu by Cao Xueqin, one of the Four Great Classical Novels of China.
items.a: Dream of the Red Chamber [or Story of the Stone, or Hong lou meng, or Shi tou Ji or A Dream of Red Mansions]

items.q: An anonymous commentator on this novel often used the word "maimed," leading to their nickname "Elderly Maimed Tablet." Practitioners of a field called this novel's "-ology," which include translator David Hawkes, dispute the provenance of its last 40 chapters. In this novel, an elegy to some flower petals is written by the protagonist's sickly cousin, who is also his main love interest. Late in this novel, the (*) Prospect Garden is seized after the central family becomes disfavored by the Emperor. This novel's protagonist, who falls in love with Lin Daiyu, is born with a talking piece of jade in his mouth. For 10 points, Cao Xueqin ("tsao shweh-chin") wrote what classic Chinese novel about the downfall of the Jia ("j'yah") family, often titled for a room?
items.a: Dream of the Red Chamber [or Story of the Stone; or A Dream of Red Mansions; or Hong Lou Meng; or Shitou ji; prompt on redology]

items.q: This book includes a poem in which the "frenzy of poetry" creeps over idle people "Day and night," which appears shortly before several poems about savoring crab meat. The speaker of a poem in this book is "wounded at heart" as she feels both resentment and regret over Spring, because "suddenly it comes and suddenly goes." A couplet about the "Great Void" in this book states "When false is taken for true, true becomes false; / If non-being turns into being, being becomes non-being." In this book, a (*) poetry contest leads a group of friends to write twelve poems about chrysanthemums. The speaker of a poem in this book asks "who will bury me when dead I lie" after relating how men laugh at her for burying some flowers. In this book, a Taoist priest reads verses about "a former and after life" on a stone. For 10 points, a stone is reborn into Jia Baoyu in what classic Chinese novel by Cao Xueqin ("tsao sh'way cheen")?
items.a: Dream of the Red Chamber [or The Story of the Stone; or Hong Lou Meng; or Shitou Ji]

items.q: An apocryphal legend holds that one of these works was carefully edited from three thousand to 305 entries to choose the most representative work. That work has "four beginnings" prefacing its sections of airs, hymns, greater odes, and lesser odes. Another of these works had two of its chapters excerpted and published separately as Doctrine of the Mean and Great Learning. One of these works traces events in the (*) State of Lu for a period of about 250 years. The most famous of them is attributed to Wenwang and includes sixty-four hexagrams, which are formed from a series of trigrams seen on a tortoise's back. They are often paired with the Four Books. For 10 points, name this series which includes the Spring and Autumn Annals and the I Ching, a core group of Confucian texts.
items.a: Five Classics

items.q: A rare benign tumor that usually grows under these structures develops from a thermoregulatory structure called the glomus body. These structures can be deformed to a concave, spoonlike shape in patients with iron-deficiency anemia. A classic vascular manifestation of endocarditis is the appearance of splinter hemorrhages in these structures. The eponychium ("ep-uh-NICK-ee-um") is a layer of stratum corneum at the base of these structures, which consist of a soft "bed" that lies under a hard "plate." The lunula is a white, crescent-shaped visible extension of the germinal matrix from which these structures grow continuously. Onychomycosis ("ON-uh-ko-my-CO-sis") and onychocryptosis ("ON-uh-ko-crip-TOE-sis") are conditions in which these structures become discolored by fungal infection or become ingrown, respectively. For 10 points, name these structures made of keratin that protect the tips of the digits.
items.a: nails [accept fingernails and toenails; prompt on fingers or toes]

items.q: One of these objects was used to mark the New Year at the temple of the Etruscan goddess Nortia. Slitting mills produced the precursors of these objects. Vienna is home to a tree called the Stock im Eisen to which many of these objects have been attached for good luck, and which inspired the practice of attaching these objects to statues of knights, which was used to raise funds for World War I in Germany and Austria-Hungary. The size of these objects is measured in (*) pennies, abbreviated d from the Latin word denarius. A brad is a small, thin variety of this object. In order to deliver Israel from the troops of Jabin, Heber's wife Jael killed Sisera using one of these objects. Four of the Five Holy Wounds were inflicted with these objects during Christ's crucifixion. For 10 points, name these fasteners driven with hammers.
items.a: nails [accept tent pegs]

items.q: A Maori story tells how Maui took 19 of these objects from Mahuika, which were really her disguised children, in order to give fire to humans, but when he tried to take the 20th, Mahuika threw it on the ground and nearly burned the entire world. In some accounts, either Shiva or Rudra used one of these objects to cut off the fifth head of Brahma. In a Sumerian myth, Enki created two neuter deities to cure Ereshkigal using mud found beneath these objects. In Japanese legends, the kitsune-tsuki demons can enter a person's body through the breast or these objects; in another Japanese myth, along with his beard and hair, these objects were removed from Susano'o when he was exiled from heaven. At Ragnarok, Loki will steer a ship filled with the enemies of the gods made of these objects. For 10 points, name these objects, which make up the ship Naglfar in Norse myth.
items.a: Nails [or Ungues; accept "Fingernails" or "Toenails"]

items.q: The number of these interactions for orally active drugs is limited by Lipinski's Rule of 5. This interaction occurs between every fourth residue of an alpha helix. The higher melting point of guanine-cytosine pairs are attributed to their ability to form three of these interactions, while only two of them occur between (*) thymine and adenine. These interactions are responsible for the lattice structure of ice as well as the high boiling point, high surface tension, and low viscosity of water. For 10 points, name these weak intermolecular bonds between electronegative atoms and the namesake lightest element.
items.a: hydrogen bonds [or hydrogen bonding; prompt on intermolecular bond s or intermolecular force s or IMF s or van der Waals forces or dipole-dipole interactions]

items.q: Liquids are "associated" when they have these structures. Water and ethanol form an azeotrope due to these structures. Carboxylic acids are dimerized by these interactions, which are responsible for the (*) secondary structure of proteins. 3 of these interactions are present between guanine and cysteine in DNA due to their polar nitrogens and oxygens. Water's high specific heat is explained by, for ten points, what intermolecular interactions named after the lightest element?
items.a: hydrogen bonds (accept word forms such as hydrogen bonding, do not accept or prompt on "bonds" alone or specific bonds such as "covalent bond" or "ionic bond")

items.q: In PyMol, these phenomena and polar contacts are typically shown with yellow dashed lines. A mixture of methanol and acetone shows positive deviations from Raoult's law because acetone disrupts some of these phenomena. These phenomena cause carboxylic acids to form dimers. Three of them occur between (*) guanine and cytosine, while two occur between adenine and thymine. These phenomena occur between a donor and an electronegative acceptor like oxygen or nitrogen, and are the reason that ice is less dense than water. For 10 points, what intermolecular forces are named for the lightest element?
items.a: hydrogen bonds [or H-bonds; accept bonding in place of "bond"]

items.q: In the catalytic triads of serine proteases, this low-barrier interaction between histidine and aspartate facilitates the formation of a tetrahedral adduct. In the gas phase, carboxylic acids dimerize due to the presence of this interaction. This interaction is responsible for ammonia's high boiling point compared to phosphine. This type of interaction between positions i and i+4 is responsible for the structure of (*) alpha helices. These interactions occur in compounds containing highly electronegative atoms bonded to their namesake element, such as in hydrofluoric acid. For 10 points, name these intermolecular interactions responsible for water's lattice structure and unique properties.
items.a: hydrogen bonds [or H-bonds]

items.q: In some species, this process is controlled by the virB ("veer-B") genes. This process can be temporally visualized via time-of-entry mapping. Factors involved in this process, some of which are inhibited by finO and finP, are encoded by genes on the tra ("trah") operon. TraI ("trah-I") initiates this process by creating a nick onto the oriT ("OR-ee-T") site; that action eventually leads to the formation of a relaxosome. The type IV ("4") secretion system mediates the movement of the T-strand during this process. Integration of (*) fertility factors during this process often leads to the creation of Hfr ("H-F-R") strains. During this process, a donor cell bridges itself to a recipient cell using a sex pilus, which the donor also uses to transfer an F plasmid. For 10 points, name this cell-contact-dependent form of bacterial DNA transfer often described as "bacterial sex."
items.a: bacterial conjugation [prompt on type IV secretion system or T4SS with "what specific process is being conducted by the type IV secretion system?" until "type IV" is read; prompt on horizontal gene transfer or lateral gene transfer or HGT or LGT; prompt on bacterial sex until "bacterial sex" is read; reject "transformation"; reject "transduction"]

items.q: In the presence of amino acid derivatives called "opines," an autoinducer activates the genes required for this process in a model organism. In a 1956 experiment, Jacob and Wollman mapped this process by periodically "interrupting" it using a blender. It's not splicing, but this process begins with a transesterification reaction catalyzed at the oriT ("oh-ree-T") site by a Mob relaxase encoded on the Tra operon. Apart from translocation of effector proteins, this is the major ]=function of type IV ("four") secretion systems. R factors encoding antibiotic resistance are spread through this process. In Hfr strains, the genetic material involved in this process is integrated into the chromosome. During this process, two cells become positive for the F plasmid after a sex pilus ("PY-lus") bridges them together. For 10 points, name this form of horizontal gene transfer that requires direct cell-to-cell contact, unlike transduction or transformation.
items.a: bacterial conjugation [prompt on horizontal gene transfer until read]

items.q: This process is coupled to MAGE (mage) in the name of a technique used in 2011 to engineer a whole synthetic genome lacking a stop codon. The tra(TRAH) protein family forms a relaxosome to nick DNA during this process. Type IV (four) secretion systems are homologous to the proteins used in it. Joshua Lederberg discovered this process's mechanism, which requires either an F-positive cell or an Hfr (H-F-R) strain that has the fertility factor chromosomally integrated. This process (*) spreads R factors, which encode antibiotic resistance. During this process, a pilus forms between two bacteria, enabling horizontal gene transfer that's distinct from transduction and transformation. For 10 points, name this process often analogized to "bacterial sex".
items.a: bacterial conjugation [or word forms; prompt on horizontal gene transfer or HGT]

items.q: Erik Jarvik reclassified these organisms as members of the less-complex holocephalians after examining the premaxillary bones of their skull roofs. The male members of the Lepidosiren genus of these animals develop vascularized filaments in their pelvic appendages so that they provide oxygen to their eggs. The Protopterus, but not the Neoceratodus, type of these sarcopterygians engages in estivation by creating a cocoon of mucus and burying itself in mud. The "marbled" African type of these animals has the largest known animal genome, while the South American type of these so-called "living fossils" possess two of the namesake structures, which it uses in place of gills during certain times of the year. For 10 points, name these most primitive living fish, which are able to sustain themselves by consuming oxygen from air.
items.a: lungfish [or salamanderfish; or dipnoi; or barramunda] 4

items.q: Cancer cells in these structures are detected by sentinel biopsies. Trypanosomes enlarge the jugulodigastric type of these structures in Winterbottom's sign. As centroblasts pass into these structures' dark zones, cytidine deaminase rapidly mutates their cell-surface receptors. In TNM staging, cancer cells invade these structures, then metastasize. Fluid enters these structures through an afferent vessel and drains out of a subcapsular sinus. (*) Germinal centers in these structures and the spleen are the site of B cell maturation. The plague causes these organs to form buboes ("byoo-bose") at the groin or under the armpits. For 10 points, the tonsils are an example of what bean-shaped structures that swell during infection?
items.a: lymph nodes [accept germinal centers or GCs; prompt on nodes; prompt on lymphatic tissue or lymphoid tissue or lymphoid organs; reject "lymph" by itself]

items.q: Efferent vessels attach to these structures at the hilum. The subcapsular and trabecular sinuses are located in these structures, which may act as germinal centers, where isotype switching occurs. Peyer's patches are analogous to these structures in the small intestines. These structures are the "N" in TNM, an important acronym involved in cancer staging. These structures are infected in Hodgkin's disease, and their swelling is a telltale symptom of AIDS. Humans have more than five hundred of these structures in the body, each storing macrophages and lymphocytes. Tonsils are large examples of, for 10 points, what "nodes" storing white blood cells?
items.a: lymph nodes [prompt on "nodes"; prompt on "lymphoid tissue"]

items.q: Troisier's sign is an example of a hardened one of these structures, one of which is named for Virchow. CCL21 is a cytokine most commonly expressed in them, and ones located between the pectoralis major and pectoralis minor muscles are named for Rotter. B lymphocytes are localized in follicles that make up its outer cortex, while T cells are distributed in the paracortical area. The adaptive immune response begins here, where antigen-presenting cells and antigens are delivered. For 10 points, name these organs that often enlarge when fighting infections.
items.a: lymph nodes

items.q: For the most part, each one has a hilus into which blood vessels can enter or exit. A framework of trabeculae emanate from the capsule and the germinal centers, where macrophages and inactivated B and T cells reside. For 10 points, name this structure that serves to filter foreign antigens and release namesake infection-fighting cells into the blood, located prominently in the groin, neck, and armpits.
items.a: lymph nodes

items.q: This structure's epithelium contains wing cells. Mooren's ulcer disrupts this structure. Viral infections of this structure can cause pseudo-dendrites or dendrites, and a "ring infiltrate" appears when this structure is infected by Acanthamoeba (a-CAN-thuh-MEE-buh). Bowman's membrane protects this structure. This structure suffers from amyloid buildup in lattice dystrophy, while it gradually degenerates in Fuchs' (FEWKS) dystrophy. A fluorescein (floor-ESS-in) stain is used to diagnose CMV or HSV infection of this structure, which is called keratitis. This body part's namesake limbus is where it meets the sclera. This structure is avascular, so it gets its nutrients from the aqueous humor. An excimer laser is used to reshape this structure in LASIK surgery, and it has more refractive power than the lens. For 10 points, name this clear outer portion of the eyeball.
items.a: cornea [prompt on eye]

items.q: Mutations in the TGFBI gene can lead to the appearance of honeycomb or dot patterns, or map and fingerprint like lines in this structure's epithelium. Harminder Dua was criticized for claiming that "textbooks will literally need to be re-written" to accommodate his 2013 discovery of a new layer in this structure. Proceeding in a posterior direction, this structure's five established layers are the anterior epithelium, Bowman's layer, the stroma, Descemet's membrane, and the endothelium. Infection with Chlamydia trachomatis may result in the abrasion of this structure due to contact with hairs. Chemical burns or oxygen deprivation can cause a deleterious neovascularization of this structure, which normally lacks blood vessels except at the edges. The irregular curvature of this structure in astigmatism can be corrected with LASIK surgery. For 10 points, name this transparent front covering of the eye.
items.a: cornea

items.q: This structure contains a layer composed of collagen known as Bowman's layer that lies between the epithelium and the stroma; below the stroma is Descement's membrane. The prefix "kerat" describes this structure, such as a disease affecting it called keratitis. This structure lies in front of a chamber containing aqueous humor and is surrounded by the conjunctiva, which is responsible for protecting the sclera. This structure, responsible for refracting the majority of the light that enters the eye, malfunctions in sufferers of astigmatism and is in front of the pupil and the iris. For 10 points, name this outermost layer of the eye.
items.a: cornea

items.q: Gutatta appear when hexagonal cells in this structure's endothelium self-destruct in the genetic disease Fuchs' Dystrophy. No one is sure what it's Bowman's membrane does other than separate its largest layer from its epithelium, while that layer is separated from its endothelium by Descemet's membrane. Recklinghausen discovered the motile corpuscles in this structure's stroma, which consists mostly of collagen. This structure is completely avascular because it must be completely transparent to work properly, and its radius of curvature is changed in LASIK surgery. For 10 points, name this outermost layer of the eye.
items.a: cornea

items.q: The coefficient of confidence measures the likelihood of interference in this process. Spo11 (S-P-O- "eleven") intentionally induces damage to begin this process, whose repair leads to mostly NCO sites, as well as CO sites through a double Holliday junction. Unequal instances of this process may, like gene conversion, result in gene duplication. This process is ectopic if it occurs between non-homologous sites. This process can occur in the pseudoautosomal region in men. This process finishes during the (*) pachytene ("PACKET"-een) stage at a chiasma (ky-AS-muh). The synaptonemal complex forms to enable this process during prophase I. For 10 points, what process during meiosis helps provide genetic diversity to germ cells by exchanging the genes of homologous chromosomes?
items.a: genetic recombination [or crossing over or crossover recombination; prompt on synapsis]
